title: ComponentOverview consumes the paginated versions endpoint
description:
Depends on the backend pagination story.

pages/ComponentOverview/index.tsx already has correct loading / error / empty states — they simply never fire because the request takes 16-30s or 500s.

Change: pass limit/offset through the query hook and render <Pagination> from ~/components/Pagination (offset style, matching the backend and ADR-043). Keep the existing QueryBoundary states.

Verify: /components -> click the top row (golang.org/x/crypto) -> page renders under 2s with working page controls. Confirm stdlib also loads.
notes:
Files: web/src/api/queries/components.ts, web/src/pages/ComponentOverview/index.tsx, web/src/pages/ComponentOverview/index.test.tsx
Approach: ComponentVersionParams gained limit/offset (in queryKey), defaulting to DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE/0, plus keepPreviousData so paging dims rather than blanks. Page holds an offset signal, resets it via on(...defer) when name/group/version change, and renders <Pagination> only when total > DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE. Header counts were the real trap: 'N versions across N SBOMs' counted rows on screen, which pagination redefines as 'on this page' while still reading as the corpus — now qualified against pagination.total when paged. 4 new tests, mutation-verified (removing limit/offset + forcing isPaged false fails 3 of 4). Live timing check on prod deferred with .7.

title: Paginate GET /api/v1/components/versions
description:
The endpoint is unpaginated and returns the full version history for a component name. Measured against prod:
  golang.org/x/crypto  -> 500 @ 30.4s
  stdlib               -> 500 @ 30.5s
  zlib                 -> 200 @ 24.6s / 2.54 MB
  github.com/pkg/errors-> 200 @ 21.6s / 2.49 MB
  ca-certificates      -> 200 @ 16.1s / 2.77 MB
Peers for scale: /artifacts?limit=20 2.27s, /vulns?limit=20 3.25s, /licenses?limit=20 0.54s.

The top rows of /components are the most-used components, so they are exactly the ones that time out — the list page's primary links are dead.

Change: add limit/offset to db/queries/*.sql, the service method, and the huma handler in internal/api/. Per ADR-043 the ordering here is stable and the UI wants numbered pages with a total, so OFFSET is the derived style — do not use a keyset cursor. Default limit = DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE (20). Return a total count alongside the page.

Run: make generate (sqlc), then make openapi (regenerates web/openapi.json and web/src/types/openapi.d.ts — tsc enforces these, so a stale type breaks the Docker build).

Verify: curl -w '%{http_code} %{time_total} %{size_download}' on ?name=golang.org/x/crypto -> 200, under 2s, under 100 KB.
notes:
Files: db/queries/search.sql, internal/repository/search.sql.go (sqlc), internal/service/search.go, internal/service/search_component.go, internal/api/types_search.go, internal/api/search.go, web/openapi.json, web/src/types/openapi.d.ts, pkg/client/types.go, plus tests in internal/service/search_test.go and internal/api/search_test.go
Approach: GetComponentVersions' 'LIMIT 5000' safety cap replaced with LIMIT @row_limit OFFSET @row_offset. Offset per ADR-043 (stable ordering, UI wants numbered pages + a total). New ComponentVersionFilter carries name/group/version/type/limit/offset/visibility; the service now returns PagedResult[ComponentVersionEntry]; the handler embeds PaginationParams (default 20, max 200) and emits paginationMeta.
The total is a SEPARATE CountComponentVersions query, deliberately not this file's usual COUNT(*) OVER(). The page query carries three LEFT JOINs (artifact + two enrichments) and a four-key sort purely to shape its rows; a window count would drag every matching row through all of that just to discard it, which is the cost that made the endpoint time out. The count needs only the sbom visibility join and stays on idx_component_name_group. Rationale is written into the .sql comment.
Regenerated: make generate (sqlc), make openapi, make generate-client -- pkg/client/types.go is guarded by generate-client-check in make check.
Tests: service level -- window reaches the query, total comes from the count not len(rows), a failed count does not fall through to a page query. API level -- limit/offset reach the filter, pagination comes back in the body, default is 20/0, and limit=5000 is rejected 422.
Not verified against prod: this branch is not deployed, and the story's curl check needs the new code running. The 30s timeout is a scan-volume problem the window directly bounds, but the real timing should be re-measured after the epic merges.
Gates: make check green end-to-end (lint 0 issues, all Go tests, openapi-check, generate-client-check, frontend lint/typecheck/test, helm-check).

title: Vulnerability severity filter has no visible active state
description:
pages/Vulnerabilities.tsx:132 emits class 'tab-btn' / 'tab-btn tab-active'. NEITHER class exists in index.css — the real contract is '.tab-bar button.active' (index.css:525). The active severity filter is therefore indistinguishable from the rest.

Measured live on https://ocidex.app/vulnerabilities — all six tabs (All, CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, UNKNOWN) return identical computed style: border-bottom rgba(0,0,0,0) 2px, color rgb(139,144,165), font-weight 500.

Contrast: pages/Licenses.tsx:84 uses the same tab-btn class but with ' active', which DOES match .tab-bar button.active, so its category filter highlights correctly.

Fix: replace the hand-rolled markup in Vulnerabilities.tsx with <TabBar> from ~/components/ui (it already emits the correct .tab-bar + .active contract and exists precisely to stop this copy-paste drift — see its doc comment). Then grep the whole tree for 'tab-active' and 'tab-btn' and convert every remaining site.

Verify: getComputedStyle on .tab-bar button -> the active tab's border-bottom-color differs from its siblings.
notes:
Files: web/src/pages/Vulnerabilities.tsx, web/src/pages/ClusterDetail/VulnerabilitiesTab.tsx, web/src/pages/Licenses.tsx, web/src/components/ui/TabBar.tsx, web/src/components/ui/tabBarContract.test.ts (new), web/src/pages/Vulnerabilities.test.tsx, web/src/pages/ClusterDetail/index.test.tsx
Approach: Grepped the tree -- three hand-rolled strips, not one. Vulnerabilities.tsx and ClusterDetail/VulnerabilitiesTab.tsx both emitted 'tab-btn'/'tab-active' (neither class exists in index.css); Licenses.tsx used ' active' so it worked, but carried the same stray tab-btn. All three now render <TabBar>, the single writer of the '.tab-bar button.active' contract. TabBar gained an optional `class` prop for Licenses' mb-4. Vulnerabilities keeps '' as the no-filter query value, so activeSeverityTab() maps that to the 'All' tab id.
Guards: new tabBarContract.test.ts asserts index.css still defines .tab-bar button.active AND that no .ts/.tsx under src emits the two dead class names (comments stripped first, since the converted sites name them in prose). Two cases in Vulnerabilities.test.tsx assert against the rendered DOM -- exactly one .tab-bar button.active, it is 'All' initially, and clicking HIGH moves it and sets params().severity. ClusterDetail/index.test.tsx's '.tab-bar .tab-btn' selector updated to '.tab-bar button'.
Gates: frontend-lint 0 errors (5 pre-existing warnings), typecheck clean, 335/335 tests.

title: Admin tab strip and rendered panel desync
description:
At /admin/jobs the strip highlights Jobs but the body renders the Sources panel. Reproduces after a hard reload, so it is not a client-nav artifact.

Root cause, web/src/pages/Admin.tsx:
- line 56: tabs() = user()?.role === 'admin' ? TABS : TABS.filter(t => !t.adminOnly). Sources is the ONLY tab with adminOnly:false (line 44).
- On first paint user() is still loading, so tabs() === [Sources].
- line 60: active() = tabs().find(t => t.paths.includes(location.pathname)) ?? tabs()[0] -> Sources.
- line 97: <Show when={active()}>{(tab) => tab().render()}</Show>. Show is NON-KEYED, so once when is truthy the children function never re-runs. When user() resolves to admin the panel stays frozen on Sources forever, while the strip's inline style bindings (lines 83-89) update correctly.

Fix: hold rendering until !user.loading, and make the panel swap reactive — either <Show when={active()} keyed> or render via <Dynamic component={...}>.

Add pages/Admin.test.tsx: mount at /admin/jobs with an auth context whose user resolves on a later tick; assert the Jobs panel renders and Sources does not.

Verify: cold-load /admin/jobs, /admin/keys, /admin/status — each renders its own panel.
notes:
Files: web/src/pages/Admin.tsx, web/src/pages/Admin.test.tsx (new)
Approach: Both causes fixed, since either alone still misrenders. (1) Wrapped the whole page in <Show when={!user.loading} fallback={<SkeletonHeader />}> so tabs()/active()/the page title are never computed from a half-known session. (2) Added `keyed` to the panel <Show> so the children function re-runs when active() changes identity -- this is what unfroze the panel.
New Admin.test.tsx (9 cases): the regression case renders at /admin/jobs with a resource-shaped auth double whose `loading` is a reactive getter (a plain boolean property never re-runs the tracking scope), asserts nothing commits while loading and that panel:jobs -- not panel:sources -- renders once the admin session resolves. Plus an it.each cold-loading all six routes into their own panel, the legacy /admin/registries -> Sources path, and a non-admin falling back to Sources on an admin-only path. Mutation-checked: reverting either fix fails the regression case.
Gates: frontend-lint 0 errors (5 pre-existing warnings), typecheck clean, 331/331 tests.

title: /vulnerabilities/:id renders for signed-out visitors
description:
pages/VulnerabilityDetail.tsx imports RunningWorkloadsList from ~/pages/ClusterDetail/RunningWorkloads. That component calls /api/v1/vulns/{id}/workloads, which 401s anonymously and bounces the whole public CVE page to /login.

Verified: GET /api/v1/vulns/CVE-2026-46595 returns 200, but https://ocidex.app/vulnerabilities/CVE-2026-46595 redirects.

Change: wrap the RunningWorkloadsList section in <Show when={user()}> so the public page keeps its CVE content and only the cluster-exposure block is withheld.

Verify: firefox MCP, private window, /vulnerabilities/CVE-2026-46595 -> CVE detail renders, location.pathname unchanged. Extend pages/VulnerabilityDetail.test.tsx.
notes:
Files: web/src/pages/VulnerabilityDetail.tsx, web/src/pages/VulnerabilityDetail.test.tsx
Approach: Confirmed anonymously with curl -- /api/v1/vulns/CVE-2026-46595 -> 200, /api/v1/vulns/CVE-2026-46595/workloads -> 401. Added useAuth + a signedIn() accessor and wrapped the 'Running in your clusters' card in <Show when={signedIn()}>, also passing signedIn() as RunningWorkloadsList's `when` so the query is gated, not just the markup (it already gates on `when` because it is mounted per-row elsewhere). Test file gained a ~/context/auth mock with a settable user and a case asserting that signed out the advisory content still renders, the section does not, and useVulnWorkloads is never called.
Gates: frontend-lint 0 errors, typecheck clean, 322/322 tests.

title: / renders for signed-out visitors
description:
Depends on the unwrap() and me.ts fixes. Reproduce in a private window: https://ocidex.app/ currently redirects to /login.

Sweep pages/Home.tsx and pages/HomeDiscovery.tsx for any remaining query that 401s anonymously; wrap auth-scoped sections in <Show when={user()}>.

Add a case to pages/Home.test.tsx: render with no user in the auth context, assert the page content renders and no navigation to /login occurs.

Verify: firefox MCP, private window, navigate to /, evaluate_script -> location.pathname === '/'.
notes:
Files: web/src/components/Layout.test.tsx, web/src/pages/Home.test.tsx
Approach: No production change was needed. Verified anonymously with curl that /api/v1/stats -> 200, /api/v1/discover -> 200, /api/v1/users/me -> 401 (the only 401), and context/auth.tsx's fetchMe already handles that 401 correctly (raw fetch, returns undefined -- it never went through unwrap). So the / redirect was caused entirely by .1 (unwrap's hard navigate on any 401) and .2 (HomeBand's three ungated /users/me/* queries), both already closed.
Added the regression guards instead: Layout.test.tsx gets an it.each over /, /vulnerabilities/:id, /artifacts, /components asserting an unauthenticated visitor triggers no navigate -- authedPaths is a prefix match, so this is what stops a future '/' entry. Mutation-checked: adding '/' to authedPaths fails all four. Home.test.tsx gets the case the AC named: renders the catalog with no user in the auth context and window.location.pathname unchanged.
Gates: frontend-lint 0 errors (5 pre-existing warnings), typecheck clean, 321/321 tests.

title: Gate the /users/me/* queries behind a signed-in user
description:
web/src/api/queries/me.ts: none of the five hooks accept an 'enabled' option, so they fire for anonymous visitors and 401.

web/src/pages/Dashboard/HomeBand.tsx mounts three of them (useMyNamespaces, useWatches, useMyDriftFeed) at component scope. Its <Show when={user()}> guard is inside the returned JSX — far too late to stop the fetches. The file's own doc comment says 'Only mount this when there is a user'; the code does not honour it.

Change: add an options arg carrying 'enabled' to all five hooks in me.ts (TanStack Query supports it in the options object returned from createQuery). Pass 'enabled: user() !== undefined' from HomeBand.tsx and any other caller.

Verify: private window on / -> devtools network shows zero /users/me/* requests.
notes:
Files: web/src/api/queries/selfScoped.ts (new), me.ts, watches.ts, index.ts, web/src/pages/Dashboard/HomeBand.tsx, HomeBand.test.tsx
Approach: New SelfScopedOptions { enabled?: () => boolean } + selfScopedEnabled() helper shared by every /api/v1/users/me/* hook. Applied to all five hooks in me.ts and both in watches.ts (useWatches, useWatchFeed) — useWatches is one of the three HomeBand mounts, so gating me.ts alone would have left the bug half-fixed.

enabled is an ACCESSOR, not a boolean, because the auth resource resolves after first paint: a by-value 'user() !== undefined' captures false at mount and the query would then never run for a signed-in user either. Documented at both the type and the call site.

HomeBand passes { enabled: signedIn }. Its existing <Show when={user()}> only ever gated the markup — the hooks run at component scope, which is exactly why the file's own doc comment ('Only mount this when there is a user') was not being honoured.

Tests: two new HomeBand cases asserting the enabled accessor resolves false signed-out and true signed-in. Noted in the test why the pre-existing 'renders nothing when signed out' case passed while the component still fired three 401s.

Gates: frontend-typecheck clean, frontend-lint 0 errors (5 pre-existing warnings), frontend-test 37 files / 316 tests.

title: unwrap() must not hard-navigate to /login on 401
description:
web/src/api/client.ts: unwrap() does 'window.location.href = "/login"' on ANY 401. One auth-scoped widget on an otherwise-public page therefore destroys the whole page.

Change: delete the redirect branch; always throw APIClientError(response.status, error). Add an optional 'expectsAuth?: boolean' so a genuinely auth-only call can still opt into signalling.

Redirect responsibility already lives in the right place: components/Layout.tsx has an authedPaths createEffect (["/admin", "/dashboard", "/clusters"]) that navigates to /login when !user.loading && user() === undefined. Its own comment acknowledges the unwrap hack. Leave that effect as the only redirect.

Verify: grep for window.location in web/src returns no auth redirect. make frontend-typecheck + frontend-test green.
Blocks ocidex-ag4q.3 and .4 — do this first.
notes:
Files: web/src/api/client.ts, web/src/api/client.test.ts (new)
Approach: Deleted the 'if (response.status === 401) window.location.href = "/login"' branch from unwrap(); it now always throws APIClientError. Documented in the doc comment that redirecting is a routing decision owned solely by Layout's authedPaths effect, and that elsewhere a 401 is data the caller decides how to degrade.

Deviation from the issue text: instead of the proposed 'expectsAuth?: boolean' opt-in (which would have shipped an unused parameter with no consumer), added an exported isUnauthorized(err) predicate. That is the shape the downstream stories actually need — .4 hides the workloads section, .43 degrades a section to empty, .46 degrades one palette result group — and it keeps unwrap() free of routing concerns entirely.

Regression test: client.test.ts is a .test.ts, so per vite.config.ts environmentMatchGlobs it runs in vitest's node environment where window is undefined. A reach for window.location fails there as a ReferenceError, so asserting the rejection is an APIClientError is a genuine guard against the redirect coming back rather than a restatement of the happy path.

Gates: frontend-typecheck clean, frontend-lint 0 errors (5 pre-existing warnings), frontend-test 37 files / 314 tests passing.

title: sbom-push pod unschedulable: summed step CPU requests exceed node capacity
description: Tekton schedules on the sum of a pod's container requests, but steps run sequentially. sbom-push has 6 steps summing to 1100m CPU; the single untainted worker has ~1000m free while an image-build (600m) runs. The pod pends for the full 1h task timeout, fails, and Tekton then skips the remaining 5 image builds and helm-publish — blocking image push and deploy.
notes:
Files: .tektonic/jobs/sbom-push/spec.ts, .tekton/tasks/sbom-push.k8s.yaml
Approach: cut CPU *requests* (not limits) on the three steps this task owns — build-binaries 500m→250m, syft-catalog 200m→50m, push-sboms 100m→50m. Pod request sum 1100m→650m, which fits the worker's ~1000m free alongside a 600m image-build. Limits unchanged, so the build still bursts to 2 CPUs on an idle node. Verified with an isolated TaskRun (verify-sbom-push-sched) against kp4zn's workspace PVC: pod scheduled onto talos-jlf-6ro and all six steps exited 0. tektonic is not installed locally so the generated YAML was hand-edited to match the spec, per CLAUDE.md.
close_reason: sbom-push step CPU requests cut 1100m->650m sum; verified in isolated TaskRun and confirmed Succeeded in push pipeline lx4g6

title: perf: rollup tables + refresher for components/licenses/vulns lists
description:
The three list endpoints aggregate the whole 10.9M-row component table on every request (COUNT(DISTINCT) forces GroupAggregate, COUNT(*) OVER() forces full materialization). EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the Components query: 53,203ms, 1,051,986 rows sorted with a 65MB external-merge disk spill, 499,729 heap fetches. Results are tiny: 121,079 rows at (registry_id,name,group_name,type) grain.

New migration 00048_list_rollups.sql with plain tables (not matviews - sqlc parses tables unambiguously):
- component_rollup(registry_id, type, name, group_name, versions text[], sbom_count bigint) ~121k rows
- license_rollup(license_id, registry_id, identity_key text) <=500k rows
- vuln_rollup(canonical_id, registry_id, sbom_count bigint, purls text[]) <=24k rows

Grain is (registry_id, ...) because sbom_visible() is purely a function of registry. sbom_count sums exactly (an SBOM belongs to one registry); arrays preserve distinct sets so COUNT(DISTINCT) stays exact under any visibility subset.

Rewrite SearchDistinctComponents, ListLicenses, ListTopVulnerabilities against the rollups; point GetSummaryCounts and GetTopPackagesByVersionCount at component_rollup too (removes 2 of the 7 warmer queries).

Refresher (internal/service/rollup_refresher.go + internal/repository/rollup_refresh.go): CREATE TEMP TABLE AS <aggregate> then TRUNCATE+INSERT in one txn so the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock is held sub-second. Single-flight via pg_try_advisory_lock. Runs on the 2-conn background pool from ocidex-ckv.1.

Files: db/migrations/00048_list_rollups.sql, db/queries/search.sql, db/queries/vulnerability.sql, internal/service/search_stats.go
notes:
Files:
- db/migrations/00051_list_rollups.sql (component_rollup, license_rollup, vuln_rollup + seed)
- db/migrations/00052_visible_registry_ids.sql (set-returning companion to sbom_visible)
- db/queries/search.sql (SearchDistinctComponents, ListLicenses, ListComponentPurlTypes)
- db/queries/stats.sql (GetSummaryCounts, GetTopPackagesByVersionCount)
- db/queries/vulnerability.sql (ListTopVulnerabilities)
- internal/repository/rollup_refresh.go (aggregates, advisory lock, temp-table swap, watermark)
- internal/service/rollup_refresher.go (+_test.go) (watermark-gated poll loop)
- cmd/ocidex/main.go (startup log)
- tests/{auth,integration,vuln}_integration_test.go (rollup/stats harness)

Approach:
The three list endpoints aggregated the whole 10.9M-row component table per
request. Replaced with rollup tables at (registry_id, identity) grain — 121k,
10.3k, 3.2k rows. Grain works because sbom_visible() is purely a function of the
registry, so a viewer's row subset re-aggregates exactly. Counts that decompose
over registries are integers; counts needing DISTINCT across registries keep
their sets in arrays and are re-counted at read time.

Second, separate win found during EXPLAIN: sbom_visible() is STABLE with an
EXISTS over registry inside, so filtering a rollup called it once per rollup row
— 121,080 EXISTS lookups and 242k buffer hits to distinguish 8 registries. Added
visible_registry_ids() (migration 00052) returning the visible set, so the
planner evaluates the rule 8 times and semi-joins. Scan node 3,818ms -> 100ms.
Equivalence to sbom_visible proven exhaustively on dev: 0 disagreements across
every (registry x viewer x admin-flag) combination. Callers keep an explicit
'registry_id IS NULL OR' arm because NULL registry_id is visible to everyone but
matches no IN list.

Measured on dev (1-core Postgres, concurrently loaded by the still-deployed
pre-ckv.1 warmer):
  old, aggregate component      53,203 ms, 65MB external-merge spill
  rollup, per-row sbom_visible   6.7-8.4 s  (4 interleaved rounds)
  rollup, visible_registry_ids   1.0-1.8 s  (same rounds; 498ms best observed)
A 13MB external merge remains at work_mem=4MB; homelab-aeg's work_mem=32MB turns
it into an in-memory quicksort.

Refresh: BuildRollupSnapshots into ON COMMIT DROP temp tables (the slow part,
no locks), then TRUNCATE+INSERT in the same txn, so the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE window
is sub-second. Guarded by pg_try_advisory_xact_lock for single-flight across
replicas; SET LOCAL lock_timeout so the swap cannot queue behind a long read.

Freshness: rollup-backed search meant a just-ingested SBOM would not appear for
up to the refresh interval. Added a watermark — (count(*), max(created_at)) over
sbom, thousands of rows not millions — polled every 30s, with a 2-minute minimum
gap so a registry scan cannot cause back-to-back rebuilds on the 2-connection
background pool, and the 15-minute interval as an unconditional backstop for
vulnerability/license changes the sbom watermark cannot see. RefreshNow() drives
one pass synchronously for the integration harness.

Parity vs the old queries, verified in REPEATABLE READ txns that rebuild and roll
back against live data:
- components: 0 mismatches in admin, anon, and registry-subset scopes
- vulnerabilities: 0 mismatches in all three scopes
- licenses: every difference traced to two defects in the OLD query, both fixed
  by the rewrite. (1) COUNT(DISTINCT (a, COALESCE(b,''), COALESCE(c,''), d)) over
  a non-matching LEFT JOIN row yields (NULL,'','',NULL), which is not the NULL
  row, so COUNT counted it — every license with zero visible components reported
  exactly 1 (14 licenses in dev). (2) The visibility test sat in WHERE rather
  than the JOIN condition, so a license whose components are all in invisible
  registries lost every joined row and vanished from the list entirely — 158
  cases in the registry-subset scope, all confirmed to have zero visible
  components (dropped_licenses_with_visible_components = 0).

Known behaviour change: the purl_type filter. The old query filtered individual
component rows, so an identity spanning two ecosystems reported only the matching
subset's versions/SBOMs; the new one tests = ANY(r.purl_types) and selects the
whole rollup row. Measured at 18 of 121,080 rollup rows (0.015%). Documented in
the component_rollup.purl_types COMMENT. Keeping purl_types as an array is what
lets sbom_count stay a summable integer.

NOT verified: the integration suite could not be run locally — the Docker daemon
is unavailable in this environment, so testcontainers cannot start. The
integration changes (refreshRollups/warmStats harness) are compile-checked by go
vet and go build only. tests/vuln_integration_test.go:276 was already broken by
the committed ckv.1 work (GetDashboardStats no longer computes on a cache miss
and NewSearchService always installs a cache, so the test saw Warming:true);
warmStats() fixes it, but that fix is likewise unrun.

Gates: go build, go vet, gofmt clean; go test ./... all packages ok; make lint
59 issues vs a 61-issue committed baseline (dupl 2 dropped), zero new.

title: perf: bound stats warmer, per-registry cache key, no synchronous compute
description:
The ocidex-7qt stats warmer runs on a fixed 5-min ticker but a pass takes ~5.6 min (171s/scope x 2 scopes), so passes overlap forever. Each pass runs 7 aggregates concurrently against a 1-CPU Postgres, saturating all 10 pool connections; HTTP handlers then queue past the 30s chi timeout.

Also GetDashboardStats computes synchronously on cache miss, and statsCacheKey returns u:<uuid> for authenticated non-admins which warmedScopes() never warms - so those users always take the 170s path, always time out, and never populate the cache.

Changes:
- StatsWarmer.Run: sleep-after-completion loop instead of time.Ticker so passes never overlap
- WarmDashboardStats: errgroup SetLimit(2)
- statsCacheKey: key on hash of visible registry IDs (admin -> 'all') instead of user UUID
- GetDashboardStats: return cached-or-empty with a warming marker, never fall through to WarmDashboardStats
- cmd/ocidex/main.go: dedicated pgxpool (MaxConns 2) for warmer/refresher

Files: internal/service/stats_warmer.go, search_stats.go, stats_cache.go, cmd/ocidex/main.go
notes:
Files: internal/service/stats_warmer.go, search_stats.go, search.go, stats_cache.go; internal/api/types.go, search.go; cmd/ocidex/main.go; db/queries/registry.sql; web/src/api/queries/stats.ts, web/src/pages/Home.tsx.

Approach: four changes, each addressing one leg of the pool-starvation loop.
1. StatsWarmer.Run: time.Ticker -> timer reset after tick() returns, so the interval is a gap between passes not a period. Production passes took ~5.6min against a 5min ticker, so passes overlapped without bound and held all 10 pool connections permanently.
2. WarmDashboardStats: errgroup g.SetLimit(statsWarmConcurrency=2). Seven aggregates scanning the same large tables on a 1-core Postgres gain nothing from 7-way fan-out.
3. normalizeStatsScope: an authenticated non-admin owning no private registry sees exactly the public set (per sbom_visible), so collapse them onto the shared 'anon' scope the warmer keeps fresh. New query CountOwnedPrivateRegistries. Fails closed - keeps the viewer's own scope on error rather than widening it.
4. GetDashboardStats no longer falls through to WarmDashboardStats on a miss; it returns DashboardStats{Warming:true}. Computing on the request path could never finish inside the 30s chi timeout and each attempt occupied connections in-flight requests needed.
Plus: dedicated background pgxpool (MaxConns=2) via WithWarmDB so warm passes cannot touch the request pool; setupDatabase now opens both (merged with the old setupBackgroundDatabase, which had pushed run() to gocyclo 16).
Frontend: 'warming' surfaces on DashboardStatsOutput; Home.tsx treats it as loading rather than rendering '0 artifacts', and the query polls every 15s while warming.

Tests: stats_scope_test.go (scope collapse, fail-closed, admin/anon passthrough, warming-on-miss, warmed-entry serving); TestStatsWarmerNeverOverlapsPasses asserts max 1 pass in flight; Home.test.tsx covers the warming placeholder. make test green; lint baseline unchanged (61 pre-existing issues on main, gocyclo regression fixed).

title: provenance reports Verified=true with zero cryptographic checks
description:
applyVerification (internal/enrichment/provenance/verify.go:53-62) and applyKeylessVerification (keyless.go:107-120) both do:

    verified := true
    if raw.SigPresent { verified = verified \&\& verifyOCISignature(...) }
    if raw.AttPresent \&\& raw.AttArtifactType != inTotoArtifactType { verified = verified \&\& verifyOCIAttestation(...) }
    p.Verified = \&verified

The only guard is 'if !raw.SigPresent \&\& !raw.AttPresent { return }'. A buildkit-native raw in-toto attestation (application/vnd.in-toto+json) with no cosign signature satisfies that guard and then skips BOTH branches, so Verified is set to true having performed no verification at all. The comment on verify.go:57 states raw in-toto atts are 'excluded from cryptographic verification' — that exclusion is being reported to users as 'Verified'.

The keyless path is worse: it also sets p.SignerIdentity and p.SignerIssuer on the false positive, so the UI names a signer whose certificate was never checked.

Reproduced with a throwaway unit test (real ECDSA P-256 key via cryptoutils.MarshalPublicKeyToPEM, RawArtifacts{SigPresent: false, AttPresent: true, AttArtifactType: inTotoArtifactType}) which asserted Verified=true with no verifier invocation.

Fix: track whether any verification branch actually executed; if none did, leave p.Verified nil so SigningStatus falls through to 'signed' rather than 'verified'.
acceptance_criteria: A raw in-toto attestation with no cosign signature yields Verified=nil (status 'signed'), not Verified=true. SignerIdentity/SignerIssuer are only populated when a Fulcio certificate was actually matched. Regression test covers both applyVerification and applyKeylessVerification.
notes:
Files: internal/enrichment/provenance/verify.go, keyless.go, provenance_test.go, keyless_test.go
Approach: added a 'checked' bool in both applyVerification and applyKeylessVerification, set true only when a branch actually invokes verifyOCISignature/verifyOCIAttestation. If neither branch executed, return early leaving p.Verified nil (falls through to SigningStatus 'signed') instead of defaulting to Verified=true. keyless path also skips setting SignerIdentity/SignerIssuer in that case. Added regression tests: raw_intoto_only_no_signature case in TestVerification, TestApplyKeylessVerification_RawInTotoOnlyNoSignature.

title: EMERGENCY: stop the orphan reconciler in prod
description: The reconciler is currently republishing 100 jobs every 5 min on each scanner-worker pod, creating duplicate stream messages that workers waste cycles re-processing (confirmed by 'skipping duplicate sbom ingestion' log lines). Remove the runJobReconciler goroutine from cmd/scanner-worker/main.go. Ship this independently before the bigger refactor so prod gets relief immediately. The catalog walker + workers will drain the 1093-job backlog naturally over ~45h.
notes: Files: cmd/scanner-worker/main.go\nApproach: Removed the runJobReconciler goroutine startup; left the function body in place for the outbox refactor to delete cleanly. Confirmed via prod logs that the reconciler was claiming exactly 100 jobs per 5-min tick (batchSize cap) and workers were processing 'skipping duplicate sbom ingestion' rows — direct evidence of self-inflicted duplicate work.

title: Authenticated local dev rig for browser-verifying auth-gated pages
description:
Auth-gated surfaces (/clusters, /dashboard, /admin) have had zero browser verification this epic. The prod-proxy rig (make frontend-dev-live) is signed-out only, because the prod session cookie is scoped to ocidex.app and does not travel to localhost. Everything on those pages is unit-test-verified, which cannot catch the bug class this epic exists to fix: a dialog too narrow for its fields, a select that overflows, contrast failures.

Two blocking premises turn out to be false:

1. CLAUDE.md and web/vite.config.live.ts both assert there is no local Postgres because docker is unavailable. postgresql (17.10) and nats-server (2.14.2) are already in the Flox manifest as native binaries. No containers needed.

2. No auth-bypass code is needed. internal/api/middleware.go:44 already accepts 'Authorization: Bearer <api-key>' as a first-class path equivalent to a session, and hasWriteAccess grants writes to a read-write key. Keys are 'ocidex_' + base64url(rand) stored as sha256 hex (internal/service/auth.go:195,334), so a local admin user plus key is a pair of SQL inserts.

Build: a scripted local stack (initdb/pg_ctl on a scratch dir, nats-server, ocidex migrate up, seeded admin user + read-write API key, go run ./cmd/ocidex) and a dev-only vite config that injects the Bearer header into the /api proxy.

Explicitly rejected: injecting the production session cookie into the live proxy. It would authenticate as the user against production, and the surfaces needing verification are write flows -- verifying the cluster modal would create real clusters in the real database. The read-only constraint on that rig stays.

Also correct the stale docker claim in CLAUDE.md and vite.config.live.ts.
notes:
Files: scripts/dev-auth.sh (new), web/vite.config.auth.ts (new), Makefile (dev-auth-{up,down,status,reset}, frontend-dev-auth), .gitignore (.dev/), CLAUDE.md, web/vite.config.live.ts.

Approach: two false premises removed the need for most of the anticipated work.

(1) postgresql 17.10 and nats-server 2.14.2 were already in the Flox manifest as native binaries -- the 'docker is unavailable so there is no local Postgres' claim in CLAUDE.md and vite.config.live.ts was simply stale. scripts/dev-auth.sh does initdb/pg_ctl on .dev/pgdata (:5433), nats-server (:4222, -js), 'ocidex migrate up', seeds an admin + namespace, and runs 'go run ./cmd/ocidex' (:8080) with pidfiles. Subcommands: up/down/status/key/reset.

(2) No auth-bypass code was needed. internal/api/middleware.go:44 already accepts 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' as equivalent to a session cookie, and hasWriteAccess (line 24) grants writes to a read-write key. The script mints one hashed exactly as internal/service/auth.go:195,334 does it -- 'ocidex_' + base64url(rand32), stored as hex(sha256(plaintext)), prefix = first 8 chars -- so it validates through the ordinary ValidateAPIKey path. vite.config.auth.ts (:3200) injects the header in the proxy, and only when absent, so a deliberate 401 test still works. GitHub OAuth vars are placeholders purely because startup validates their presence; /auth is never exercised.

Rejected: injecting the prod session cookie into vite.config.live.ts. It would authenticate as the user against PRODUCTION, and the pages needing verification are write flows -- checking the cluster modal that way would create real clusters in the real database. The live rig's read-only constraint stays, and CLAUDE.md now says so explicitly.

Verified end to end: /users/me returns role=admin through the proxy while an unauthenticated call to the same API 401s; up/down/up cycle clean with credentials persisting; /clusters, /admin/jobs and the register dialog all render signed in. Screenshotting the dialog immediately found two defects invisible to happy-dom -> filed .56 (dialog CSS lives in SourcesTab.css, not with the Modal primitive) and .57 (740px dialog with 189px fields).

Gates: frontend-lint 0 errors / 5 pre-existing warnings, tsc clean, bash -n clean.

title: Rebuild SBOMDetail: one package count, StatBand summary
description:
pages/SBOMDetail/ shows THREE different package counts on one screen. A user cannot tell which is authoritative, which is the sharpest single example of the app feeling untrustworthy.

Change:
- establish which figure is correct (total components vs deduped vs OS-package-only), render ONE, and document the definition in a tooltip using components/ui/Tooltip
- adopt the generic StatBand from the Phase 1 story, including its new vulnerability tile
- keep the existing SBOM-specific helpers (provenanceSubline, shortBuilder) at this call site

Verify: /sboms/:id shows a single package figure that matches the API response; all frontend gates green; SummaryBand.test.tsx updated.
notes:
Files: web/src/pages/SBOMDetail/index.tsx, PackagesTab.tsx, PackagesTab.test.tsx (new, 8 tests - first coverage for this file)

Which figure is authoritative: packageCount. db/queries/search.sql CountSBOMPackages counts component WHERE type != 'file' (958 on the reference SBOM); CountSBOMComponents counts every row including file entries (4193). The packages tab lists exactly the non-file set, so packageCount is the one that matches what is on screen. The third figure, 200, was just props.components.length - the window the infinite query had loaded.

Approach:
- header subtitle drops the component count entirely; the StatBand tile owns the package figure (epic rule: no card restates what the header said)
- PackagesTab takes totalCount + componentCount props and quotes the server total: '200 of 958 packages loaded' while hasMore, plain '958 packages' once complete
- a filtered count stays quoted against the loaded rows and now says so ('12 of 200 loaded packages') - text/type filters are client-side, so quoting a filtered count against 958 would be wrong
- removed the count from the 'All types (200)' select option; the count line beside it is the honest one
- Tooltip on the count line explains the definition and reconciles all three former figures

Tooltip placement is deliberate: it went on the count line, not the Packages tile, because the tile is a <button> and Tooltip's trigger span carries tabindex=0 - nesting them adds a second tab stop that announces nothing.

Mutation-verified: quoting the loaded window instead of the total => 2 tests fail; quoting the filtered count against the total => 1 fails. Browser-checked on :3100 - one package figure (958) on the page, tooltip renders the reconciliation.

title: Rebuild ArtifactDetail: one header, one tab strip
description:
pages/ArtifactDetail/index.tsx currently stacks, top to bottom:
  <ArtifactHeader>       — name, type, namespace
  <ArtifactAboutCard>    — repeats the header VERBATIM
  <VulnSummaryBar>       — a bare bar, not part of any summary
  <TabBar> then a second <TabBar>
Two tab strips on one page is the clearest instance of 'buried layers deep' in the app.

Target shape (from pages/ClusterDetail/, the best page in the app):
  PageHeader -> StatBand (the answer, above the fold) -> one TabBar -> detail on demand.

Change:
- delete ArtifactAboutCard; anything it shows that the header does not goes into StatBand tiles
- fold VulnSummaryBar into a StatBand vulnerability tile
- collapse the two TabBars into one; if the second strip's dimension is genuinely orthogonal, it becomes a Toolbar filter, not a second nav

Verify: screenshot /artifacts/:id at 1440x900 and diff against ~/.firefox-devtools-mcp/ocidex/ — the answer must now be above the fold. All frontend gates green.
notes:
Files: web/src/pages/ArtifactDetail/{index.tsx,ArtifactHeader.tsx,ArtifactBand.tsx,ArtifactBand.test.tsx}, web/src/components/{VulnTile.tsx,SummaryBand.tsx}, db/queries/artifact.sql, internal/service/search_artifact.go

Approach: Page now follows the ClusterDetail shape - header, StatBand, one TabBar.
- ArtifactBand (new): 5 tiles - versions/SBOMs/vulnerabilities/signing/tracked. Signing tile is container-gated (on an uploaded binary it would be a permanent 'unsigned' nothing can change).
- ArtifactAboutCard deleted: it restated the header verbatim. The two facts it alone carried (purl/cpe/internal id) moved into a collapsed <details> ArtifactIdentity below the band.
- VulnSummaryBar folded into components/VulnTile.tsx, now shared with SummaryBand so the two bands cannot disagree. No summary => 'not scanned', never 0 (ADR-044: unknown must not read as clean). Tile is deliberately non-selectable - neither page has a vulnerabilities tab.
- Second TabBar (semver/all) demoted to a btn-group segmented control with aria-pressed, shown only for the versions/changelog tabs. It orders one list; it is not a destination.
- Backend bug found while verifying: ArtifactDetail inherits SufficientSbomCount from ArtifactSummary and GetArtifact never set it, so the detail endpoint served a permanent 0 while the list endpoint served 246 for the same artifact. Fixed additively with CountSufficientSBOMsByArtifact (separate query, so CountSBOMsByArtifact's callers do not churn).
- Tests: ArtifactBand.test.tsx, 11 cases, mutation-verified against 3 regressions (dropping the container gate, collapsing the 'all fully enriched' branch, letting unscanned read as clean). Note for future test authors: Solid mergeProps skips an undefined value in a later source, so JSX-spread defaults silently ignore an explicit `vulns: undefined` - merge in plain JS and spread once.
Gates: frontend lint/typecheck clean, 431 frontend tests pass, go build + go test ./internal/... pass. Browser-verified at 1470px: 1 tab bar, band bottom at 232px (above the fold), 0 tile overflow, no body h-scroll.

title: Generalize SummaryBand into a reusable StatBand
description:
components/SummaryBand.tsx + TileBand.css is the strongest summary pattern in the app, but it is hardcoded to 'export type SbomTab = packages | provenance | image | git | raw' and has exactly one call site (SBOMDetail). Every other detail page therefore invents its own top-of-page summary — five different patterns across the app.

Change: make it generic over the tab id and data-driven —
  StatBand<T extends string>({ tiles: { id: T; head; value; sub; icon?; tone? }[], active: T, onSelect: (id: T) => void })
Keep TileBand.css untouched. Port the SBOM call site to the generic form, preserving its provenanceSubline / shortBuilder helpers (move them to the SBOM caller — they are SBOM-specific).

Also add a VULNERABILITIES tile to the SBOM band; it is missing today, which is why SBOMDetail's vuln count is buried below the fold.

The target shape is pages/ClusterDetail/'s CoverageBand (containers / matched / no-SBOM / unresolvable) — the best summary in the app. StatBand becomes the shared version of it.

Verify: SummaryBand.test.tsx updated and passing; /sboms/:id renders the same band plus the new vuln tile.
notes:
Files: web/src/components/ui/StatBand.tsx (new), StatBand.test.tsx (new, 15 tests), components/SummaryBand.tsx, SummaryBand.test.tsx, components/TileBand.css, ui/index.ts, pages/SBOMDetail/index.tsx

Approach: StatBand takes tiles: {id?, href?, icon?, head, value, sub?, valueClass?}[] and is generic over the tab id. Tile element is derived from which nav field is set - id => button reporting to onSelect and carrying .active, href => link (CoverageBand's shape), neither => plain div - so there is no separate 'interactive' flag to keep in sync and a read-only tile cannot look clickable. valueClass is free-form rather than a tone enum on purpose: trust and severity vocabularies already live in utils/trust.ts and VulnBadge.tsx.

SummaryBand now builds tiles and delegates, keeping the SBOM-specific shortBuilder/provenanceSubline. It gained the vulnerability tile the band was missing (new vulns prop, wired from SBOMDetail). That tile distinguishes never-scanned ('not scanned') from scanned-and-clean ('no known vulnerabilities') per the epic's rule that an unknown must never read as clean, and puts severity in a SeverityPill in the sub-line rather than colouring the count - the sev-* classes are badge backgrounds and would paint a block behind the number.

TileBand.css: grid is repeat(auto-fit, minmax(11rem, 1fr)) plus min-width: 0 on .tile. Both previous fixed column counts shipped wrong and neither failed a unit test - a literal 4 wrapped the SBOM band's 5th tile onto its own row, and a count derived from tile count made 6 tiles ~100px, narrower than the 'Verification failed' badge, so every tile overflowed. Found in the browser on :3100, then pinned by CSS contract tests in the StatBand layout describe (mutation-verified: fixed count => 2 fail, dropped min-width => 1 fail). Left as a deliberate trade: a 6-tile band wraps 4+2 below ~1290px rather than clipping.

Non-selectable vuln tile is intentional until ocidex-ag4q.34 gives the page a destination for it.

title: Add a Toolbar primitive for list-page filters
description:
Four list pages use four different filter idioms:
  Artifacts.tsx   — 300ms-debounced live input + a <select> whose value lives in useSearchParams; keyset LoadMore
  Components.tsx  — three UNDEBOUNCED live inputs in local signals + a Clear button; offset Pagination
  Vulnerabilities.tsx — .tab-bar severity filter + a submit-on-Enter form for ID search
  Licenses.tsx    — .tab-bar category filter + a two-input submit form

Create components/ui/Toolbar.tsx, exported from the barrel. It renders one filter row and standardises on the best behaviour already present in the tree:
- text inputs debounced at 300ms (the Artifacts behaviour)
- selects
- a Clear action (the Components behaviour)
- all state persisted via useSearchParams, so every filtered view survives reload and is shareable — Artifacts already does this for its type filter and explains why in a comment

Reuse the existing .search-bar CSS (index.css:487-497).

DO NOT migrate the four pages here — that is four separate Phase 2 sessions.

Verify: Toolbar.test.tsx covering debounce, clear, and URL round-trip.
notes:
Files: web/src/components/ui/Toolbar.tsx (new), Toolbar.test.tsx (new, 16 tests), components/ui/index.ts (barrel), index.css (.toolbar-check only).

Approach: one <form class="search-bar"> holding text/select/checkbox fields declared as a ToolbarField[] config array. All filter state lives in useSearchParams — the component holds no state of its own beyond the in-flight keystroke draft.

Decisions worth carrying into the four adoption stories (.28-.31):
- The debounce delays the URL WRITE, not the input's displayed value. A local draft signal drives the box, so typing is never laggy or reordered. The resync effect skips any field with a timer in flight, so an external URL change (back button, Clear) never yanks characters out from under the cursor.
- Enter flushes pending writes immediately instead of waiting out the timer, which is why this is a <form> rather than a <div>. That preserves the submit affordance Licenses and Vulnerabilities have today.
- A cleared field drops its param rather than writing an empty one, so 'absent' is the single representation of 'not filtering'.
- Clear counts a pending draft as active — hiding the button while there is visible text in a box reads as the button being broken.
- OUT OF SCOPE, deliberately: the Vulnerabilities 'Jump to CVE id' form. It navigates to a detail page rather than narrowing a list, so it is not a filter even though it currently shares .search-bar.

Two findings for later stories:
- This repo runs vitest WITHOUT globals, so @solidjs/testing-library cannot register its own afterEach. Components stay mounted across tests; a debounce left pending by one test commits into the next test's URL. Any future timer-based test needs an explicit afterEach(cleanup). Cost me a real failure here.
- @solidjs/router coerces an empty-string param to absent on its own. The test that looked like it proved the undefined mapping actually proved the router's behaviour; retitled and commented rather than left overstating.

Mutation-verified: removing the debounce fails 2 tests, removing Clear's timer cancellation fails 1.

Gates: lint 0 errors (5 pre-existing warnings elsewhere), tsc clean, 395/395 tests.

title: Add a Button primitive
description:
65 raw 'btn' class strings across web/src and no Button component in components/ui/ — the barrel (components/ui/index.ts) exports Badge, Card, DetailGrid, FormField, Modal, QueryBoundary, SigningBadge, TabBar, Tooltip, TypeBadge, expanded, but nothing for the most-used control in the app.

Create components/ui/Button.tsx + Button.test.tsx, exported from the barrel.
Props: variant 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'danger' | 'ghost'; size 'sm' | 'md'; loading; disabled; as?: 'a' (so link-styled buttons stop hand-rolling the class).
It must wrap the EXISTING CSS — .btn, .btn-primary, .btn-danger, .btn-sm, .btn-group (index.css:419-486). No new visual language in this story.

DO NOT migrate callers here — that is the Phase 2 adoption sweep, split across three sessions.

Verify: Button.test.tsx covers each variant's class output and the disabled/loading states.
notes:
Files: web/src/components/ui/Button.tsx, Button.test.tsx, ui/index.ts, web/src/index.css, web/src/components/Feedback.css
Approach: variant primary/danger/ghost map to .btn-$variant; SECONDARY DELIBERATELY EMITS NOTHING — the bare .btn is the secondary button and no .btn-secondary rule exists (one caller writes that dead string today; the .20 sweep removes it). Added .btn-ghost (transparent .btn, regains chrome on :hover) because the app already had ghost buttons written as inline styles. Added .btn-spinner sized in em + currentColor so it scales with btn-sm and stays legible on btn-primary's fill; moved @keyframes spin from Feedback.css to index.css since only index.css is guaranteed loaded. as='a' renders an anchor and signals disabled via aria-disabled only (an anchor has no disabled property). loading implies disabled — a spinning button that still accepts clicks is how double-submits happen. 18 tests incl. a contract block asserting every class the primitive can emit has a rule in index.css. Browser-verified via injected probe on :3100: all five variants + spinner + btn-group active resolve to distinct computed styles.

title: Add a PageHeader primitive
description:
The .page-header / .page-header-row markup from components/Layout.css is hand-repeated in 19 page files, e.g. pages/Admin.tsx:65-76.

Create components/ui/PageHeader.tsx, exported from the barrel.
Props: title, subtitle?, actions? (right-hand slot), breadcrumb? (reserved for the Phase 4 breadcrumb story — accept and render it now).
Emit exactly the existing .page-header / .page-header-row structure so no CSS changes.

DO NOT migrate the 19 pages here — that is a separate Phase 2 story.

Verify: PageHeader.test.tsx asserting the class structure and that actions land in the right slot.
notes:
Files: web/src/components/ui/PageHeader.tsx (new), PageHeader.test.tsx (new, 9 tests), components/ui/index.ts (barrel export). Approach: emits the existing .page-header > .page-header-row structure verbatim, so zero CSS changes. Props: title, subtitle?, actions?, breadcrumb?. Three decisions worth carrying forward: - The title+subtitle wrapper div is load-bearing, not cosmetic. .page-header-row is justify-content: space-between; emitting h2/p/actions as three siblings spreads them across the row instead of pinning actions right. Mutation-verified: unwrapping it fails 2 of the 9 tests (row child count). - The subtitle carries NO class. Several call sites write

, but .page-header p already resolves to --color-text-muted, so that class is a no-op. Not carried forward. - breadcrumb renders INSIDE .page-header, above the row; pages currently emit a sibling .breadcrumb div just before the header. Verified in the browser (localhost:3100 probe) that both produce identical title/action geometry, so the Phase 4 breadcrumb story can move call sites in without a layout shift. No callers migrated — that is the Phase 2 story (plan 2.2). Gates: lint clean (5 pre-existing warnings elsewhere), tsc clean, 379/379 tests.

title: Establish a type scale
description:
index.css sets html { font-size: 14px }. Measured on prod: body 14px, h2 21px — a 1.5x ratio, which is why headings do not establish hierarchy and pages read flat.

Change: add --text-xs through --text-3xl tokens to the @theme block alongside the existing --radius-* scale, and apply them to h1-h4, .page-header h2, and .card-header h3. Keep the 14px root (it is deliberate density) but widen the heading ratios.

Do not change component markup here — this is tokens + element selectors only.

Verify: make frontend-test green; screenshot /artifacts and /clusters/:id at 1440x900 and compare heading weight against the baselines in ~/.firefox-devtools-mcp/ocidex/.
notes:
Files: web/src/index.css, web/src/components/Layout.css, web/src/typeScale.test.ts
Approach: --text-xs..3xl in @theme. Key constraint found during the work: Tailwind v4 GENERATES text-xs/sm/base/lg/xl/2xl/3xl utilities from this exact token namespace, so xs/sm/base are pinned to Tailwind's defaults (70 text-sm call sites) and only the heading end widens. Second finding: preflight resets h1-h6 to font-size/font-weight inherit, so bare headings were body-size app-wide — hence new h1-h4 base rules (600 weight, tightened leading) alongside the token application. .page-header h2 1.5rem -> --text-3xl (28px), .card-header h3 1rem -> --text-lg (16px); both now one real step apart. typeScale.test.ts guards existence, strict monotonicity, the Tailwind-default pin, and that the six guarded selectors size from var(--text-*) not literals. Mutation-verified. Screenshot comparison deferred until the epic deploys.

title: Load the typefaces the tokens already specify
description:
index.css:1 links ONLY Space Grotesk. But the tokens declare:
  --font-sans: 'Inter', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif
  --font-mono: 'JetBrains Mono', 'Fira Code', 'Cascadia Code', monospace
Neither Inter nor JetBrains Mono is ever fetched, so every body string renders in the OS system font and every digest / purl / SHA renders in generic monospace.

Verified live: Array.from(document.fonts) on ocidex.app returns only Space Grotesk entries. body computed font-family is the Inter stack, resolving to -apple-system.

Change: extend the Google Fonts @import at index.css:1 to include Inter (400,500,600,700) and JetBrains Mono (400,500) with display=swap.

This is the single highest visual-payoff change in the epic and is a one-line diff.

Verify: firefox MCP -> Array.from(document.fonts).map(f => f.family + ':' + f.status) shows Inter and JetBrains Mono as 'loaded'.
notes:
Files: web/src/index.css, web/src/fontContract.test.ts
Approach: extended the single Google Fonts @import to Inter 400/500/600/700 + JetBrains Mono 400/500 alongside Space Grotesk, one request, display=swap kept. Added fontContract.test.ts asserting every family a --font-* token names FIRST is actually requested — the failure mode here is silent (the token still resolves, just to the fallback), so an assertion-only check would not have caught it. Mutation-verified by dropping Inter from the request. Live document.fonts check deferred until the epic deploys.

title: UI overhaul: design system + information architecture
description:
The app reads as inconsistent, bland, and buried. A live sweep of https://ocidex.app (signed out and signed in as pfenerty) plus a read of web/src separates that into three causes.

BROKEN (styling never applies, or the page throws you out):
- unwrap() in web/src/api/client.ts hard-navigates to /login on ANY 401, so one auth-scoped widget destroys an otherwise-public page. Verified: / and /vulnerabilities/CVE-2026-46595 both bounce anonymous visitors even though GET /api/v1/vulns/CVE-2026-46595 returns 200.
- /admin/<tab> renders the wrong panel. At /admin/jobs (even after hard reload) the strip highlights Jobs and the body renders Sources. Cause: web/src/pages/Admin.tsx:97 — on first paint user() is still loading so tabs() is the single non-admin tab (Sources) and active() falls to tabs()[0]; <Show> is non-keyed so its children never re-run when user() resolves.
- The vulnerability severity filter has no visible active state. pages/Vulnerabilities.tsx:132 emits 'tab-btn tab-active'; neither class exists in index.css (the contract is .tab-bar button.active). Live computed style: all six tabs identical.
- The designed typefaces never load. index.css:1 links only Space Grotesk; --font-sans: Inter and --font-mono: JetBrains Mono fall back to -apple-system / generic monospace.
- /components top rows are dead links. GET /api/v1/components/versions?name=... measured 500 @ 30.4s (golang.org/x/crypto), 500 @ 30.5s (stdlib), 200 @ 24.6s / 2.54MB (zlib). Peers: /artifacts?limit=20 2.27s, /licenses?limit=20 0.54s. Unpaginated.

NO DESIGN SYSTEM. 129 .tsx / 17782 lines against 25 .css / 2008 lines, and the de-facto component library is a @layer components block in index.css. Measured: 207 inline style={{}}; 65 raw 'btn' strings with NO Button primitive in components/ui/; 39 raw class=card vs 11 files using <Card>; 15 files with a raw <table> vs 24 using <DataTable>; .page-header hand-repeated in 19 pages. Four list pages use four different filter idioms. tab-bar is overloaded as both filter control and page navigation.

BURIED IA. ArtifactDetail stacks a header, an ArtifactAboutCard that repeats it verbatim, a bare VulnSummaryBar, then TWO TabBars. SBOMDetail shows three different package counts on one screen. Clusters keeps a Register-cluster form permanently expanded. .main-content has no max-width (1220px used of a 2200px window). At 390px the 56px rail still renders a 3-line sign-in label over character-wrapped cells.

THE TEMPLATE EXISTS: pages/ClusterDetail/ — 4-tile CoverageBand, tabs, ranked severity, honest exclusion caveat. Every other detail page converges on that shape.

Plan: ~/.claude/plans/i-m-pretty-disastified-with-velvety-hearth.md
Phases: 0 P0 bugs, 1 design-system foundation, 2 adoption sweep, 3 page IA rebuild, 4 findability, 5 responsive/polish. Each child story is one 15-30 minute agent session.

title: False verified→unsigned provenance drift from swallowed registry errors
description: provenance discover() treats every registry failure (429/401/5xx/timeout) as 'no signature found', producing status=unsigned on a successful Enrich, which the dispatcher records as verified→unsigned drift. Fix: classify 404 as absent and everything else as transient error; add a confirmation gate before recording an unsigned transition; widen the reverifier requeue to cover failed jobs.
notes:

title: ADR-042 SBOM lookup 500s when architecture enrichment is absent
description:
GET /api/v1/sboms/lookup returns HTTP 500 for any SBOM that has no successful oci-metadata or user enrichment.

LookupSBOMs in db/queries/sbom.sql casts the architecture COALESCE to ::text, so sqlc infers a NOT NULL column and generates 'Architecture string'. The expression is NULL whenever neither enrichment row exists, and pgx fails with: can't scan into dest[3] (col: architecture): cannot scan NULL into *string.

Reproduced against a live server while verifying the MCP server (ocidex-x59x.4): ingest an SBOM by upload, then look it up by artifact+version. Affects every caller of the resolver - web, CLI and ocidex_lookup_sbom - not just MCP.

Fix: drop the ::text cast so sqlc yields pgtype.Text, regenerate, and read row.Architecture.String in internal/service/search_lookup.go.
notes:
Files: db/queries/sbom.sql, internal/repository/sbom.sql.go (regenerated), tests/lookup_resolver_test.go
Approach: the ::text cast on the architecture COALESCE makes sqlc infer NOT NULL, so a NULL (no oci-metadata and no user enrichment) failed the pgx scan. Added '' as the final COALESCE argument so the cast never sees NULL; absent architecture now reads as empty string, matching the other qualifiers. Integration test ingests an SBOM with no enrichment and asserts /api/v1/sboms/lookup returns 200. Verified against a live server before and after.

title: requireTestInfra silently skips tests under load
description:
requireTestInfra runs 'docker info' per test with a 3s context timeout. On a healthy daemon the probe costs ~1.65s idle, leaving only ~1.35s of margin; once 50+ tests are each starting a Postgres container, the probe exceeds the budget and the test SKIPS with 'neither TEST_POSTGRES_URL nor docker available'.

Observed 2026-08-16: TestVulnSBOMSummaryJoin skipped after exactly 3.00s in a full run (56 pass / 0 fail / 1 skip); the same test passes in 2.72s when run in isolation. Which test gets sacrificed is arbitrary and moves run to run.

This is the precise failure the guard's own doc comment says it exists to prevent: the suite reports ok while a test never ran. It fails open into a skip, and is load-dependent, so it will bite hardest on a busy CI machine.
acceptance_criteria:
Probe runs at most once per test binary, not once per test.
Probe result is cached and load-independent.
Timeout is generous enough that a healthy-but-busy daemon is never mistaken for an absent one.
Full 'make test-integration' run reports 0 skips.
notes:
Files: tests/integration_test.go
Approach: replaced the per-test 'docker info' probe in requireTestInfra with a package-level sync.OnceValue (dockerProbe). The probe now runs at most once per test binary, before any container starts, so its verdict no longer depends on concurrent load. Timeout raised 3s -> 60s: the cost is paid once, and a short budget can only produce the false-negative it caused. Verified: full 'go test -v -race -count=1 ./tests/...' went from 56 pass / 0 fail / 1 skip to 57 pass / 0 fail / 0 skip; make check exits 0.
Caveat: the pre-existing nil-pointer panics in the make check log come from TestAuthClassEnforced in internal/api (deliberate nil-dependency handlers, recovered by chi); unrelated to this change and that test passes.

title: Lookup and search tools built on the ADR-042 resolvers
description: The ADR-042 lookup resolvers are the natural core of the tool set because they are name-keyed rather than UUID-keyed, which is exactly what an agent can supply - an agent asking about nginx has a name, never a UUID. Wrap the artifact, SBOM and license lookup endpoints plus component search, artifact detail, and namespace listing. The important detail is the 409 response: ADR-042 returns 409 with a candidate list when a name is ambiguous under the qualifier ladder, and that must surface to the agent as an actionable disambiguation prompt listing the candidates, not as a generic tool error. Getting that wrong makes the whole server feel broken on the most common query shape.
acceptance_criteria: Tools cover artifact/SBOM/license lookup, component search, artifact detail and namespace listing; a 409 from any lookup returns the candidate list in a form an agent can select from and retry; tool descriptions state the qualifier ladder so an agent knows which qualifiers narrow a search; unit tests via fake_client cover the unique, not-found and ambiguous cases.
notes:
Files: cmd/ocidex-mcp/catalog.go, catalog_test.go, server.go
Approach: six tools registered from registerCatalogTools — ocidex_lookup_artifact, ocidex_get_artifact, ocidex_lookup_sbom, ocidex_lookup_license, ocidex_search_components, ocidex_list_namespaces — all thin wrappers over pkg/client, no raw HTTP. Optional args are plain strings (empty = absent) converted with optional(); jsonschema-go treats omitempty as optional, so required args are the tags without it. Outputs are lean projections of the generated types rather than the types themselves, keeping $schema and transport fields out of the tool output schema. Tool descriptions spell out each ADR-042 ladder (artifact: name->type->group; sbom: artifact+version->arch->flavor, or digest alone; license: spdx_id is a natural key, never ambiguous). 409s route through the existing toolError/describeCandidates, so the candidate list arrives with the query that produced it (describeSBOMQuery). Two impossible queries are rejected locally rather than by a 400 round trip: lookup_sbom without digest-or-(artifact+version), and search_components without name-or-purl. Tests exercise the real SDK in-memory transport (schema validation included) over FakeClient: unique, not-found, ambiguous-with-candidates for artifact and sbom, license found/not-found, component search incl. empty page as a non-error and default limit, namespaces incl. forbidden. Gates: make check EXIT=0, golangci-lint 0 issues.

title: cmd/ocidex-mcp scaffold with CLI credential reuse
description: New stdio MCP server binary wrapping the existing pkg/client SDK. That SDK is oapi-codegen output from the OpenAPI spec and is drift-guarded by make check via the generate-client target, so tool schemas track the API for free - no server changes and no new transport plumbing. Reuse the CLI's credential handling from cmd/ocidex-cli/config.go and login.go so that ocidex-cli login provisions the MCP server too, rather than inventing a second credential store. This story is the transport, lifecycle, config and error mapping; the tools themselves follow in sibling stories. Pick and pin the Go MCP SDK here and record the choice.
acceptance_criteria: cmd/ocidex-mcp builds and registers successfully via claude mcp add; it reads credentials written by ocidex-cli login; API errors from pkg/client map to useful MCP tool errors rather than opaque failures; a smoke test exercises server startup and tool listing against pkg/client/fake_client.go.
notes:
Files: cmd/ocidex-mcp/{main,server,errors}.go + tests; internal/cliconfig/config.go (new, moved out of cmd/ocidex-cli/config.go); cmd/ocidex-cli/{root,login,login_test}.go rewired; docs/adr/0045-mcp-server.md; Makefile build line; CLAUDE.md ADR table + project structure.

Approach:
- SDK: github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk v1.7.0 (spec's own Go SDK, past 1.0, 4 transitive deps). Its generic AddTool derives input/output schemas from Go types and validates arguments before the handler runs, so schemas cannot drift from pkg/client (itself guarded by make check's generate-client-check).
- Credentials: config file handling extracted verbatim into internal/cliconfig (File/Path/Load/Save) plus Resolve (flag>env>file>default) and Settings.RequireKey. cmd/ocidex-cli/config.go deleted, not shimmed — one implementation, so ocidex-cli login provisions the MCP server and logout de-provisions it. No --key flag (argv is visible in the process table).
- Missing key = startup failure, exit 2. A server that connects then fails every tool looks to a model like an empty catalog.
- toolError maps pkg/client's typed errors to messages with advice (404 -> may be invisible rather than absent; 403 -> names the scope; 401 -> re-run ocidex-cli login; 409 ConflictError -> candidate list with sorted qualifiers per ADR-042). All wrap with %w; a first draft did not, and the errors.Is test caught it.
- Shutdown: uses IOTransport over a stdinWatcher rather than StdioTransport. The SDK reports a peer-closed pipe as 'server is closing: EOF' with the EOF formatted in, not wrapped, and the sentinel it does wrap is in an internal package — so errors.Is cannot see it. Watching the read side is the check that does not depend on either. Found by smoke-testing the real binary: it exited 1 on every clean client disconnect.

Verification: make check green (golangci-lint 0 issues). Real-binary stdio smoke test — fed initialize + notifications/initialized + tools/list to bin/ocidex-mcp, got both results back and exit 0, for both a held-open stdin and an abruptly closed one. Not run: 'claude mcp add', which would mutate the user's MCP config; the handshake it exercises is what the smoke test covers.

title: /api/v1/users/me/* self-scoped resources
description: There is no user-scoped anything today beyond GET /api/v1/users/me returning the bare user record, and the API-key endpoints which are self-scoped in the service layer. Add self-scoped collections - my namespaces, my sources, my registries, my artifacts, and my recent activity - so the frontend does not have to fetch everything and filter client-side. These are thin: each is an existing list query with the caller's user ID applied through the ownership path rather than the visibility path, since 'public but not mine' must be excluded here whereas the normal list includes it. That distinction is the one subtle part and is worth a comment at the service boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Each /api/v1/users/me/* collection returns only resources the caller owns, excluding public resources owned by others; endpoints require authentication and are declared in the auth conformance table; pagination follows the ADR from ocidex-wp9b.5; pkg/client and the CLI pick the new endpoints up via make generate-client.
notes:
Files: db/queries/{namespace,source,registry,artifact,search}.sql; internal/service/{registry,namespace,source,search,search_artifact,search_sbom}.go; internal/api/{authz,auth,authclass,namespace,source,registry,search,types_*}.go; tests/me_scoped_test.go
Approach: VisibilityFilter gained OwnedOnly + ownedFlag(); the four existing list queries gained an owned_only narg selecting the ownership path (owner_id = user) instead of the visibility path (admin OR public OR mine) via CASE, so there is one query per resource rather than two that can drift. Admin deliberately does not widen the ownership path. Handlers refactored into shared private bodies (listNamespaces/listSources/listRegistries/listArtifacts) with the me-variants differing only in ownedFilterFromContext. Activity is a new ListOwnedActivity query (SBOM ingest stream over owned namespaces, keyset on created_at DESC,id DESC per ADR-043 rule 2) - no visibility twin to share. All five rows added to authRules with noteSelfScoped. Regenerated sqlc, openapi, auth matrix, pkg/client. Integration test seeds a second tenant with a PUBLIC namespace so the ownership/visibility difference is observable.

title: Owner-scoped variants of the admin-only feeds
description: This is the substance of 'real actionable views' - the queries mostly exist, the scoping does not. Today /api/v1/registries/drift-feed and /api/v1/registries/trust-summary both return 403 unless the caller is admin, and the scan-job and enrichment-job listings are similarly gated, so an ordinary namespace owner cannot see drift, signing posture, or ingest health for their own artifacts. Reuse the existing service queries and add the namespace filter rather than writing parallel ones. Declare the auth class for each new operation in ocidex-wp9b.2's conformance table.
acceptance_criteria: A non-admin namespace owner can retrieve drift, trust summary, and scan/enrichment job status for their own artifacts; admins still get the unscoped cross-tenant view; no query is duplicated - the owner-scoped path reuses the admin query plus a filter; integration tests prove a non-owner receives zero rows from each endpoint.

Files: db/queries/{scan_jobs,enrichment_jobs,provenance_drift,registry}.sql, internal/service/{job,enrichjob,registry,search,search_sbom}.go, internal/api/{jobs,enrichjobs,registry,router,authclass}.go, internal/repository/repository.go, tests/owner_scoped_feeds_test.go, docs/AUTH_MATRIX.md

Reachability: scan_jobs -> registry_id -> source.namespace_id; enrichment_jobs + provenance_drift_events -> sbom.namespace_id (NOT NULL since 00054); trust summary -> sbom.namespace_id inside latest_provenance CTE. Rows with a deleted registry/SBOM have no namespace and stay admin-only via the COALESCE(is_admin,false) arm. Threaded service.VisibilityFilter through JobService.List/Get, EnrichJobService.List/Summary, RegistryService.TrustSummary, SearchService.ListRecentProvenanceDrift; added VisibilityFilter.adminFlag() helper. Router: drift-feed and trust-summary moved adminMW -> authMW. authclass.go rows updated to ClassAuthenticated + noteNamespaceScoped; AUTH_MATRIX.md regenerated. jobService.CountByState (admin system-status) explicitly passes IsAdmin:true. GET /jobs/{id} now 404s cross-tenant. Wired real job services into tests/ setupServerWithStats so the feeds are exercisable. New integration tests: TestOwnerScopedFeedsExcludeNonOwners (owner sees rows, stranger 0, admin sees all, flipping ns public exposes them) and TestGetScanJobHidesOtherTenantsJob. Unit test TestTrustSummary_PassesVisibilityFilter pins filter threading. Full ./tests suite green (65s).

title: Leakage tests for the anonymous discovery surface
description: The discovery endpoint is the first surface deliberately built for unauthenticated viewers, so its visibility guarantee needs a dedicated test rather than relying on the SQL filter being right. docs/AUTH_MATRIX.md already flags the underlying risk: read endpoints have no handler gate to fall back on if the SQL filter has a bug. Add integration tests in tests/ that seed a private namespace alongside a public one and assert a private artifact appears in NO section of /api/v1/discover - not in rankings, not in recency, not in vulnerability blast-radius counts, and not as a contribution to any aggregate number - for an anonymous caller AND for an authenticated non-owner. Assert the counts themselves, not just the item lists, since an aggregate can leak the existence of private data without naming it.
acceptance_criteria: Integration test seeds public and private namespaces and asserts zero private leakage across every section and every aggregate count, for both anonymous and authenticated-non-owner callers; test fails if the public-only filter is removed from any of the ranking queries.
notes:
Files: tests/discover_visibility_test.go (new).

Approach: two integration tests against the real SQL, not the Go filter.

Fixtures are shaped so every section fails loudly if its filter is dropped:
- docker.io/discover-shared exists in BOTH namespaces (public v1.0 ingested
  first, private v2.0 second), so top_artifacts' versionCount/sbomCount are 1
  only while the filter holds, and recent_artifacts must resolve to the OLDER
  public SBOM rather than the newer private one.
- CVE-2030-0001 affects a public purl and a private purl, so its blast radius
  is 1 artifact / 1 SBOM only while the filter holds.
- MIT licenses one public and two private components, so its spread count is 1.
- discover-private / CVE-2030-0002 / GPL-3.0-only exist in private content
  alone and must be absent entirely — checked against the raw response body as
  well as the decoded one, so a leak into a field the test does not model still
  trips it.

Callers: anonymous, authenticated non-owner, and the private namespace's own
owner all get byte-identical bodies (the endpoint takes no viewer parameter).
Second test covers the degenerate all-private catalog: warm, not warming, and
every section empty.

Warms via setupServerWithStats' searchSvc.WarmDiscovery so the assertions read
the same cache the server serves; asserts warming=true before the warm.

Verified by mutation, not just by passing: replaced
visible_namespace_ids(NULL::uuid, false) with 'SELECT id FROM namespace' in
each of the four generated queries in turn (discover.sql.go lines 23/82/143/295)
— every one was caught. Working tree restored afterwards.

Gates: make check clean; full make test-integration green (tests 104.555s, 0
failures). This also closes the runtime-verification gap carried over from
ocidex-q1z7.1 — the four discovery queries had only been sqlc-type-checked
until now.
