title: GET /api/v1/discover with warmed aggregates
description: New endpoint returning the discovery payload: top artifacts, recently updated artifacts, notable vulnerabilities by blast radius, and license spread. These are expensive aggregates, so do NOT compute them per-request - route them through the existing internal/service/stats_cache.go and stats_warmer.go pattern, including the warming payload state that Home.tsx already knows how to render. Auth class is public, declared in ocidex-wp9b.2's conformance table. The anonymous response is byte-identical for every caller, so set cache headers that let it be cached at the edge; a signed-in caller gets the same public payload here, with personalisation handled separately in ocidex-998g.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/v1/discover returns the four sections; first call before warm-up returns the warming state rather than blocking; aggregates refresh on the warmer's schedule; response is cacheable and identical across anonymous callers; declared public in the auth conformance table; make openapi and make generate-client regenerated.
notes:
Files: internal/service/discover.go (new: Discovery DTOs, GetDiscovery/WarmDiscovery), internal/service/discover_test.go (new), internal/service/stats_cache.go (ttlCache generified to ttlCache[T]; newStatsCache shim), internal/service/search.go (interface + discoverCache field), internal/service/stats_warmer.go (+warmDiscovery in tick), internal/service/stats_warmer_test.go, internal/api/types_discover.go (new), internal/api/search.go (GetDiscovery handler), internal/api/router.go (registerDiscoverOps), internal/api/authclass.go, internal/api/search_test.go, regenerated docs/AUTH_MATRIX.md, web/openapi.json, web/src/types/openapi.d.ts, pkg/client/types.go.

Approach: single-slot TTL cache reusing the stats warmer. GetDiscovery returns Warming with empty sections on a miss rather than computing on the request path (dashboard contract, already rendered by Home.tsx). WarmDiscovery fans the four q1z7.1 queries out on an errgroup bounded by statsWarmConcurrency and writes the cache; StatsWarmer.tick calls it after the two visibility scopes, sequentially, so the overlap regression guard still covers it.

No viewer parameter anywhere on the path: the queries are public-scoped in SQL, so anonymous and authenticated callers get identical bytes. That is the cacheability precondition and it makes the no-private-data property structural. Cache-Control is set per response: 'public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300' when warm, 'no-store' while warming (an edge storing the warming payload would pin an empty landing page for the full max-age).

ttlCache generified so both payloads share one implementation; newStatsCache kept so stats_cache_test.go compiles unchanged.

Tests: warming-vs-cached service behaviour, Cache-Control per state, byte-identical response for anonymous vs bearer caller, warmer warms discovery on every pass. make check green (Go + frontend + helm).

title: Popularity ranking queries, scoped to public namespaces
description: There is no popularity signal anywhere in the system today - GetDashboardStats returns bare counts. Derive ranking from data already present rather than adding telemetry: ADR-041 usages counts, which say how many SBOMs contain a given artifact, plus version count and scan recency. Write the sqlc queries in db/queries/ constrained to PUBLIC namespaces through the existing visible_namespace_ids SQL function - private data must never contribute to an anonymous-visible aggregate, even indirectly through a count. Deliverables: top artifacts by usage, recently updated artifacts, vulnerabilities ranked by blast radius across public artifacts, and license spread. Keep the ranking formula in one place so it can be tuned without touching four queries.
acceptance_criteria: Queries return sensible rankings against seeded data via make seed; every query is constrained by visible_namespace_ids with the public-only filter; a private-namespace artifact contributes nothing to any returned count; make generate regenerates the repository layer.
notes:
Files: db/migrations/00060_discovery_score.sql (new), db/queries/discover.sql (new), internal/repository/discover.sql.go (sqlc-generated)
Approach: Four queries — GetDiscoverTopArtifacts, GetDiscoverRecentArtifacts, GetDiscoverTopVulnerabilities, GetDiscoverLicenseSpread. Public scope is expressed once, as namespace_id IN (SELECT visible_namespace_ids(NULL, false)); that call reduces to visibility='public' because the admin term is false and owner_id = NULL is never true, so the visibility rule keeps a single definition in the DB. No viewer parameter on any of them: identical response for every caller = edge-cacheable, and no code path by which private data widens an anonymous aggregate.
Ranking weights live in discovery_score(usage_count, version_count, last_activity), a STABLE SQL function, so tuning touches one place. Log-damped counts (usage is heavy-tailed; a linear term lets a few base images own every slot permanently), usage weighted 3:1 over version breadth, recency a bounded 0..2 bonus rather than a multiplier.
usage_count is the ADR-041 usages relation counted rather than listed, using the same coarse match (purl base via idx_component_purl_base, tuple fallback for purl-less rows). The Go componentKey() pass is skipped: the ranking is ordinal and a few qualifier variants cannot reorder a log-damped score. The two match branches are separate CTEs UNION ALLed, not one OR predicate — an OR across two relations cannot be planned as a hash join.
Vulnerability blast radius is two-stage: rank candidates from vuln_rollup (cheap, pre-aggregated), then compute the affected *artifact* count via the purl->component->sbom join only for the surviving candidates. Artifact count is the honest headline (an SBOM count double-counts every rescan) but is not worth a full component-table join to rank the whole catalog.
Verification gap: no Postgres or Docker is available in this environment, so the queries were validated by sqlc's parse and type-check against the migration catalog (make generate, make check green) but NOT executed against seeded data. Runtime execution and the private-namespace leakage assertions land in ocidex-q1z7.4.

Inside the workspace shell from ocidex-998g, add cluster registration and management, a running-workloads list per cluster, and the view that justifies the whole epic: vulnerabilities filtered to images that are ACTUALLY RUNNING, not the whole catalog. Reach through the digest join so each running workload links to its artifact, SBOM, and vuln summary. Distinguish three states clearly - workload matched to a known artifact, workload whose digest has no ingested SBOM, and workload whose image is unresolvable - because a silent gap here reads as a clean bill of health. Add query hooks in web/src/api/queries/clusters.ts following the existing pattern and build on the components/ui primitives from ocidex-wp9b.9.

title: cmd/k8s-agent: Pod watcher and inventory reporter
description: New binary that runs as a per-cluster Deployment. Watches Pods across all namespaces or a configured allowlist, reads running image digests from status.containerStatuses[].imageID, resolves each back to its owning workload kind and name via owner references, aggregates to a snapshot, and pushes it on an interval. Follow the existing worker conventions rather than inventing new ones: config via internal/config with caarlos0/env, ADR-027 structured lifecycle logging and the --once flag for a one-shot Job mode, graceful shutdown, and pkg/client for the HTTP call so it inherits the generated types. Note that imageID formats vary by runtime - containerd reports docker.io/library/nginx@sha256:... while some report a bare digest - so normalise before reporting, and cover the variants in tests.
acceptance_criteria: cmd/k8s-agent builds and runs both as a long-lived Deployment and with --once; digest normalisation handles the imageID formats seen across containerd and CRI-O; RBAC needs only pod read access; verified end to end against make dev-cluster-up with workloads visible in the API afterwards.
notes:
Files: cmd/k8s-agent/{main.go,inventory.go,inventory_test.go,main_test.go}, pkg/client/cluster.go + client.go/fake_client.go, internal/config/config.go (K8sAgentConfig/LoadK8sAgent) + config_test.go, docs/CONFIGURATION.md (k8s-agent section).

Approach: push-based agent modeled on cmd/vuln-worker (main->run, --once, JSON slog, health.New, SIGTERM). Config modeled on OperatorConfig (API-only; explicit non-empty validate because env's required tag passes on an empty secretKeyRef). Kube config via controller-runtime GetConfig so in-cluster and kubeconfig both work; pods listed paged (limit 500) across all namespaces or an OCIDEX_NAMESPACES allowlist, a failed namespace warns rather than failing the whole snapshot.

normalizeImageID covers the full K3 table; the rule 'a scheme with no @ is a local image ID' makes docker://sha256:... unresolvable (it can never equal sbom.digest, so accepting it would look like a coverage gap and point at the wrong remedy). Ownership resolved from the pod alone (pod-template-hash strips the ReplicaSet suffix exactly) so RBAC is pods read-only; Node-owned static pods report as kind Pod, since kind Node would merge every control-plane component on a node into one workload named after the machine. Aggregation key = (k8s ns, kind, name, container, digest) matching 00059's natural key, so a rollout's two digests stay separate rows. Non-Running pods excluded (current state, not history); rows with no digest are reported, never dropped.

Verified end to end against the local Talos dev cluster (docker-started nodes, migrations up to 59, API run from source on :8099, namespace+cluster registered via API): 19 pods -> 17 workloads with correct Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet/Pod kinds and pod_count 2 for the 2-replica DaemonSets; OCIDEX_NAMESPACES=kube-system then pruned the 13 omitted rows. Long mode reported on its 8s interval, /healthz and /readyz 200, clean SIGTERM; --once exited 0. make check green.

title: Cluster CRUD and inventory ingest endpoint
description: Add cluster registration endpoints alongside the existing namespace and source resources in internal/api, plus POST /api/v1/clusters/{id}/inventory taking a full snapshot of running images. Authenticated by API key. An open decision this story must settle: the current scopes are read and read-write, and an agent needs write access to inventory but should not be able to delete SBOMs or registries - decide whether that warrants a third scope or a per-resource restriction, and record the answer. Epic ocidex-wp9b.2's conformance test forces the auth class to be declared explicitly, so the decision cannot be left implicit. Snapshot handling is a transactional replace: upsert reported workloads, prune rows for that cluster absent from the snapshot, stamp last_seen_at on the cluster.
acceptance_criteria: Cluster CRUD follows the existing namespace and source handler patterns and uses visibilityFilterFromContext; POST inventory replaces the cluster's workload set transactionally; scope decision recorded in the ADR and reflected in the auth conformance table; integration test proves a non-owner API key is rejected and that a second snapshot prunes disappeared workloads.
notes:
Files: internal/service/cluster.go, internal/api/cluster.go, internal/api/types_cluster.go, internal/api/router.go (registerClusterOps), internal/api/authclass.go, internal/api/handler.go (+clusterService), internal/repository/repository.go (ClusterRepository), tests/cluster_api_test.go; regenerated docs/AUTH_MATRIX.md, web/openapi.json, web/src/types/openapi.d.ts, pkg/client/types.go.

Approach: ClusterService mirrors SourceService but also holds the pool, because ReplaceInventory needs its own transaction: it re-reads the cluster inside the tx, stamps every upsert with one observed_at, prunes last_seen_at < observed_at, then TouchClusterLastSeen — so a partially-applied snapshot is never visible and an out-of-order older snapshot cannot clobber a newer one. last_seen_at is stamped even for an empty snapshot (ADR-044 K2).

Authz: reads are ClassAuthenticated gated on namespace visibility (404 not 403, so a private cluster's existence is not confirmed); every mutation INCLUDING put-cluster-inventory is ClassOwner via clusterOwnerCheck -> namespaceOwnerCheck. Ownership rather than visibility is deliberate: a public namespace must not make inventory writable. Per ADR-044 K8 the read-write scope is reused; that breadth is stated in authclass.go Notes and narrowing is deferred to ocidex-wp9b.2.

Coverage counts ship inside ListClusterWorkloadsOutput.Body rather than on a separate endpoint, so a client cannot report vuln figures without the unmatched counts (K5).

Testing: tests/cluster_api_test.go drives it over HTTP — non-owner 403, anonymous 401, owner's READ-scoped key 403, no rejected push leaves a row, second snapshot prunes the omitted workload while updating pod_count in place, empty snapshot prunes all and still stamps last_seen_at, non-owner can still read a public cluster, PATCH/DELETE by non-owner 403. Full ./tests suite green.

Incidental fix: both migration round-trip tests now use goose.DownTo(version-1). A bare goose.Down rolls back whichever migration is last, so adding 00059 turned TestArtifactWatchMigrationRollsBack into an assertion about cluster tables (it failed true != false). Pinned versions survive future migrations.

title: Schema: cluster and cluster_workload tables
description: New goose migration in db/migrations/ adding a cluster table (id, namespace_id owner, name, description, last_seen_at) and a cluster_workload table recording what a cluster reported: cluster_id, k8s namespace, workload kind and name, container name, image reference, image digest, replica or pod count, first_seen_at, last_seen_at. cluster is owned by a namespace so it inherits the ADR-039 visibility model rather than inventing a second one - visible_namespace_ids must gate it exactly like sources and registries. Snapshots are full replacements per cluster, so the write path is a transactional upsert plus prune of rows not present in the snapshot. Add sqlc queries in db/queries/ and run make generate; do not hand-edit internal/repository/*.sql.go.
acceptance_criteria: Migration applies and rolls back cleanly via make migrate-up and make migrate-down; cluster rows are owned by a namespace and filtered by visible_namespace_ids; a digest join from cluster_workload to artifact returns the expected artifact for a seeded SBOM; sqlc output regenerated via make generate.
notes:
Files: db/migrations/00059_cluster_workload.sql, db/queries/cluster.sql, internal/repository/cluster.sql.go + models.go (sqlc-generated), tests/cluster_inventory_test.go, docs/adr/0044 (amended K4), CLAUDE.md.

Approach: cluster (namespace_id owner, name, description, last_seen_at) + cluster_workload (cluster_id, k8s_namespace, workload_kind/name, container_name, image_ref, image_digest, pod_count, first/last_seen_at). No visibility column on cluster — inherited from namespace via visible_namespace_ids, same as source (ADR-039).

Found and fixed a real defect in the ADR's join rule while implementing: containerd records the IMAGE INDEX digest in imageID for multi-arch images pulled by tag, while the scanner stores the per-platform child digest in sbom.digest and the index in sbom.index_digest. A strict sbom.digest join would have missed the majority of real workloads. Amended ADR-044 K4 with a two-tier join (exact -> index) plus a new idx_sbom_index_digest, and the tier is returned rather than hidden.

Made match_state a NOT NULL 4-valued column ('exact'|'index'|'unknown'|'unresolvable') rather than a nullable match_tier: a NULL is trivially ignored, and the one thing this feature must never do is let an unmatched workload render like a matched-and-clean one (ADR-044 K5). Added GetClusterWorkloadCoverage so a vuln count can never be reported without its unmatched counts.

Natural key includes image_digest with NULLS NOT DISTINCT (PG15+, deployment is 18.4): during a rollout one container legitimately runs two digests and collapsing them hides the half still vulnerable; without NULLS NOT DISTINCT every unresolvable row would accumulate a duplicate per snapshot. Prune is last_seen_at < observed_at (strict, so a concurrent newer snapshot is not clobbered by an older one committing).

No artifact_id/sbom_id column on cluster_workload deliberately — storing a resolved match would freeze it at snapshot time, leaving a workload 'unknown' forever after its SBOM was finally ingested.

Verified: 4 integration tests pass against testcontainers Postgres (migration up/down/up round-trip, four-state digest join incl. index tier, snapshot upsert+prune+first_seen_at preservation+rollout two-row case, visibility for owner/outsider/anon/admin/owned_only). make check clean. NOTE: docker IS available in this env despite CLAUDE.md saying otherwise.

title: ADR: standalone push-based K8s inventory agent
description: Record the connector decision and its rejected alternatives before any code. Chosen: a standalone push-based reporting agent, decoupled from cmd/operator, so it runs in clusters that do not want CRDs installed. Rejected: extending the existing operator with a Pod-watching controller, which couples inventory to CRD adoption; and pull-via-kubeconfig, which requires OCIDex to reach every cluster API server and to store cluster credentials. The ADR must also state the join rule and why it is cheap: running image digests from status.containerStatuses[].imageID join to artifact BY DIGEST, and ADR-040 guarantees sbom.digest is UNIQUE, so the match is exact rather than heuristic. Note the known limitation - a running digest with no ingested SBOM is an unknown workload, and the UI must distinguish that from a clean one.
acceptance_criteria: ADR merged in docs/adr/ with Context, Decision, Consequences, and explicit rejected alternatives; digest join rule and its ADR-040 dependency stated; unknown-workload semantics defined; ADR number added to the CLAUDE.md ADR summary table.
notes:
Files: docs/adr/0044-k8s-inventory-agent.md, CLAUDE.md (ADR summary row 044).
Approach: Recorded the connector shape as ADR-044 with 8 normative rules (K1-K8). Chose standalone push-based cmd/k8s-agent; rejected operator Pod-watching controller (couples inventory to CRD adoption, conflates ingest config with runtime state) and pull-via-kubeconfig (needs reachability to every API server, makes OCIDex a cluster-credential store). K3 tabulates the four imageID formats and their normalization, including the unresolvable docker:// image-ID form. K4 states the digest join rule and its ADR-040 UNIQUE dependency explicitly. K5 defines three workload states (matched / unknown / unresolvable) and makes visual distinction normative, since an unmatched digest reading as clean is the feature's worst failure mode. K6 reuses namespace ownership + visible_namespace_ids per ADR-039. K7 makes snapshots full transactional replacements (upsert + prune). K8 settles zeta.3's open scope question: reuse read-write + ClassOwner, defer per-resource scopes to ocidex-wp9b.2, with the interim exposure stated plainly. Non-goals recorded: ClusterInventory CRD, historical retention, fuzzy matching, non-Pod sources.

title: Decompose the largest frontend pages and grow components/ui
description: The frontend god-file problem is worse than the backend's: SourcesTab.tsx 47K, ComponentOverview.tsx 26K, SBOMDetail/index.tsx 24K, VulnerabilityDetail.tsx 23K, admin/JobsTab.tsx 21K, SBOMDetail/PackagesTab.tsx 21K - against a web/src/components/ui holding only four primitives (Badge, SigningBadge, Tooltip, TypeBadge). Split those six files and promote the patterns they repeat (forms, modals, tab shells, empty and error states) into components/ui, following ADR-023 visual identity and ADR-036 cell-renderer conventions. This is the prerequisite that keeps epics B, C and D from adding three more 20K-line pages - all three ship substantial new UI.
acceptance_criteria: No page or tab component exceeds roughly 400 lines; repeated form/modal/tab-shell/empty-state patterns live in components/ui with tests; existing Vitest suites still pass; make frontend-lint-fix then make frontend-lint clean; no visual regression against ADR-023.
notes:
Files: web/src/components/ui/{Card,DetailGrid,TabBar,FormField,Modal,QueryBoundary,expanded,index} + Card/TabBar/QueryBoundary tests; web/src/components/diffTreeModel.ts (+test); web/src/pages/admin/jobs/*; web/src/pages/admin/sources/*; web/src/pages/ComponentOverview/*; web/src/pages/ArtifactDetail/ArtifactHeader.tsx; web/src/pages/SBOMDetail/{DependencyTreeView,componentHref}.
Approach: pure-refactor split of every >400-line frontend file into focused modules, plus a components/ui layer for the card/detail-grid/tab-bar/form-field/modal/query-boundary markup that was duplicated across pages. DiffTreeView's traversal was lifted into a pure diffTreeModel module so the ADR-0021 contract (backend roots verbatim, file-typed nodes dropped, nodeRef change join, orphan changes, context/transitive gating, ancestry-scoped cycle guard) is unit-testable without mounting. DetailField's 'when' guard uses "when" in props so an explicitly-passed undefined hides the field. Kept JobsTab's pipeline switcher on btn/aria-pressed rather than TabBar to avoid a visual change. Gates: 28 test files / 214 tests green, frontend-lint clean (2 pre-existing warnings), make check green.

title: Namespace and source frontend parity (ADR-039 follow-through)
description: ADR-039 landed backend-only. Namespaces have migrations, internal/service/namespace.go, six API endpoints in router.go, and a Go SDK at pkg/client/namespace.go - but ZERO frontend. There is no query hook, no page, and no admin tab; the only web/src hits for 'namespace' are the generated openapi.d.ts and purl.ts. The entity that now owns every artifact and governs visibility is invisible to users, which directly blocks the user-workspace epic. Add web/src/api/queries/namespaces.ts following the existing useX hook pattern and export it from queries/index.ts, then build a namespace management surface (admin tab plus the ownership affordances the workspace epic will build on). Also surface each source's owning namespace in SourcesTab.tsx, which currently references namespaces only incidentally.
acceptance_criteria: web/src/api/queries/namespaces.ts exists and is exported from queries/index.ts; a user can list, create, rename, change visibility of, and delete namespaces from the UI; SourcesTab shows each source's owning namespace; Vitest coverage for the new surface; make frontend-lint clean.
notes:
Files: web/src/api/queries/namespaces.ts (+ index.ts export), web/src/api/client.ts (Namespace type), web/src/pages/admin/NamespacesTab.tsx (+test), web/src/pages/Admin.tsx (TABS table), web/src/App.tsx (/admin/namespaces route), web/src/pages/admin/SourcesTab.tsx, web/src/pages/admin/sources/NamespaceGroups.tsx, web/src/pages/admin/SourcesTab.test.tsx.
Approach: added the five namespace hooks following the existing useX pattern (delete also invalidates sources/registries/artifacts, since it removes everything ingested under the namespace). New admin tab at /admin/namespaces lists name/visibility/owner/source-count/created with inline rename+visibility edit (two mutable fields do not justify a dialog) and a delete confirm that names how many sources go with it. SourcesTab passes the namespace list into NamespaceGroups so each heading carries a visibility badge, the owner, and a link to the new tab; a namespace the caller cannot read falls back to the plain heading. Admin.tsx's five duplicated nav blocks became a TABS array, keeping the /admin/registries legacy path. Gates: 29 files / 222 tests green, frontend-lint clean (2 pre-existing warnings), make check green.

title: Authz conformance test and generated AUTH_MATRIX.md
description: docs/AUTH_MATRIX.md is dated 2026-04-24 and stale: it omits namespaces, sources, vulns, jobs, enrichment-jobs, lookup, diff-tree, and the artifact usages/contains/versions/drift/vuln-summary endpoints, and still describes SBOM ownership as 'via registry_id' when the code resolves GetSBOMNamespaceID (post-ADR-039). A hand-maintained security matrix that drifts is worse than none. Build a table in internal/api declaring the intended auth class for every operation ID (public | authenticated | member | admin | owner | secret). A test walks the registered huma OpenAPI operations and FAILS on any operation missing a declaration, so a new endpoint cannot ship without an explicit auth decision. Generate docs/AUTH_MATRIX.md from that same table via make openapi or a sibling target. This is the highest-value item in the epic: it converts a convention into a build failure, and it is what stops epics B, C and D reintroducing the inline-check pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Every registered operation has a declared auth class; the test fails when a declaration is deleted or a new unclassified operation is added; AUTH_MATRIX.md is generated and its regeneration is wired into a make target; the generated matrix reflects the post-ADR-039 namespace-based ownership.
notes:
Files: internal/api/authclass.go (new, authRules table + AuthClass + markdown renderer), internal/api/authclass_test.go (new, 5 conformance tests), cmd/authmatrix/main.go (new), docs/AUTH_MATRIX.md (now generated), Makefile (auth-matrix + auth-matrix-check, wired into check), internal/api/router.go (authMW on 8 read ops).
Approach: one declarative table keyed by huma operation ID, joined against the live OpenAPI spec. Coverage test catches undeclared operations and orphaned declarations in both directions; three behavioural tests probe the running router (anonymous->401 for every non-public class, viewer->403 for member class, member->403 for admin class) so a declaration nobody enforces fails the build. Write scope asserted as an iff against HTTP method. Conformance router wires a non-nil registry service on purpose: RequireRegistryOwner degrades to a pass-through when its service is nil, so nil-service wiring would have made owner-class enforcement untested. Mutation-verified: removing memberMW from list-api-keys and adminMW from list-recent-drift both go red. Known limit documented in the test file: TestAuthClassEnforced cannot tell a middleware 401 from a handler's defensive UserFromContext 401, because handlers that build a VisibilityFilter keep that check deliberately.

title: Add declarative RequireAdmin and RequireWrite huma middlewares
description: Authorization is currently enforced three ways, and the safest is the least used. Global OptionalAuthenticate (router.go:72) never blocks. On top of it sit huma middlewares (RequireMember, RequireSBOMOwner, RequireArtifactOwner, RequireRegistryOwner) declared in router.go, ~8 inline huma.Error403Forbidden('admin only') sites, and ~10 inline 'read-only API key cannot perform write operations' sites across auth.go, jobs.go, enrichjobs.go, registry.go and namespace.go. Every admin-only operation in router.go (get-registry-trust-summary, list-recent-drift, all four retry-*) carries NO middleware - 'Admin-only' exists only in the OpenAPI Description string. Add RequireAdmin(api) and RequireWrite(api) beside the existing middlewares in internal/api/middleware.go, reusing isWriteAllowed (middleware.go:25) and the roleAdmin const, then replace every inline check with a Middlewares: entry on the corresponding huma.Register call. Leave the ownership middlewares alone - they need the path param, so middleware is already the right home.
acceptance_criteria: RequireAdmin and RequireWrite exist in internal/api/middleware.go; zero inline 'admin only' or 'read-only API key' Error403Forbidden calls remain in handler bodies; every previously-admin-only operation declares its middleware in router.go; existing api tests pass unchanged.
notes:
Files: internal/api/middleware.go (new RequireAuthenticated/RequireAdmin/RequireWrite), internal/api/router.go + auth.go (registerAuthOps) declare Middlewares on every op, handlers stripped: auth.go jobs.go enrichjobs.go registry.go sbom.go source.go namespace.go.
Approach: two orthogonal middleware dimensions — auth class (RequireAuthenticated | RequireMember | RequireAdmin | Require*Owner) and key scope (RequireWrite). Mutating ops declare one of each, auth-class first so unauthenticated gets 401 before the 403 scope check. Removed requireAdminWrite helper from enrichjobs.go and all ~18 inline Error403Forbidden sites plus the now-redundant inline 401 checks on job listing handlers. Handlers that still need the principal (CreateAPIKey, CreateRegistry, source/namespace owner checks) keep 'user, ok := UserFromContext' for the ID, not for policy. Added descAdminOnly const to satisfy goconst. make openapi regenerated (Description strings changed). make check clean.

title: Foundation: authorization contract, ADR-039 parity, decomposition
description: Strengthen the base before the next-phase feature epics. Audit found the core sound (layered architecture respected, sqlc/huma/oapi-codegen chain drift-guarded, prod per-function complexity under limit, uniform frontend query layer) but three real problems: (1) authorization enforced three different ways - huma middlewares, ~18 inline handler 403 checks, and SQL-only VisibilityFilter - with every admin-only op in router.go carrying no middleware at all; (2) ADR-039 namespace/source split landed backend-only, with zero frontend and zero CLI coverage; (3) god files (api/types.go 1295 lines, service/changelog.go 1321, SourcesTab.tsx 47K) against a components/ui holding only four primitives. tokensave quality signal 7478, equality dimension 0.39 (gini 0.605). Landing this epic first is what makes epics B-E cheap: its authz conformance test is what stops each of them reintroducing the inline-check pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Authorization is declared in router.go, not hand-written in handlers; a conformance test fails on any operation without an explicit auth class; AUTH_MATRIX.md is generated, not hand-maintained; namespaces and sources are manageable from both the web UI and the CLI; the six largest frontend files and three largest Go files are decomposed; make check, make test-integration, make openapi and make generate-client all clean.

title: Catalog walk ignores tags/list pagination — repos with >100 tags scan nothing
description:
internal/scanner/catalog.go ociListTags issues a single GET /v2/<repo>/tags/list and returns result.Tags, ignoring the OCI Distribution 'Link: rel=next' header. Both ghcr.io and quay.io paginate: ghcr defaults to 100 tags/page (honours ?n= up to 1000), quay caps at 100/page regardless of n. Tags come back oldest-first, so for any long-lived repo the only tags ocidex ever sees are ancient ones.

Discovered during ocidex-8wun end-to-end seed verification: every one of the 6 seeded registries reported 'queued: 0'. ghcr.io/dexidp/dex returns 100 tags on page 1 (v2.26.0..v2.31.x) plus a next link; the seeded filter v2.45.? matches 0 of them, while the repo does have v2.45.0 and v2.45.1. No error is logged — an empty-after-filter walk is indistinguishable from a correctly-empty one.

Fix: follow Link rel=next until exhausted (bounded page cap), request ?n=1000 on the first page.
acceptance_criteria: ociListTags follows Link rel=next across pages with a bounded page cap; unit test with a fake paginating registry; WalkRegistry against ghcr.io/dexidp/dex with tag filter v2.45.? queues 2 images
notes:
Files: internal/scanner/catalog.go (ociListTags, ociListCatalog -> new ociListPaged + nextTagPageURL), internal/scanner/walk_test.go (paginateTags fake, TestWalkRegistry_PaginatedTags, TestOCIListTags_PageCap)

Approach: both list endpoints now follow the OCI 'Link: <...>; rel=next' header through a shared ociListPaged helper, request n=1000 on the first page (ghcr honours it, quay caps at 100 regardless), and stop after maxTagPages=50 so a registry that pages forever cannot loop.

Root cause: a single GET returned page 1 only. Registries return tags oldest-first, so for ghcr.io/dexidp/dex page 1 is v2.26.0..v2.31.x and the seed filter v2.45.? matched nothing. The walk logged 'queued: 0' with no error, so a truncated walk was indistinguishable from a correctly-empty one — which is why this survived the ocidex-y19y stub-API testing.

Verified live before/after with a throwaway main() calling WalkRegistry: dex v2.45.? went 0 -> 10 submissions (2 tags x 5 arches), quay metallb/controller v0.15.? -> 20. Then end-to-end via make seed: 7 artifacts, 65 SBOMs, keycloak at 7 distinct versions.

title: Scanner-worker cannot scan: readOnlyRootFilesystem blocks syft/stereoscope tmp dirs
description:
Every image scan in ocidex-dev has failed since 2026-08-08 with:

  scan: getting source for ghcr.io/...: oci-registry: mkdir /tmp/stereoscope-2275016733: read-only file system

syft/stereoscope unpacks image layers into a temp dir under /tmp. The chart-wide securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem=true shipped by ocidex-1d9 makes that impossible, and there is no emptyDir mounted over /tmp for the scanner-worker.

Impact is total, not partial. scan_jobs by day on ocidex-dev:

  2026-08-14  failed 1401
  2026-08-13  failed   89
  2026-08-12  failed   79
  2026-08-11  failed   65
  2026-08-09  failed   20
  2026-08-08  succeeded 81   <- last successful scan
  2026-08-07  succeeded 83

Zero successful scans in six days. Each job burns its full 3-attempt retry budget before landing in failed, which is why the daily count climbs.

Found incidentally while verifying ocidex-s3tu: a replayed scan of a previously-succeeding image (ghcr.io/pfenerty/apko-cicd/rust) failed three times in 600ms with the mkdir error. Unrelated to the NATS change — the scanner-worker pod spec was untouched.

ocidex-1d9 verified readOnlyRootFilesystem against the operator and nginx, but nothing exercised a real scan, so this shipped green.
design:
Follow the nginx precedent already in the chart: deployment-web.yaml mounts emptyDirs over the paths nginx must write, gated on readOnlyRootFilesystem so disabling the setting leaves no stray volumes. Do the same for /tmp on deployment-scanner-worker.yaml.

Audit the other workers rather than assuming scanner-worker is alone — git-worker clones repositories and the provenance worker invokes cosign, both of which are likely to want writable temp space. The enrichment path has been succeeding (17731 rows), so check before changing anything.

Consider sizeMemoryBackedVolumes or an explicit sizeLimit: layer unpacking of a large image into a memory-backed emptyDir could otherwise pressure the node.

Also worth deciding whether TMPDIR should be set explicitly rather than relying on /tmp.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A scan of a previously-succeeding image completes and produces an SBOM.
2. Verified against a real scan on the cluster, not just a render or a dry-run.
3. The other worker deployments are audited for the same class of failure and fixed or explicitly cleared.
4. scan_jobs stops accumulating failed rows in ocidex-dev.
notes:
Files: charts/ocidex/templates/deployment-scanner-worker.yaml, charts/ocidex/values.yaml, internal/enrichment/provenance/keyless.go

Approach: emptyDir over /tmp on scanner-worker, gated on securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem so disabling the setting leaves no stray volume (nginx precedent, deployment-web.yaml). Node-disk backed rather than medium: Memory — a multi-GB image unpacked into the 1536Mi container limit would OOM-kill the worker. New value scannerWorker.tmpSizeLimit=5Gi bounds node ephemeral storage; exceeding it evicts the pod instead of filling the node. No TMPDIR env var: stereoscope's os.MkdirTemp("", ...) already resolves to /tmp.

Audit (criterion 3): scanner-worker broken; provenance-worker latent — keyless.go fetched the sigstore trusted root via tuf.DefaultOptions(), which caches to $HOME/.sigstore/root or os.TempDir(), both read-only; fixed with WithDisableLocalCache (sigstore-go's documented read-only mode; the in-process trustedRootCache already made the disk cache near-worthless). Cleared: git-worker (GitHub REST only), oci-metadata-worker, user-enricher-worker (HTTP only), vuln-worker (streams OSV JSON, no tempfile), api (Reverifier only requeues DB rows). syft's own cache defaults to bypassedCache, so /tmp was the only path needed.

Verification (criteria 1, 2): ocidex-dev is a Flux-managed namespace on rpi-cluster, not the local Talos cluster. Patched the live scanner-worker Deployment with this exact volume/mount, triggered a walk via a ScanRequest CR. Result: 0 read-only errors (previously 100% of scans), and sbom sha256:96828ed4d69e30a2b16343d03a83c9e49566667f11c6720b05959e3c621e8992 created 15:37:06 from an end-to-end scan — first successful scan since 2026-08-08. Live patch and test ScanRequest reverted/deleted afterwards.

Criterion 4 partially: read-only failures are gone, but scan_jobs still accumulates failed rows from a distinct bug this fix unmasked — cosign .sig artifacts queued as scannable images (47 failures in 10 min). Filed as ocidex-ptj2. The gsip-class failure no longer contributes.

Note: the rust image named in the report (sha256:e774b63f...) already had an SBOM from 2026-08-08, so re-scanning it dedupes on sbom.digest UNIQUE and produces no new row — which is why the new-digest ingest above is the proof, not that image.

title: sbom-push runs a permanently stale ocidex-cli image and reports green while every upload fails
description:
sbom-push push steps fail with 'error: unknown flag: --version-file' while the TaskRun reports Succeeded.

Root cause: the steps run ghcr.io/pfenerty/ocidex-cli:main with no imagePullPolicy. Kubernetes defaults to IfNotPresent for any tag other than :latest, so the kubelet reuses the node-cached layer and never re-pulls the mutable :main tag. Proof from run ocidex-ocidex-push-9cl9q (18:11Z, sha a74d0ae): the pod ran sha256:6b4df8c7 = sha-12b11d22, a build that predates the flag, while :main in GHCR already pointed at sha256:fece8687 = sha-305ded74 (pushed 15:58Z by run hj58f, image-build-cli Succeeded). The 'self-heals on the second post-merge run' premise recorded in ocidex-2u7y and in spec.ts:13-31 is therefore false - it never self-heals on that node.

Second bug: onError: continue on every push step plus reportOnlyStatusReporter (failOnError: false) means nine steps exiting 2 still produce a green TaskRun. SBOM uploads have been a silent no-op since 549035b.

Fix: run the .sbom-bins/ocidex-cli that build-binaries already compiles from the current commit, instead of the published image. CLI and args then always come from the same commit, removing both the stale-pull bug and the 'new flag costs one degraded run' hazard. Collapse the nine distroless steps back into one shell step that loops, restoring the API-key skip and the 'N of M uploads failed' summary that ocidex-2u7y lost.
notes:
Files: .tektonic/jobs/sbom-push/spec.ts, .tektonic/jobs/sbom-push/push-sboms.nu (restored from 549035b^ and amended), .tekton/tasks/sbom-push.k8s.yaml (synth).

Approach: reverted the image half of ocidex-2u7y. The nine distroless push steps on ghcr.io/pfenerty/ocidex-cli:main are replaced by one push-sboms step on goImage running .sbom-bins/ocidex-cli — the binary build-binaries already compiles from the current commit, since ocidex-cli stays in shippedBinaries as its own SBOM subject. CLI and args now always come from the same commit, so neither the IfNotPresent stale-pull nor flag skew can recur. tektonic's TaskStepSpec has no imagePullPolicy field, and a pinned digest would need a bump on every CLI change, so neither was viable.

Kept --version-file/--arch-file rather than deriving version inline: already implemented and unit-tested, and the CLI errors on a missing/blank file instead of pushing a versionless SBOM. No Go changes.

Silent-green fix: the script raises via 'error make' (never 'exit 1' — ocidex-es6) on a genuine upload failure. reportOnlyStatusReporter is failOnError:false, so this reddens only the sbom-push check and cannot gate a release. Restores the API-key skip and the 'N of M uploads failed' summary that ocidex-2u7y lost, and drops held CPU requests from nine steps to one.

Verified by ad-hoc TaskRun in ocidex-ci (with podTemplate securityContext):
- test-sbom-push-bb6zh: push-sboms exit=0, 'OK: all 9 SBOMs pushed', real SBOM UUIDs returned by the dev API.
- test-sbom-fail-px2jh (OCIDEX_URL pointed at an invalid host): push-sboms exit=1, summary '9 of 9 uploads failed', report-status logged exit-code=1 state=failure and posted a GitHub failure status, while the TaskRun still reported Succeeded — the report-only contract intact with the failure now visible. Under the old code this same condition reported exit=0.

Side effect: the fail-test left sbom-push=failure as the newest commit status on a74d0ae. The truthful state is success (posted 22:42:28 by the passing run).

title: fix(ci): go-integration-test postgres sidecar blocked by kubelet non-root policy
description:
Push pipelines ocidex-ocidex-push-9wchq and -htxpt both failed with go-integration-test as the only failed task (CreateContainerConfigError), skipping 11 downstream tasks.

Root cause: tektonic stamps runAsNonRoot: true onto every PipelineRun podTemplate.securityContext (see .tekton/ocidex-ocidex-push.k8s.yaml:478), merged over defaultPodSecurityContext in .tektonic/pipeline.ts:120-124. The postgres sidecar sets runAsUser: 0 (.tektonic/jobs/go-integration/spec.ts) but not runAsNonRoot, so it inherits true and the kubelet rejects it: "container's runAsUser breaks non-root policy". The existing code comment reasons this is fine because ocidex-ci is a PSA privileged namespace — true but irrelevant; the kubelet runAsNonRoot check is independent of Pod Security Admission.

Introduced by ocidex-113l, which was verified with ad-hoc TaskRuns. A bare TaskRun carries no podTemplate, so root sidecars start fine there and only fail under a real PipelineRun.
acceptance_criteria: postgres sidecar reaches running state under a PipelineRun-equivalent podTemplate; go-integration-test passes 32/32 with zero SKIPs; CLAUDE.md ad-hoc TaskRun template includes the podTemplate securityContext.
notes:
Files: .tektonic/jobs/go-integration/spec.ts (postgres sidecar securityContext); .tekton/tasks/go-integration-test.k8s.yaml (regenerated, +1 line); CLAUDE.md (ad-hoc TaskRun template + 2 gotcha rows).

Root cause: tektonic stamps runAsNonRoot: true onto every PipelineRun podTemplate.securityContext, merged over defaultPodSecurityContext (.tektonic/pipeline.ts:120-124). The postgres sidecar set runAsUser: 0 but not runAsNonRoot, so it inherited true and the kubelet refused the container (CreateContainerConfigError, 'container's runAsUser breaks non-root policy'). The kubelet runAsNonRoot check is independent of Pod Security Admission, so the existing comment's reasoning ('ocidex-ci is PSA privileged') did not apply.

Fix: securityContext: { runAsUser: 0, runAsNonRoot: false } — container-level false overrides the pod-level true. Only postgres needs it; the nats sidecar runs fine as uid 1024 with JetStream state in /tmp.

Why CI never caught it (ocidex-113l was 'verified in-cluster'): a bare ad-hoc TaskRun carries no podTemplate, so root sidecars start fine there and the constraint only exists under a real PipelineRun. Closed that gap by adding the podTemplate securityContext block to the CLAUDE.md ad-hoc TaskRun recipe, plus gotcha-table rows for both the kubelet error and the ad-hoc/pipeline divergence. Also corrected 'kubectl apply' -> 'kubectl create' in that recipe (apply rejects generateName).

Verified: ad-hoc TaskRun WITH the podTemplate block — sidecar-postgres reached running (previously CreateContainerConfigError), suite PASS, ok github.com/pfenerty/ocidex/tests 60.600s, zero SKIPs, TaskRun Succeeded. report-status was pointed at a non-existent repo so the run wrote no GitHub commit status.

title: Non-container artifacts are invisible: sufficiency gate is container-only
description:
GET /api/v1/artifacts defaults to require_sufficient=true (internal/api/search.go:317, 'requireSufficient := input.Sufficient != "false"'). sbom.enrichment_sufficient is only ever set true by Dispatcher.applyEnrichmentSufficiency (internal/enrichment/dispatcher.go:203), which runs for the oci-metadata and user enrichers and requires BOTH imageVersion and architecture to be non-empty.

architecture is an OCI image concept. An uploaded binary/library SBOM has no image to read it from, so enrichment_sufficient stays false forever and the artifact never appears in the default list. Every non-container artifact is structurally invisible.

Verified against ocidex-dev on 2026-08-06:
- artifact table: 38 container, 9 application
- namespace 'ocidex' is PUBLIC, so artifact_visible() is not the cause
- sbom rows: application 45/45 enrichment_sufficient=f; container 4062 t / 77 f
- the 9 application SBOMs DO have subject_version (e.g. 0.0.0-f5e9dd9e) and user:success enrichment — only architecture is missing
- GET /api/v1/artifacts?limit=100            -> 37 container, 0 application
- GET /api/v1/artifacts?limit=100&sufficient=false -> 38 container, 9 application

This predates ocidex-rj4; rj4's type-aware UI is correct but has nothing to render.
design:
Sufficiency was defined when every artifact was an image. It needs to be evaluated per artifact type: for a non-container, caller-declared identity (ADR-040) plus a subject version is the equivalent of 'we know what this is'. Requiring architecture of a library or source artifact is asking for a field that does not exist.

Existing rows need a backfill; re-enrichment alone will not clear them if the rule stays unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
- a non-container artifact with a declared subject version appears in GET /api/v1/artifacts with no sufficient= parameter
- the 45 existing application SBOMs in ocidex-dev are corrected by migration, not by manual SQL
- container sufficiency semantics are unchanged (imageVersion + architecture)
- dispatcher unit tests cover the non-container path
notes:
Files (part 1, b4e5574): internal/enrichment/dispatcher.go (requiresArchitecture + type-aware applyEnrichmentSufficiency), internal/enrichment/dispatcher_test.go, db/migrations/00056_non_container_sufficiency.sql.
Files (part 2, da2ce45): cmd/ocidex-cli/sbom.go (--arch flag), cmd/ocidex-cli/sbom_test.go, .tektonic/jobs/sbom-push/{spec.ts,push-sboms.nu}, .tekton/tasks/sbom-push.k8s.yaml.

Approach: root cause was GET /api/v1/artifacts defaulting require_sufficient=true while enrichment_sufficient was only set when enrichment JSON carried BOTH imageVersion and architecture. Architecture is an OCI image concept, so every ADR-040 non-container upload was permanently invisible. Proved against ocidex-dev: /artifacts returned 37 containers, /artifacts?sufficient=false returned 38 containers + 9 applications; the user-enricher payload for those SBOMs was exactly {"imageVersion":"0.0.0-286f2524"}.

Fix 1 (correctness): architecture is required only for type container or empty (empty = pre-ADR-040 rows, all of which were images; defaulting the other way would promote half-enriched images). Migration 00056 backfills the already-stranded rows, keyed on subject_version rather than the enrichment payload; dry-run of the Up predicate against ocidex-dev matched exactly the 45 stranded SBOMs.

Fix 2 (data completeness): ocidex-cli sbom push --arch feeds IngestParams.Architecture -> SubjectRef.Architecture -> user enricher emits "architecture", so uploads satisfy the gate with real metadata. Not defaulted to runtime.GOARCH — the pushing machine is not necessarily the target. The CI task writes go env GOARCH to .sbom-bins/.goarch at build time and push-sboms.nu appends --arch only if that file exists.

Verified: go build ./... clean; ./internal/... and ./cmd/ocidex-cli/... tests pass; golangci-lint on cmd/ocidex-cli 0 issues; make tekton-synth preserved both scripts (no dropped expansions); both generated nu step scripts parse clean under nu --ide-check; the GOARCH write/read/append fragment simulated locally against the real go toolchain.

title: Persist the buildkit root on a cache PVC
description: buildctl-daemonless.sh starts a throwaway buildkitd whose state dir dies with the step, so each of the ten serial image builds re-pulls the base image, re-runs go mod download, re-materialises builder-base, and discards the --mount=type=cache Go build cache. Point buildkitd --root at a PVC-backed cache workspace (pattern: goCacheWs/nodeCacheWs). Two workspaces — push chain (amd64) and release chain (multi-arch) can overlap and buildkitd takes an exclusive root lock. Requires a matching PVC change in homelab talos-cluster/flux/apps/ocidex-ci/cache-pvcs.yaml, landed first. Needs a prepare step to chmod 0777 the root subdir (build step runs uid/gid 1000, pod fsGroup is 1024) and a buildkitd.toml GC policy (native snapshotter copies rather than overlays).
acceptance_criteria: Second isolated TaskRun of image-build-git-worker shows go mod download + distroless pull CACHED; a following image-build-api run against the same PVC shows builder-base fully CACHED and only 'go build ./cmd/ocidex' executing.
notes:
VERIFIED 2026-08-05 with four ad-hoc TaskRuns in ocidex-ci (no commits pushed).

Files: .tektonic/shared.ts (buildkitCacheWs, buildkitReleaseCacheWs), .tektonic/pipeline.ts (both under caches:, 25Gi local-path), .tektonic/jobs/image-build/spec.ts (prepare-buildkit-root step, cacheWs param on buildImageTask/serialChain, --root/--config in BUILDKITD_FLAGS), .tekton/** regenerated. PVCs live in homelab talos-cluster/flux/apps/ocidex-ci/cache-pvcs.yaml (commit 1ef7a0c, local only — must be pushed for Flux).

Approach: point buildctl-daemonless.sh buildkitd --root at a PVC-backed workspace so the content store, snapshots and the Dockerfile --mount=type=cache mounts outlive the step. Explicit buildkitd.toml gcpolicy (keepBytes 14GiB, all=true) because declaring one replaces buildkit defaults. prepare-buildkit-root runs at pod uid 1024 and chmod 0777s the root subdir — the build step is uid 1000 (buildkit rootless) against an fsGroup-1024 volume; changing runAsGroup instead would risk rootlesskit subuid/subgid mapping.

MEASUREMENTS (image-build-git-worker unless noted, step-build-and-push wall time):
- pass 1, cold root:                    10m46s
- pass 2, same image, warm root:         5m35s   (COPY go.mod go.sum / go mod download / distroless pull all CACHED)
- image-build-api, warm root:            8m28s   (one-time COPY . . re-key from the 2vr.1 context switch, 156s)
- git-worker after api, steady state:    5m18s   builder-base fully CACHED (#12-#15), only go build ./cmd/git-worker ran

Steady state per image = 5m18s, of which 95.6s is the registry cache export (see ocidex-2vr.3). Residual is #16 go build at ~210s.

Projected pipeline: ~8m first build + 9 x ~5m18s = ~56m with the registry cache still on, ~41m without it. Baseline 121m.

PVC pinned to talos-jlf-6ro (16Gi RAM / ~220Gi disk) as required; the three 3.8Gi nodes cannot host these builds. Usage after 2 images / 4 builds: 4.3G of the 25Gi claim, all under root/runc-native — comfortably below the 14GiB keepBytes ceiling. Re-measure after a full ten-image run.

title: Dev DB objects owned by postgres, not ocidex: blocked migration 00052, then broke components/licenses/vulns pages
description:
Migration 00052_visible_registry_ids.sql failed on every retry in ocidex-dev (jobs 264-280), leaving the DB pinned at goose version 51 and blocking the Flux rollout of sha-949ffec4.

Error: 'ERROR: must be owner of function visible_registry_ids (SQLSTATE 42501)'

Root cause: the function already existed in the dev DB, owned by role 'postgres'. It was created out-of-band (by hand) during the ocidex-ckv.2 rollup performance work and never dropped. The migration job connects as role 'ocidex'; CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION requires ownership of the existing function, so it could never succeed. sbom_visible, artifact_visible and signing_status are all owned by 'ocidex' (created by migrations) - visible_registry_ids was the only outlier.

Not a defect in the migration SQL itself: applying 00052 against a clean local DB works, and the same SQL run as 'postgres' against dev worked. It is purely an ownership mismatch created by manual DB surgery.

Immediate fix applied to ocidex-dev:
  ALTER FUNCTION visible_registry_ids(UUID, BOOLEAN) OWNER TO ocidex;
Job ocidex-dev-migrate-282 then completed and the rollout proceeded.

Remaining work is prevention, not repair.
design: Forward risk that makes this urgent rather than merely tidy: migration 00053_namespace_source.sql (ocidex-9xs.2, committed today) issues 9 ALTER TABLE statements against component_rollup, license_rollup and vuln_rollup to rekey them from registry_id to namespace_id. ALTER TABLE requires ownership. So 00053 will fail on ocidex-dev exactly the way 00052 did unless the rollup tables are owned by 'ocidex' first. Deploying epic ocidex-9xs is blocked on this repair.
acceptance_criteria:
- A guard exists against out-of-band DB objects blocking migrations (options: audit query for public functions/tables not owned by the app role, run in CI or as a preflight; or a documented rule that dev-DB experiments must be done as the app role).
- docs/DEVELOPMENT.md notes that manual psql surgery on a deployed DB must use the 'ocidex' role, never 'postgres', because CREATE OR REPLACE and DROP both require ownership.
- Any other public-schema object in ocidex-dev not owned by 'ocidex' is identified and corrected.
notes:
Files: internal/dbaudit/ownership.go (+test), tests/ownership_audit_test.go, cmd/ocidex/main.go (ownershipPreflight), docs/DEVELOPMENT.md (Database Ownership), docs/DEPLOYMENT.md (migrate Job).

Approach: preflight, not repair — ALTER ... OWNER TO itself requires ownership, so nothing in-band can fix the state; the guard detects it and prints the superuser statements. dbaudit.Misowned() queries pg_class + pg_proc in schema public where NOT pg_has_role(current_user, owner, 'USAGE') (membership counts, so a group-role owner is not a false positive), excluding extension members via pg_depend.deptype='e' (the ~30 pg_trgm functions) and indexes (ownership follows the table). Wired into 'ocidex migrate up' before goose runs, plus a standalone read-only 'ocidex migrate audit' for throwaway-pod diagnosis. Escape hatch OCIDEX_MIGRATE_SKIP_OWNERSHIP_CHECK=1.

Verified: tests/ownership_audit_test.go passes against real PG15 (testcontainers) — detects a superuser-created table + function, ignores pg_trgm and app-owned objects, and the rendered ALTER statements execute and clear the audit. Ran the audit query against ocidex-dev as role 'ocidex': zero rows. Distribution now 30 relations / 5 app functions owned by ocidex; the 31 postgres-owned pg_proc rows are all pg_trgm extension members, correctly excluded. Acceptance criterion 3 satisfied with no further repair needed.

title: Bind ingest to a source and close the NULL-visibility hole
description:
POST /api/v1/sboms?source=<name|uuid> resolves the source and its namespace, and enforces that the API key's user owns that namespace.

This is the security half of the epic: today IngestSBOM (internal/api/sbom.go:15) never sets RegistryID, and sbom_visible() treats NULL as visible-to-everyone, so every manually uploaded SBOM is world-readable.
design:
Reuse isWriteAllowed plus an ownership check modelled on GetArtifactOwnerID (internal/service/sbom.go:361).

Sequence matters: backfill or admin-assign any pre-existing namespace_id IS NULL rows BEFORE tightening the constraint, then drop the IS NULL disjunct from sbom_visible/artifact_visible. Doing it the other way round hides existing data.
acceptance_criteria:
- ingest without a resolvable source returns 400
- ingest against a namespace you do not own returns 403
- no namespace_id IS NULL rows remain
- the IS NULL disjunct is gone from both visibility functions
notes:
Files: db/migrations/00054_require_namespace.sql; db/queries/{search,stats,vulnerability}.sql (+ regenerated internal/repository); internal/service/sbom.go; internal/api/{sbom,types}.go; internal/scanner/engine/dispatcher.go; tests/ (9 files).

Approach: the namespace is derived from the source, not passed alongside it — NamespaceID was removed from IngestParams entirely, so 'the SBOM lands in the namespace that owns the source it arrived through' is unforgeable at the type level. resolveIngestNamespace() looks the source up; missing/unknown is a ValidationError -> 400.

?source= grammar: UUID or <namespace>/<name> only. Bare names are deliberately rejected — source names are UNIQUE(namespace_id, name), not globally unique, so resolving one means guessing which namespace was meant, and a push that worked would start failing the day a second namespace gained a same-named source. NOTE for 0gp.4: the plan doc's '--source ocidex-ci' CLI example must become '--source <namespace>/<name>'.

Status codes: unresolvable source -> 400 (the request named something nonexistent; the endpoint is fine). Source in a namespace you do not own -> 403, whether or not you can read it.

Closed 0gp.2's forward note by requiring subject_type and subject_name to be *declared* in validateUploadRequired, not merely resolved — a 'syft dir:' BOM always supplies both from the scratch directory, so checking resolved values could never catch an artifact named .sbom-bins (ADR-040).

Fixed a real bug in dispatcher.go: it set NamespaceID=SourceID=registryID claiming a registry's id is both. That holds only when the registry creates its own namespace; when the operator supplies an existing namespace_id, only source+registry share an id.

Migration 00054 verified up/down/up on a throwaway PG17: NOT NULL on sbom + 3 rollups, no IS NULL arm left in sbom_visible/artifact_visible/visible_namespace_ids. Pre-existing unowned rows go to a private, unowned 'unassigned' namespace (matches no viewer -> admin-only, fail closed).

Verification: go test ./internal/... green; tests/ integration failures identical to the HEAD baseline (7 pre-existing, ocidex-784 + scan_to_enrich network) — no regression. make lint's 61 issues are pre-existing and identical at HEAD; filed as a separate bug.

title: Namespace and source service + API surface
description: New internal/service/namespace.go and source.go; strip ownership lookups out of registry.go. Expose /api/v1/namespaces CRUD and /api/v1/sources, and keep /api/v1/registries writing all three rows in one transaction.
design:
subject.Ref keeps RegistryID but resolves it via source: the provenance enricher looks up registry by source id, and an upload source (no registry row) returns CanEnrich == false rather than erroring.

Ownership checks model on GetArtifactOwnerID (internal/service/sbom.go:361).

After the API changes run make openapi, then update pkg/client (registry.go + new namespace.go, source.go).
acceptance_criteria:
- namespaces and sources are CRUD-able
- creating a registry writes namespace + source + registry atomically
- provenance enricher returns CanEnrich=false for upload sources
- make openapi produces no diff after regeneration
notes:
Files: internal/service/namespace.go, internal/service/source.go (new); internal/api/namespace.go, internal/api/source.go (new); internal/api/{types,handler,router,middleware}.go; internal/enrichment/{subject/subject.go,provenance/provenance.go}; internal/service/registry.go; cmd/ocidex/main.go; pkg/client/{client,fake_client,namespace,source,types}.go; web/openapi.json; web/src/types/openapi.d.ts.

Approach: NamespaceService/SourceService added over the 00053 tables. canManageNamespace is now the single ownership rule; source-level checks route through Handler.namespaceOwnerCheck rather than each handler growing its own. RequireSBOMOwner/RequireArtifactOwner take NamespaceService and resolve owners directly, deleting the ADR-039 registry-id workaround. Registry create/update still writes namespace+source+registry in one transaction and registry.sql joins namespace for owner_id/visibility so canManageRegistry is unchanged. Provenance enricher resolves registry via source id and returns CanEnrich=false for upload sources. NewHandler grew 9->11 positional params (8 call sites updated). make openapi + make generate-client regenerated clean; generate-client-check now passes, which also resolves ocidex-52a.

title: Repoint query and repository layer to namespace_id
description:
Update the ~85 registry_id references across db/queries/*.sql and regenerate sqlc. Heaviest files: stats.sql (22), registry.sql (21), search.sql (14), artifact.sql (7).

registry.sql splits three ways — namespace.sql, source.sql, registry.sql — and registry create/update becomes a three-table transaction.
design:
Preserve the stats.sql pattern: rollup paths use IN (SELECT visible_namespace_ids(...)), not a per-row function call. A regression here undoes ocidex-ckv.2.

Do not edit internal/repository/*sql.go or models.go directly — edit db/queries/*.sql and run make generate.
acceptance_criteria:
- make generate produces a clean build
- EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the components list keeps the semi-join plan
notes:
Files: db/queries/{namespace,source,registry,stats,search,artifact,vulnerability,sbom,enrichment_jobs,provenance_drift}.sql; internal/repository/{repository.go,rollup_refresh.go} + regenerated sqlc; internal/service/{registry,sbom,enrichjob,search_sbom,search_stats}.go; internal/api/middleware.go; internal/scanner/{catalog.go,engine/dispatcher.go}; tests + fakes.
Approach: registry.sql split three ways per ADR-039. Registry create/update use data-modifying CTEs to write namespace+source+registry in one statement (a service-layer pool.Begin would panic in unit tests, which inject a fake repo with a nil pool). Reads use sqlc.embed(r) joined to source+namespace, adapted through a single registryComposite in the service. SetEnabled/MarkPolled re-read via Get since UPDATE ... RETURNING cannot join. DeleteRegistry now deletes the source (cascades to registry) leaving namespace+SBOMs standing, closing the visibility-widening hole. enrichment_jobs claims emit source_id, so GetRegistry(source_id) resolves for OCI sources and returns not-found for uploads (ADR-039 CanEnrich==false, no new code). internal/repository/rollup_refresh.go held raw SQL outside sqlc and also needed repointing. Rollup predicates keep the IN (SELECT visible_namespace_ids(...)) semi-join (ocidex-ckv.2 constraint) — only the column name changed.
Verified: go vet clean, make test green, openapi-check clean, frontend gates green. make lint fails on 61 pre-existing issues (identical count on main). Integration tests: vuln rollup tests now pass; remaining failures are the pre-existing 400/422 ingest set (ocidex-784) plus TestScanToEnrichFlow, which shares one 4-minute deadline between the SBOM wait and the enrichment wait and ran out of budget after syft pulled layers.

title: Migration 00053: namespace + source tables, repointed FKs, visible_namespace_ids
description:
The schema change itself. Highest-risk story in the epic — verify both directions on a seeded DB before moving on.

Creates namespace and source, makes registry a subtype keyed on source.id, repoints every registry_id FK, and rewrites the visibility functions.
acceptance_criteria:
- migrate-up then migrate-down is clean on a seeded DB
- no sbom.namespace_id is NULL after migration
- per-namespace SBOM counts match pre-migration per-registry counts
- scan_jobs still keys on registry_id
notes:
Files: db/migrations/00053_namespace_source.sql (only file; query layer is 9xs.3).

Approach: id-preserving split per ADR-039. One namespace + one source per existing registry, both reusing registry.id, so every stored registry_id stays valid as both namespace_id and source_id — repointed FKs, not a data remap. registry becomes the oci_registry subtype via a self-referencing PK FK to source. sbom.registry_id -> namespace_id plus a new nullable source_id; artifact_registry -> artifact_namespace; three rollups rekey to namespace_id; scan_jobs untouched. visible_registry_ids -> visible_namespace_ids preserving the set-returning shape from 00052.

Verification: scratchpad Postgres 17 cluster, fixture seeded at v52 with the edge cases (public/private/other-owner registries, an SBOM with NULL registry_id, an artifact in two registries, rollup rows in both keyed and NULL buckets). 22 assertions pass after up, 16 after down, 22 again after re-up. Assertions compare against _pre_counts/_pre_vis tables frozen before the migration rather than hand-copied numbers, so visibility is checked bit-identical per (sbom, viewer) pair.

Two Down bugs found and fixed during verification:
1. Postgres validates LANGUAGE sql bodies at CREATE time, so the three visibility functions cannot be recreated until registry.visibility/owner_id are restored. All three are now dropped up front and recreated at the very end of the Down.
2. ALTER TABLE ... RENAME CONSTRAINT has no IF EXISTS, so both constraint renames are wrapped in DO blocks guarded on pg_constraint. Without this, Down failed on any DB migrated up before the rename was added.

Also confirmed the latent security bug ADR-039 cites is closed: pre-migration, DELETE FROM registry NULLed sbom.registry_id and sbom_visible's NULL arm returns true for everyone, so deleting a private registry silently published its SBOMs. Now the namespace outlives the registry; deleting either the registry or the whole source leaves namespace_id and visibility unchanged. Tested explicitly in rolled-back transactions.

Deviation from the stated acceptance criteria: 'no sbom.namespace_id is NULL after migration' cannot hold yet. namespace_id stays nullable here deliberately — closing that hole is ocidex-0gp.3's job, and one risky change at a time. What was asserted instead: no previously-owned SBOM became NULL, and the one intentionally-unowned row is still NULL.

Not done here: EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the components list. The rollup queries in stats.sql still reference registry_id, so there is nothing meaningful to plan until 9xs.3 repoints them. Moved to 9xs.3.

title: ADR-039: namespace and source model
description:
Record the decomposition of registry's three jobs into namespace (ownership/visibility), source (ingest channel) and registry (OCI-specific config).

Must capture: the placement rule, the rejected alternative and why, and the K8s naming collision mitigation. This ADR is the normative contract the rest of the epic is checked against.
design:
Placement rule: ownership and visibility on `namespace`; how-we-found-it on `source`; anything meaningful only when you can pull a manifest on `registry`.

Rejected: owner_id/visibility directly on artifact. Per-artifact visibility destroys the IN (SELECT visible_*_ids) semi-join that 00052_visible_registry_ids.sql exists to enable — that migration's comment is a load-bearing performance constraint.

K8s collision: all 3 CRDs are scope=Namespaced. Mitigation is to make it a feature — the operator defaults an OCIRegistry's OCIDex namespace from its K8s namespace — plus unambiguous Go naming.
acceptance_criteria:
- docs/adr/0039-*.md exists and states the placement rule
- rejected alternative recorded with its performance reason
- ADR summary table in CLAUDE.md updated
notes:
Files: docs/adr/0039-namespace-and-source-model.md (new), CLAUDE.md (ADR summary table row 039).

Approach: MADR template, matching ADR-038's evidence-heavy style. Four options weighed; ownership-on-artifact rejected on the k.o. criterion that per-artifact visibility destroys the IN (SELECT visible_*_ids) semi-join that 00052 exists to enable (121,080 calls / 3,818ms / 242k buffer hits -> 100ms for 8 registries). The 'source-supertype-carries-ownership' option is recorded as rejected too, since it renames rather than decomposes.

Documented the placement rule, the 26-column four-job breakdown of registry, the id-preserving migration trick (namespace.id = source.id = registry.id, so stored registry_id values stay valid), and scan_jobs staying on registry_id as the correctness check on where the subtype line is drawn.

Corrections made during writing, both verified against source rather than assumed:
- RequireRegistryOwner does not exist; the real helper is canManageRegistry (internal/api/registry.go:518).
- Registry visibility currently defaults to PUBLIC (both the 00017 column default and the CreateRegistry handler). ADR originally claimed a private default; narrowed to 'namespaces created implicitly for upload sources default to private', with existing data and POST /api/v1/registries explicitly unchanged.
- ADR-025 is amended, not superseded: its roles table and API-key scopes carry over; only 'Registry Owner' -> 'Namespace Owner' changes. ADR-025 itself named this trigger condition ('if multi-tenancy requirements grew beyond single-owner registries').

New design point surfaced: managed_by/managed_ref stay on registry and are NOT copied to namespace, because two OCIRegistry CRs in one K8s namespace map to one OCIDex namespace. The operator therefore creates namespaces but never deletes them on CR deletion.

title: Namespace/source decomposition: split tenancy from ingest channel
description:
Extract ownership and visibility out of `registry` into a new `namespace` table, and the ingest-channel identity into a new `source` table, leaving `registry` as the oci_registry subtype holding only url/auth/patterns/trust config.

Today `registry` does three unrelated jobs: ownership/visibility (owner_id, visibility), discovery config (url, auth, patterns, polling), and trust policy (verification_mode, trust keys). This blocks non-container artifacts entirely — an SBOM uploaded from CI has no registry, so it has no owner, and `sbom_visible()` treats a NULL registry as world-visible.

Two findings justify the split rather than a rename:
- 00052_visible_registry_ids.sql shows rollup `registry_id` is semantically a *visibility bucket*, not a registry identity (3818ms -> 100ms by evaluating visibility once per registry).
- Registry is not a user browse axis: Artifacts.tsx/Components.tsx never filter by it; registries.ts is admin-only.

Rejected alternative: ownership directly on `artifact`. Most honest model, but per-artifact visibility destroys the cheap IN (SELECT visible_*_ids) semi-join that 00052 exists to enable.

Foundational: blocks the non-container lifecycle epic and the relationships epic.
design:
Target model:
  namespace (id, name, owner_id, visibility)     <- authorization anchor
  source    (id, namespace_id, kind, name)       <- ingest channel
    registry (id -> source.id, url, auth, patterns, trust)  <- oci_registry subtype
  sbom      (namespace_id, source_id)
  *_rollup  (namespace_id)
  scan_jobs (registry_id)  -- unchanged; truly registry-scoped

Migration is cheap because ids are preserved: one namespace AND one source per existing registry, both reusing registry.id. Every existing registry_id value stays valid as both namespace_id and source_id, so this is repointed FKs, not a data remap. scan_jobs staying put is the check that the split is drawn in the right place.

Naming: OCIDex `namespace` collides with K8s metadata.namespace (all 3 CRDs are scope=Namespaced). Turn it into a feature: the operator defaults an OCIRegistry's OCIDex namespace from its K8s namespace. Keep Go types unambiguous (service.Namespace vs client.ObjectKey.Namespace); never a bare `ns` in controller code.
acceptance_criteria:
- namespace, source tables exist; registry is a subtype keyed on source.id
- visible_namespace_ids replaces visible_registry_ids with the same set-returning shape
- no rollup query regresses: EXPLAIN ANALYZE keeps the semi-join plan
- migration is reversible on a seeded DB
- auth boundary tests cover private-namespace invisibility to non-owners

title: Raise push/tag pipeline timeout from 2h to 4h
description: Run ocidex-ocidex-push-khjtq hit PipelineRunTimeout at exactly 2h with 7 of 9 images built and image-build-vuln-worker cancelled before it started. Image builds run serially at ~15-18 min each on the homelab node; total budget is ~8 min pre-build + 9 x ~16 min + helm = ~2h40m, so 2h could not fit and 3h would leave only ~13% headroom.
acceptance_criteria: timeouts.pipeline is 4h in both generated push and tag PipelineRuns; .tektonic/pipeline.ts is the source of the change; generated YAML validates server-side.
notes:
Files: .tektonic/pipeline.ts (source of truth), .tekton/ocidex-ocidex-push.k8s.yaml, .tekton/ocidex-ocidex-tag.k8s.yaml (generated)
Approach: Bumped timeout 2h -> 4h on both pushPipeline and tagPipeline in pipeline.ts, then regenerated with make tekton-synth. Sized from measured data rather than guessed: taskrun timings from the failed run show pre-build tasks 8 min, then 9 serial image builds at ~15-18 min each, plus helm — ~2h40m. 3h would leave ~13% headroom, 4h is comfortable. PR pipeline left at the 1h default (last run finished in 9.5 min; it builds no images).
Verified: make tekton-synth produced a 2-line diff touching only 'pipeline: 2h' -> '4h' — no collateral from the known synth bug that drops ${VAR#prefix} patterns. timeouts block sets only 'pipeline', no tasks/finally sub-timeouts to conflict. Both generated PipelineRuns pass kubectl apply --dry-run=server against ocidex-ci.
