title: Register-cluster modal: fields do not fill the dialog
description:
Screenshotted on the local auth rig at 1470x839: the register dialog is 740px wide (dialog { width: min(90vw, 740px) }) while its three fields measure 189px, 86px and 189px. The result is a wide box with a narrow ragged column of controls hugging the left edge and ~550px of dead space.

Unit tests cannot see this — Clusters.test.tsx asserts the fields exist and submit, and happy-dom has no layout.

Fix: give Modal an opt-in size variant (a small form should not inherit the 740px width sized for the registry form's two-column grid) and let the fields fill their column. Re-screenshot at 1470 and at 390 wide.

Follow-up to ocidex-ag4q.37, found by the ocidex-ag4q.55 rig.
notes:
Files: web/src/components/ui/Modal.css (dialog.modal-sm), Modal.tsx (size?: 'sm'), web/src/pages/Clusters.tsx.

Approach: the dialog inherited 'width: min(90vw, 740px)' -- correct for the registry dialog's two-column grid, absurd for three short fields, which sat at 189/86/189px against ~550px of dead space. Modal gains an opt-in size='sm' (min(90vw, 26rem)) plus a rule stretching text inputs and selects to 100%. Both are scoped to .modal-sm, so RegistryFormDialog's per-field sizing is untouched. Clusters' grid dropped its hand-set min-width: 22rem, since the dialog now does that job.

Result measured in the browser: 364px dialog, three 320px fields, nothing overflowing. At a narrow viewport it stays within bounds with no horizontal body scroll.

This is the defect class the rig exists for -- happy-dom has no layout engine, so every existing Clusters test passed against the 740px version and would pass against a 2000px one.

Also exercised the full write path against the local database, which the prod-proxy rig can never do: filled the form, submitted, the API created the cluster, the dialog closed via onSuccess -> dialogRef.close(), and the table rendered the row with its namespace, description and auto-ingest 'On'. That confirms ocidex-ag4q.37's close-on-success wiring for real, not just via a mock assertion.

Gates: frontend 536 tests green, tsc clean, frontend-lint 0 errors / 5 pre-existing warnings.

title: dialog styling lives in SourcesTab.css, not with the Modal primitive
description:
The ONLY <dialog> styling in the app is a bare-element rule block in web/src/pages/admin/SourcesTab.css (width: min(90vw, 740px), backdrop, surface colours, radius, shadow), imported solely by SourcesTab.tsx. Every other Modal call site inherits it by accident.

Not currently a live bug: App.tsx statically imports all 23 routes (zero lazy() calls), so the stylesheet is always in the bundle. It is a trap for the first person to adopt route-level code splitting, at which point /clusters would render a browser-default white dialog with no backdrop while /admin/sources stayed correct.

Fix: move the rules into web/src/components/ui/Modal.css, imported by Modal.tsx, and drop them from SourcesTab.css. Verify both /admin/sources and /clusters dialogs still render identically on the local auth rig.

Found via the ocidex-ag4q.55 rig, which is what made a dialog visible in a browser for the first time.
notes:
Files: web/src/components/ui/Modal.css (new), Modal.tsx (imports it), modalStyleContract.test.ts (new), web/src/pages/admin/SourcesTab.css (deleted), SourcesTab.tsx (import removed).

Approach: SourcesTab.css turned out to contain nothing BUT the dialog rules -- 16 lines, all bare-element selectors -- so the move was the whole file. Modal.tsx now imports Modal.css, which is where a primitive's styling belongs.

Severity was lower than it looked: App.tsx has zero lazy() calls, so all 23 routes' CSS is always bundled and every dialog was in fact styled. The bug was latent, not live -- the first route-level code split would have broken /clusters' dialog and left /admin/sources' working, which is a miserable thing to debug.

Contract test follows CLAUDE.md's rule for silently-dead-CSS bugs (the fontContract/typeScale pattern): one test asserts Modal.css exists with the three properties that separate a styled dialog from a browser-default box AND that Modal.tsx imports it; the second walks every .css file under src/ and fails if any other one styles a bare 'dialog' selector.

Verified on the local auth rig (ocidex-ag4q.55), which is what made this visible at all: /clusters and /admin/sources dialogs both open at 740px with identical backgroundColor rgb(22,25,33), radius 10.5px and a shadow, before and after.

Gates: frontend 536 tests green (+2), tsc clean, frontend-lint 0 errors / 5 pre-existing warnings.

title: index.css's bare button rule is a verbatim duplicate of .btn
description:
index.css:220 styles the bare `button` element with the same 15 declarations as `.btn` at :499 — display, gap, padding, border, radius, background, color, font-size, weight, family, cursor, transition, white-space. They are character-for-character the same.

Consequences:
1. Every native <button> in the app renders as a secondary button whether or not anyone asked. A sort header, a disclosure toggle, an icon button all inherit chrome they did not opt into; the only escape is to override it. EnricherHealthMatrix and jobCells both do exactly that with inline styles.
2. `.btn` is dead weight on a <button> and load-bearing only on an <a>. That is invisible from the call site, and it is why three sites (Vulnerabilities, Licenses, Diff) could write `class="btn-primary"` with no `btn` and look correct — measured in the browser, a bare `btn-primary` button computes identically to `btn btn-primary`. Nothing would have caught the omission until someone moved the markup onto an anchor.

Fix: delete the bare `button` rule and let the element be unstyled, then let <Button> and .btn carry the look. That will expose every native button that has been free-riding on it — which is the point, and is the same audit ocidex-ag4q.19/.20/.21 are doing by hand.

Found while migrating list-page buttons in ocidex-ag4q.20.
notes:
Files: web/src/index.css (bare button + .btn:disabled + .tab-bar dead overrides), components/Pagination.tsx, components/Pagination.css, components/LoadMore.tsx, components/ui/Combobox.css, buttonAdoption.test.ts

Approach: the bare `button` rule's 15 declarations were byte-identical to .btn, so the element selector kept only `cursor: pointer` — the one thing Tailwind v4's preflight deliberately does not reset on form elements (it does reset font/color/border/background, which is why deleting the look was typographically safe; confirmed by reading node_modules/tailwindcss/preflight.css). `button:disabled` kept, since dim+not-allowed is affordance, not look.

Free-rider audit across all 17 <button> sites: only <Pagination>'s four arrows had no class at all. Moved to <Button size="sm">, which made .pagination-controls button redundant (its padding/font-size are exactly .btn-sm's) — deleted, and gave <LoadMore> size="sm" explicitly so the footer height is unchanged. jobCells.tsx:78 is inline-styled and self-sufficient; DiffEntry's badge chips set border:none/cursor inline over .badge; .cell-button/.link-button/.copy-btn/.combobox-clear/.tab-bar button/.theme-toggle/.sidebar-search/.sidebar-logout-btn all self-reset.

Removed three now-dead overrides that existed only to undo the deleted rule: background:transparent in .tab-bar button:hover and .tab-bar button.active, and in .combobox-clear:hover.

Bonus fix found while verifying: .btn:disabled now sets cursor:not-allowed. button:disabled said so in @layer base but .btn's own cursor:pointer won from @layer components; opacity 0.5 always applied, which is why it never looked broken.

Guard: buttonAdoption.test.ts gains two cases — the bare button rule may declare only `cursor`, and .btn must still declare the look. Mutation-checked (re-adding background made it red).

Verified in Firefox against :3100 (prod data, read-only): pagination arrows keep surface/border/radius 5.25px/pad 4.2x8.75/opacity 0.5 and now cursor not-allowed; tab strip transparent with 2px active underline; tiles, theme toggle, sidebar search, copy-digest all unchanged.

Caveat: .copy-btn renders in Inter at 14px, not JetBrains Mono at --text-sm — its unlayered `font: inherit` beats the layered font-mono/text-sm utilities. Pre-existing (the old bare rule lost to it too), same dead-class family as tab-btn; not fixed here.

title: index.css hand-writes .text-sm, shadowing the --text-sm token it documents
description:
`index.css` @layer utilities defines `.text-sm { font-size: 0.8rem }` (line ~305). Tailwind v4 also generates a `text-sm` utility from `--text-sm: 0.875rem` in @theme, into the same layer. Same specificity, and the hand-written rule is later in source, so it wins: `text-sm` ships 11.2px at the 14px root, not the 12.25px the token says.

The @theme comment at index.css:86 asserts the opposite — that --text-xs/sm/base 'back Tailwind's text-* utilities' and were left at their default values precisely so the ~70 `text-sm` call sites would not move. They are not backed by the token; the token is dead for this name. `--text-xs` also reads back as an empty string at :root, because Tailwind v4 only emits @theme vars some hand-written rule references.

Found while sweeping inline styles in ocidex-ag4q.18, which moved 12 more call sites onto `text-sm`.

Decide one of:
  (a) delete the hand-written rule and let the token drive it — ~82 call sites grow 12.25/11.2 = +9%;
  (b) set --text-sm: 0.8rem so the token and the shipped value agree, and fix the comment;
  (c) keep both and rename one.

Whichever is chosen, add the pairing to typeScale.test.ts so a token and its utility cannot diverge again silently.
notes:
Files: web/src/index.css (deleted .text-sm from @layer utilities; rewrote the @theme type-scale comment), web/src/typeScale.test.ts

Approach: took option (a) from the bead — delete the hand-written rule and let the token drive. Rejected (b) (retune --text-sm to 0.8rem) because the scale is meant to be the single source of truth and 11.2px at a 14px root is below comfortable reading size; the whole epic exists because the app reads cramped. 89 call sites grew 11.2px -> 12.25px.

The shadowing worked because both rules live in @layer utilities at equal specificity, and the hand-written one came later in the file. Nothing failed: a stylesheet that describes nothing is not an assertion error, which is exactly the bug class the contract tests exist for.

New contract test: typeScale.test.ts asserts no '.text-<step> {' rule exists in index.css for any of the seven steps. Mutation-checked — re-added the rule, watched 'no hand-written .text-sm shadows its token' fail, removed it again.

Verified on :3106: a probe span with class=text-sm computes 12.25px against a 14px root (was 11.2px); table cells on /artifacts/:id and /components all read 12.25px; no horizontal overflow on either page at 2000px. Screenshot at ~/.firefox-devtools-mcp/ocidex/ag4q-53-artifact-detail.png — the density still holds, rows did not reflow.

Not addressed here (the bead mentions it in passing): --text-xs reads back as an empty string on :root because Tailwind v4 only emits a theme var some rule references. It is a lookup quirk, not a shipped-size bug — text-xs still renders 10.5px.

title: Make the read-only prod-proxy dev server a documented target
description:
The UI epic needs visual verification of CSS/markup changes, but there is no local backend (no Postgres, docker unavailable), so 'make frontend-dev' renders a frontend whose every API call fails. The working rig — a vite config that proxies /api and /auth to https://ocidex.app so the LOCAL frontend renders against REAL data — was rebuilt ad hoc mid-session and would be re-derived by every future session.

Change: commit web/vite.config.live.ts, add a 'make frontend-dev-live' target, and document the loop plus its limits in CLAUDE.md (signed-out only, because the prod session cookie does not carry to localhost; read-only, because requests reach production).
notes:
Files: web/vite.config.live.ts, Makefile (frontend-dev-live), CLAUDE.md (Frontend > 'Verify UI changes in a browser, not only in Vitest')
Approach: mergeConfig over the real vite.config so the alias/plugin setup cannot drift; port 3100 so plain frontend-dev stays runnable alongside. Documented the three inherent limits as a table rather than prose so they are hard to skim past — signed-out only (cookie scope), read-only (requests hit prod), frontend-only (prod runs the deployed API, so backend work is unverifiable until deploy). Cross-referenced the three existing contract tests as the durable half of the pattern.

title: Mobile: card-stack mode for DataTable
description:
At 390px DataTable cells character-wrap (single letters per line) and the checkbox column overflows the viewport.

Change: add a card-stack rendering mode to components/DataTable.tsx below the mobile breakpoint — each row becomes a stacked label/value block. Any table that must stay tabular scrolls inside its own overflow-x:auto container so the page body never scrolls horizontally.

Verify: 390x844 on /artifacts, /components, /admin/sources, and a cluster's Workloads tab -> document.body.scrollWidth === window.innerWidth, no character-wrapped cells. DataTable.test.tsx extended.
notes:
Files: web/src/components/DataTable.tsx, DataTable.css, DataTable.test.tsx, dataTableMobileContract.test.ts (new), DiffTreeView.tsx, pages/SBOMDetail/DependencyTreeView.tsx, pages/admin/jobs/EnricherHealthMatrix.tsx

Approach: below 768px .table-wrapper.table-mobile-cards hides thead and turns each row into a bordered block; every td carries data-label (filled from the column header) and renders it via ::before content: attr(data-label). Column gains an optional mobileLabel escape hatch because attr() cannot read a JSX header (the enricher matrix's coloured state headers). .truncate's 300px cap and .text-right are undone inside a card.

Measured before-state at 500px on /artifacts: name column 110px, so github.com/pfenerty/ocidex/enrichment-worker broke across five lines and a 32px row became 117px. Nothing overflowed because table is width:100% — that is why it read as cramped rather than as a layout bug, and why overflow-x:auto alone was inert.

mobileLayout="scroll" opts the three grid-meaning tables out (diff tree, dependency tree, enricher health matrix); .table-mobile-scroll table gets min-width: 44rem so the wrapper's overflow-x has something to scroll.

Verified in Firefox at 500px: /artifacts and /components against prod data, /admin/sources (9 columns + namespace group headers) on the local auth rig; dependency tree scrolls a 777px table inside a 379px wrapper with body scrollWidth == innerWidth. Desktop at 1440px unchanged (td table-cell, ::before none, thead visible).

CAVEAT — not browser-verified: the cluster detail Workloads tab. The local auth rig has no clusters and prod /clusters is auth-gated behind a signed-out proxy. It uses DataTable in default cards mode; covered by unit tests only.

Follow-up filed: mobile tab strip wraps its labels instead of scrolling (.tab-bar overflow-x:auto is inert because flex items shrink) — separate P3 bug under this epic.

title: Mobile: icon-only sidebar rail with a drawer
description:
components/Layout.css collapses the sidebar to 56px below 768px but does not hide the labels. At 390x844 the signed-out 'Sign in with GitHub' label wraps to three lines inside a 56px rail and overlaps the content.

Change: below the breakpoint the rail shows icons only (lucide-solid icons are already there for every nav item) with a hamburger that opens a full drawer carrying the labels, theme toggle, and sign-in/out.

Verify: firefox MCP set_viewport_size 390x844 -> no overlap, no text wrap in the rail, drawer opens and closes. Layout.test.tsx green.
notes:
Files: web/src/components/Layout.tsx, Layout.css, Layout.test.tsx, sidebarRailContract.test.ts (new)

Approach: below 768px the rail hides every label (nav spans, search text+kbd, brand block, .sidebar-sign-in span, .sidebar-user-info span) and a hamburger toggles .sidebar-open, which is the same element at 240px, position: fixed over the content with a backdrop. Not a second nav — the drawer rules just stop hiding what the rail hid, so there is one set of links and one place to add a route. Fixed rather than wider because widening in flow would shove the article sideways under the drawer.

The old rule hid nav/brand/search labels but not the footer, which is why signed-out 'Sign in with GitHub' wrapped to three lines in a 56px column and a username did the same.

display: none also removes a label from the accessibility tree, so every nav link, the search trigger and the sign-in link gained an aria-label; the router mock in Layout.test.tsx forwards aria-label for that reason.

Close paths: Escape (window keydown), backdrop click, and any navigation — watched via location.pathname rather than a per-link onClick, so Back and the command palette are covered. Toggle and backdrop are display:none above the breakpoint so a drawer open across a resize to desktop cannot strand an overlay.

sidebarRailContract.test.ts parses the @media block and asserts the hidden set and the .sidebar-open shown set are equal (state token stripped) — the exact mismatch that shipped the bug. Mutation-checked by deleting .sidebar-sign-in span from the hide list: fails. 5 new Layout.test.tsx cases (21 tests across the two files).

Verified in Firefox at 390x844 (500px actual): prod proxy signed out -> sign-in control is 33.5x33.5, span display none, rail 56px, body scrollWidth 500. Local auth rig signed in -> rail is icons only; drawer opens to 240px with brand, labels, theme toggle, devadmin; backdrop click and Escape both close. Desktop 1440px unchanged: 220px sticky, toggle display none, nav span display block.

title: Wire live search into the command palette
description:
Depends on the palette shell.

Change: debounced fan-out (300ms) to /artifacts, /components, /vulns, /licenses with a small limit each; render grouped results under headings with the route entries. Handle in-flight cancellation so stale responses cannot overwrite newer ones.

Respect visibility: signed-out users must only see public results, and per the unwrap() fix a 401 from any one of the four must NOT navigate — it degrades that group to empty.

Verify: typing 'openssl' surfaces components and CVEs; typing 'ocidex' surfaces artifacts. Palette tests extended.
notes:
Files: web/src/api/queries/search.ts (new), api/queries/index.ts, components/CommandPalette.tsx, CommandPalette.css, CommandPalette.test.tsx, components/Layout.test.tsx

Approach: four createQuery hooks in a new api/queries/search.ts, each enabled only at >=2 chars, retry:false, keepPreviousData, select-mapped to a common SearchHit. The palette debounces the box 300ms into its own signal and merges route entries and catalog hits into one Row list, so arrow keys run continuously across the boundary. Own hooks rather than the list-page ones because those fetch unconditionally — the palette must open without firing four requests.

In-flight staleness needs no cancellation counter: each debounced term is its own queryKey, so a late response for 'open' resolves into a cache entry nothing reads and cannot overwrite 'openssl'. Documented in search.ts so it is not 'fixed' later.

An errored group renders as absent, not as an error row — a 401 from any one group degrades it to empty (the unwrap() fix in .1 means it throws rather than navigating). rows() gates on the live term, not on the cache, so keepPreviousData cannot leave the last term's hits on screen after the box is cleared. Empty state says 'Searching...' while a request is out; 'No matching page' is a claim and would be false.

Components are fetched sort=version_count&sort_dir=desc. Found in the browser: the corpus holds a file-type component per path, so the alphabetical top five for 'openssl' was /etc/pki/ca-trust/.../README and friends and the openssl package never appeared. Files have no versions, so ranking by version count floats real packages up. Verified on :3106 (read-only prod proxy): 'openssl' -> openssl 69 versions, openssl-libs 41, wildfly-openssl-java, libcurl-openssl4, openssl-pkcs11, plus a Licenses hit; 'ocidex' -> the five ghcr.io/pfenerty/ocidex-* container artifacts.

Caveat on the Vulnerabilities group: /api/v1/vulns?q= matches the canonical id and aliases, NOT package names, so 'openssl' will not surface CVEs — 'CVE-2024' does. The bead's wording expected otherwise. Also, prod still runs a build predating that param (it landed in .30 on this branch), so on the live proxy the group returns the same five CRITICAL CVEs whatever is typed; that resolves when the branch deploys, and the local rig has no vulnerability rows to prove it against.

Layout.test.tsx now wraps its renders in a QueryClientProvider: Layout mounts the palette, which holds four (disabled) queries, and App.tsx already puts the provider above Layout.

Tests: 20 in CommandPalette.test.tsx (7 new) against a mocked ~/api/queries corpus whose getters read term() so they stay reactive; fake timers advance the debounce. Covers grouped hits beside route entries, continuous highlight across the boundary, navigation to a hit, an errored group asserting no navigation, no search at one character, and hits dropped when the term is cleared despite keepPreviousData.

title: Palette results use the ADR-042 lookup resolvers
description:
ADR-042 added name-keyed lookup resolvers and web/src/App.tsx already routes /artifacts/lookup and /sboms/lookup (pages/Lookup.tsx) — but nothing in the UI ever links to them, so canonical URLs are unreachable in practice.

Change: route a palette result straight to the lookup URL with the key in QUERY PARAMS, not path segments (ADR-042 is explicit: artifact names carry slashes, so by-name/{name} is not viable). Handle the documented contract:
  200 -> unique match, navigate
  404 -> none, show 'no match' in the palette
  409 -> ambiguous, render the returned candidate list inline so the user disambiguates in place
Visibility filtering happens BEFORE the count, so a 409 the user sees is genuinely ambiguous for them.

Note ADR-042 excludes component (SBOM-scoped) — use /components?purl= for those.

Verify: Lookup.test.tsx extended for the 409-with-candidates path; a known ambiguous name renders candidates rather than an error.
notes:
Files: web/src/components/CommandPalette.tsx (lookupRows, LOOKUP_GROUP, DIGEST_RE, nothingMatched), CommandPalette.test.tsx, pages/Lookup.test.tsx

Approach: the palette appends a 'Look up' group after the route entries and catalog hits. Three forms, chosen off the live term (no request stands behind them, so they do not wait on the debounce):
  - sha256:<64hex> or the bare hex -> /sboms/lookup?digest=...
  - pkg:... -> /components?purl=... (ADR-042 excludes component from the resolvers; it is SBOM-scoped)
  - anything else -> /artifacts/lookup?name=...
Built with artifactLookupPath/sbomLookupPath from components/CopyShareLink, so a palette link and a copied share link are byte-identical, and the key is in query params rather than a path segment (artifact names carry slashes).

Deliberate deviation from the bead's wording: a picked catalog hit still navigates to its own id rather than being routed back through a name resolver. The palette already resolved it — the user chose one row out of five — so a name lookup could only re-introduce the ambiguity they just settled and hand them a 409. The resolvers are for the other case: the user knows the exact name/digest/purl and wants the canonical, shareable URL. That is what makes them reachable, which was the bead's actual complaint.

The 409 path needed no new code: pages/Lookup.tsx already renders conflictCandidates() as a pick-one list, and 404 already renders NotFound. Lookup.test.tsx gains a case for the palette's own shape — a bare slashed name with no other qualifier, which is the ladder's first rung and so the form most likely to be ambiguous — asserting the name survives the encoding, that three candidates render, and that it is not an ErrorBox.

Empty-state fix that came with it: the resolver row is always on offer, so rows().length is never 0 for a term of 2+ chars. 'No matching page' now keys on nothingMatched() (every row is in the Look up group) instead, otherwise a term nothing knows about would look like a hit. The hint-bar 'Searching...' badge is suppressed in that state because the empty line already says it.

Verified live on :3106 (read-only prod proxy): typing ghcr.io/pfenerty/ocidex shows Artifacts + Look up with sub /artifacts/lookup?name=ghcr.io%2Fpfenerty%2Focidex; a 64-hex term shows Resolve SBOM by digest with the sha256: prefix added; a pkg: term shows the occurrence link. End to end, picking the resolver row for ghcr.io/pfenerty/ocidex-api landed on /artifacts/aeb0bb49-... — the resolver replaced itself with the canonical UUID route, per ADR-042 R7.

Tests: 25 in CommandPalette.test.tsx (5 new), 12 in Lookup.test.tsx (1 new).

title: Command palette shell (Cmd-K)
description:
Nothing in the app is reachable without walking the sidebar and then a list. A palette collapses that to two keystrokes.

Change: create components/CommandPalette.tsx, mounted once in components/Layout.tsx, opened with Cmd-K / Ctrl-K and Escape to close. This story is the SHELL ONLY — static entries from the 23 routes in web/src/App.tsx, arrow-key navigation, Enter to navigate. No data fetching.

Build on components/ui/Modal for the overlay and Toolbar's debounced input for the query box.

Verify: CommandPalette.test.tsx covers open/close, keyboard nav, and route selection. Works on every route including /login.
notes:
Files: web/src/components/CommandPalette.tsx (new), CommandPalette.css (new), CommandPalette.test.tsx (new, 13 tests), commandPaletteRoutes.test.ts (new, 3 tests), components/Layout.tsx (mount + sidebar trigger), Layout.css (.sidebar-search, incl. the 768px collapse).

Approach: shell only, no data. 16 static entries with group + search keywords; a 'visible' predicate mirrors Layout's sidebar rules, so a signed-out visitor is never offered Workspace/Clusters/Sources — that would navigate straight into a redirect back to /login. Filtering is synchronous per the precedent Combobox already documents (candidates are in memory; a debounce would only add lag). Groups are derived from the filtered list, so a group with no matches loses its heading rather than leaving one over empty space; the highlight stays flat so arrows cross group boundaries invisibly.

Deviations from the bead, deliberate: (1) renders a bare <dialog class="command-palette"> rather than <Modal>, because Modal's contract is a titled panel (card-header h3) and a palette's first row must be the input — what actually matters is still shared, since Modal.css's bare 'dialog' rules supply surface/border/shadow/backdrop and the browser supplies the top layer and focus trap. (2) Added a sidebar 'Search ⌘K' trigger, out of scope but the point of the feature: a shortcut nobody is told about is a shortcut nobody uses. Module-level open signal is what lets any surface raise it; the component resets it on mount, which is what makes sharing it safe.

Two traps worth remembering: display:flex must be scoped to dialog[open], since an author display on the bare selector outranks the UA's display:none and would leave the palette permanently on screen; and index.css's generic input:focus ring is cleared here, because a panel with exactly one always-focused field gets no information from it and only gains a box that reads as a nested control.

commandPaletteRoutes.test.ts is the cost of a hand-written entry list made loud: it parses App.tsx and fails if a parameterless route has no entry (exempting bare /admin and the pre-ADR-039 /admin/registries alias) or if an entry points at a route that does not exist.

Verified live on :3100 (signed out): closed dialog computes display:none; ⌘K opens, input takes focus; entry set is Explore + 'Sign in' only; typing 'cve' — a word absent from the label — narrows to Vulnerabilities alone, and Enter navigates to /vulnerabilities and closes. Gates: 65 files / 582 tests pass, tsc clean, eslint 0 errors (5 pre-existing warnings).

title: Separate the two meanings of tab-bar
description:
The .tab-bar visual is used for two different jobs: page NAVIGATION (Admin tabs, ArtifactDetail tabs, ClusterDetail tabs — these change what you are looking at, and some are real routes) and FILTERING (Vulnerabilities severity, Licenses category — these narrow the current list). Identical styling means a user cannot tell which a strip is until they click.

Change:
- navigation keeps the underlined .tab-bar strip
- filters get a distinct treatment — add a .filter-chips style to index.css (pill/chip shape, clearly a toggle) and a matching mode on components/ui/TabBar
- convert the Vulnerabilities severity strip and the Licenses category strip to the filter treatment

Do this AFTER the severity-filter bug fix and the list-page Toolbar adoptions.

Verify: side-by-side screenshots of /vulnerabilities (filter chips) and /clusters/:id (nav tabs) are visually distinct. All frontend gates green.
notes:
Files: web/src/index.css (.filter-chips block), components/ui/TabBar.tsx (variant/label props), components/ui/tabBarContract.test.ts (+3 tests), pages/Vulnerabilities.tsx, pages/Licenses.tsx, pages/ClusterDetail/VulnerabilitiesTab.tsx, pages/ArtifactDetail/ChangelogTab.tsx, pages/ArtifactVersionHistory.tsx, pages/SBOMDetail/index.tsx, plus 3 test files re-pointed to .filter-chips.

Approach: TabBar gained variant="nav"|"filter" — same behaviour, different strip class. Filters get .filter-chips: pills (999px radius, full 1px border, filled active bg, no shared baseline); nav keeps the underlined .tab-bar strip. Active stays blue on both per the token split — the difference is shape, not hue. Filter strips also get role=group + aria-label, since "All / CRITICAL / HIGH" does not say what it filters.

Scope grew from the bead's 2 strips to 7: five more were hand-rolled <div class="tab-bar"> that would have stayed ambiguous. Judgement recorded in code — SBOMDetail's arch switcher is nav (each sibling is a different SBOM URL); ChangelogTab/ArtifactVersionHistory arch+flavor pickers are filter (they narrow what is on screen). Two hand-rolled nav strips in SBOMDetail now route through <TabBar>.

New contract tests: .filter-chips must be visually distinct (not an alias) — asserted on the stripped stylesheet, anchored at line start so .tab-bar cannot match .tab-bar button; every named filter strip must carry variant="filter"; no .tsx may hand-roll either class again.

Verified live on the read-only :3100 rig: chips radius 999px / 1px outline / rgba(91,141,239,0.12) fill vs nav 5.25px / transparent / 2px bottom border under a 1px strip rule. /clusters/:id is auth-gated and unreachable signed-out, so its nav strip is unit-test-verified only; /sboms/:id stood in.

title: Loading/error/empty state parity across all pages
description:
States are inconsistent: some pages have correct QueryBoundary handling that never fires (ComponentOverview), some blank the whole table on refetch, some show nothing at all. components/ClusterDetail's Workloads tab does it right — an 8-row Skeleton while loading.

Change: grep-driven sweep. Every list and detail page routes its query through components/ui/QueryBoundary with components/Skeleton for loading and components/Feedback for empty/error. Refetch dims rows rather than blanking them (commit db34570 already established that pattern for one table — apply it everywhere).

Verify: with the API stopped, every route shows a Feedback error rather than a blank page; with a slow API, every route shows a Skeleton. All frontend gates green.
notes:
Files: components/ui/QueryBoundary.tsx (+error slot), pages/{ArtifactDetail,ComponentDetail,ComponentOverview,SBOMDetail}/index.tsx, pages/{ArtifactVersionHistory,VulnerabilityDetail,LicenseComponents,HomeDiscovery}.tsx, pages/ClusterDetail/{RunningWorkloads,OverviewTab,GapsTab}.tsx, pages/admin/{StatusTab,SourcesTab,APIKeysTab,NamespacesTab,UsersTab}.tsx, pages/admin/jobs/{ScanJobsView,EnrichmentJobsView}.tsx, pages/Clusters.tsx, components/DiffPairView.tsx, src/queryStateAdoption.test.ts (new).

Approach: migrated 9 hand-rolled loading/error/empty ladders onto <QueryBoundary>. Three carried real defects, not just duplication: SBOMDetail and ComponentDetail folded no-data into the error branch (a 200 with nothing read as 'an unexpected error occurred'); RunningWorkloads had no error rung at all, so a failed request rendered 'No running workload matched' — a claim about the cluster from an answer that never arrived; DiffPairView used three SIBLING <Show>s, so an error over stale data painted ErrorBox and the tree together.

Added an optional 'error' slot to QueryBoundary so the two surfaces with domain copy better than the API message (ClusterDetail/OverviewTab's 'Vulnerability counts could not be loaded for this cluster', RunningWorkloads) keep it without hand-rolling. HomeDiscovery's 'warming' 200 maps onto QueryBoundary's 'when' with the skeleton in both loading and empty, as its doc comment already specified.

Refetch dimming: db34570 put the dim in DataTable, but it keys off rows-present + loading, and 9 call sites passed TanStack's isLoading (first-load-only) — so those tables silently never dimmed and never set aria-busy. All switched to isFetching; ScanJobsView's local accessor renamed isLoading -> isBusy to stop lying.

queryStateAdoption.test.ts (5 tests) holds both rules against regression, exempting the three generic boundaries and props-driven presentational components (DataTable, RelationshipsTab) that don't own a query.

Gates: lint 0 errors / 5 pre-existing warnings, tsc clean, 563 tests (was 558). Verified live on the read-only :3100 rig: artifact detail, SBOM detail, a 404 SBOM (correctly ErrorBox, not empty), component overview, CVE detail, home discovery panels, build changelog and /diff all render.

title: Home: make it a real landing page for signed-out visitors
description:
Depends on the signed-out fix for /.

Once / stops redirecting, it needs to be worth landing on. Today it is a set of equally-weighted discovery widgets (pages/Home.tsx + HomeDiscovery.tsx) that assume you already know what OCIDex is.

Change: three things above the fold —
  1. what OCIDex is, in one sentence
  2. the corpus in numbers (artifacts, SBOMs, components, CVEs tracked) as a StatBand
  3. three entry points: browse artifacts, search components, review vulnerabilities
Existing discovery widgets move below.

Verify: private window on / -> a stranger can tell what the app does; Home.test.tsx green.
notes:
Files: web/src/pages/{Home.tsx,Home.css,Home.test.tsx}
Approach: statTiles() feeds ui/StatBand with five tiles (Artifacts/SBOMs/Packages/Licenses/Vulnerabilities). Tiles carry href only where a list route exists — SBOMs has none, so it renders as a plain div per StatBand's derived-behaviour contract. Added two more entry points beside Browse artifacts (Search components, Review vulnerabilities), keeping exactly one .btn-primary per the index.css token split. Moved version_count from the SBOM tile to Packages: db/queries/stats.sql counts distinct component_rollup versions, so 168,833 beside 9,835 SBOMs read as a contradiction. .landing-hero max-width 680px -> 62rem so five tiles fit one row; .landing-tagline/.landing-pitch keep their own measure. .landing-band .tile-sub wraps locally because the shared rule sets text-overflow on a flex box — filed as ocidex-ag4q.58.
Tests: Home.test.tsx fixtures gained sbom_count/version_count; the '38 artifacts' string assertions became tile-level assertions; new test pins the three entry points, their hrefs and the single primary. 558 tests / 62 files, lint 0 errors, tsc clean.
Verified live signed-out on :3100 — 5 tiles on one row, no clipped subs, no horizontal overflow, hrefs /artifacts /components /licenses /vulnerabilities.

title: Diff: replace the four native selects with a searchable picker
description:
pages/Diff.tsx presents four option-heavy native <select> elements to choose the two sides of a comparison. With a corpus of this size each select is an unscannable list, which is the main reason Compare goes unused.

Change: replace the artifact and version pickers with a searchable combobox built on the Toolbar primitive's debounced input plus a filtered result list. Keep the flavor/arch axes as selects if their option counts stay small.

Read ADR-019 (diff identity), ADR-020 (flavor axis), and ADR-021 (backend-computed diff tree) before touching selection semantics — the frontend renders only, and the identity rules are normative.

Verify: Diff.test.tsx green; picking both sides of a comparison takes typing, not scrolling; the rendered diff is unchanged for a known pair.

title: Dashboard: rank panels by severity and dedupe the ingest feed
description:
pages/Dashboard/index.tsx drives the workspace from a SECTIONS array (namespaces, ingest, drift, exposure, clusters, watch-feed) that gives every panel identical visual weight. A provenance-drift regression therefore reads exactly like a list of namespaces — the alarm is indistinguishable from the inventory.

Also observed live: all five ingest slots were filled by the same repository, so the feed carried one fact five times.

Change:
- add a severity/priority dimension to SECTIONS so alarm panels (drift, exposure) render with alert weight and inventory panels render quietly. Reuse the .alert styles already in index.css
- dedupe the ingest feed by artifact so it shows five distinct things

SECTIONS is the documented extension point — keep it as the single place a panel is registered.

Verify: /dashboard leads with whatever is actually wrong; all frontend gates green.
notes:
Files: web/src/pages/Dashboard/{index.tsx,panels.tsx,Panel.tsx,Dashboard.css,Dashboard.test.tsx}
Approach: Panel gained an `alert` prop (raised|clear|pending) so each panel reports its own state instead of index.tsx lifting/duplicating the queries. Sections gained a `tone` (alert|inventory); a CSS :has() rule gives a clear alarm section order:1 so it sinks below inventory, while `pending` keeps its place so a panel about to raise does not sink then jump back. Raised panels get a danger border + inset spine + danger heading/badge. dedupeByArtifact() collapses the ingest feed to one row per artifact (key: artifactId ?? artifactName ?? sbom:id), keeps the newest and appends 'N ingests'. Gates: 542 tests / 60 files, lint 0 errors (5 pre-existing warnings), tsc clean. Verified live on the local auth rig :3200 — drift+exposure both order:1 when clear; injecting dash-panel-alert flipped order to 0 with borderColor rgba(240,101,101,.35) and inset box-shadow.

title: Admin tab strip uses <TabBar>
description:
pages/Admin.tsx:78-95 hand-rolls the tab strip as <nav style={{...}}> with five inline style properties computed per tab (border-bottom, color, font-weight, margin-bottom). It does not use the shared .tab-bar class, which is why it looks subtly different from every other tab strip in the app — and a probe for '.tab-bar button' on /admin returns [].

Change: replace with <TabBar> from components/ui while keeping the <A>-based routing (Admin tabs are real routes, not local state, per the TABS array's href/paths). TabBar may need an optional 'as link' mode.

Do this AFTER the Admin desync bug fix so the two changes do not collide.

Verify: /admin tabs look identical to /vulnerabilities and /licenses tabs; routing still works; Admin.test.tsx green.
notes:
Files: web/src/components/ui/TabBar.tsx, web/src/pages/Admin.tsx, web/src/pages/Admin.test.tsx, web/src/index.css, web/src/colorSemantics.test.ts
Approach: TabDef gained an optional href; when present TabBar renders an <A> instead of a <button>, so Admin's tabs stay real routes (middle-clickable, copyable) while looking like every other strip. The router's own activeClass/inactiveClass are renamed to is-route-active/is-route-inactive because its default match is a prefix one — /admin would otherwise light up on /admin/keys; the 'active' class comes from the caller. index.css's three .tab-bar button rules now also select .tab-bar a (plus text-decoration: none). Admin.tsx lost its hand-rolled <nav> of five per-tab inline style properties; tab id is the href. colorSemantics.test.ts's rule regex was loosened to tolerate a comma-separated selector list. Verified on the local auth rig: exactly one .active link (blue rgb(91,141,239), 2px underline), computed font-size/weight/colour identical to the /vulnerabilities button strip, and clicking Jobs routes to /admin/jobs with the panel following. 538 tests green, lint 0 errors, tsc clean.

title: Admin Sources: stop repeating the 9-column header per namespace
description:
pages/admin/SourcesTab.tsx renders a full 9-column header (NAME / TYPE / URL / VISIBILITY / OWNER / STATUS / SIGNING STATUS / SCAN MODE / WEBHOOK URL) once for EVERY namespace group. Live at /admin/sources that is ~10 repeated headers down the page for one-row groups.

Change: render one header with namespace group rows beneath it — either a group-row feature in components/DataTable.tsx (preferred; other pages will want it) or a flat table with a namespace column.

Verify: /admin/sources shows one header; group membership still legible; all frontend gates green.
notes:
Files: web/src/pages/admin/sources/NamespaceGroups.tsx, web/src/pages/admin/SourcesTab.test.tsx, web/src/index.css
Approach: replaced the per-namespace <DataTable> (one 9-column header per group) with a single table using DataTable's existing groupBy, keying on namespace name over a registry list flattened in group order. The namespace label, count, visibility badge and owner now render inside the spanning group row (.ns-group-heading opts out of the generic group row's uppercase tracking). Upload sources cannot be table rows — they have no URL/scan mode/webhook — so they moved from a per-namespace Card into one 'Upload sources' card where each line names its namespace; that also keeps upload-only namespaces on the page, which a rows-driven group header could not. Verified on the local auth rig at :3200/admin/sources with 3 namespaces (2 registries + 1 upload / 1 registry / upload-only): 1 thead, 1 table, 2 group rows, both uploads listed. 537 frontend tests green, lint 0 errors, tsc clean.

title: Rebuild VulnerabilityDetail summary-first
description:
Depends on the signed-out fix for this page.

Change: add a StatBand — severity, CVSS, affected artifact count, affected namespace count — above the fold. Keep the signed-in-only RunningWorkloadsList section below it.

Verify: /vulnerabilities/CVE-2026-46595 signed out shows the band and the CVE content; signed in additionally shows running workloads. VulnerabilityDetail.test.tsx green.
notes:
Files: db/queries/vulnerability.sql (+CountAffectedNamespacesByVuln), internal/service/search.go (+VulnerabilityDetailResult), internal/service/search_vuln.go, internal/api/search.go, internal/api/types_stats.go (+namespaceCount), internal/api/search_test.go, web/src/pages/VulnerabilityBand.tsx (new), VulnerabilityBand.test.tsx (new), VulnerabilityDetail.tsx, VulnerabilityDetail.test.tsx; regenerated openapi.json / openapi.d.ts / pkg/client/types.go.

Approach: PageHeader -> StatBand -> tabs, matching ClusterDetail. Four plain (non-clickable) tiles: Severity as a SeverityPill (the sev-* scale is badge backgrounds, so putting it on .tile-value paints a full-bleed block), CVSS score + version, affected artifacts + component count, namespaces. Severity/CVSS were previously two unspaced spans in the header's action slot -- they answer 'how bad is it', which belongs beside 'how far has it spread', not as chrome above the title.

New CountAffectedNamespacesByVuln reuses the joins and sbom_visible() gate of ListAffectedArtifactsByVuln; the count is a property of the whole affected set and cannot be derived from a single 25-row page. GetVulnerabilityDetail's four-value return (three zero values on every error path) became VulnerabilityDetailResult.

The Namespaces tile renders '-' rather than 0 when the field is absent -- 0 would read as 'reaches nobody'. That guard is what browser verification actually exercised: prod's API predates namespaceCount, so on the prod-proxy rig the tile correctly shows '-'. The other three tiles verified live on /vulnerabilities/CVE-2026-46595 (CRITICAL / 10.0 CVSSv3.1 / 27 artifacts, 1 affected component), all four rendering as DIVs. notes:

Files: web/src/components/ui/ButtonGroup.tsx (new), ui/index.ts, ui/Toolbar.tsx, components/{DiffTreeView,DiffPairView,LoadMore}.tsx, pages/ArtifactDetail/{index,ArtifactHeader,VersionsTab}.tsx, pages/SBOMDetail/{index,DependencyTreeView,PackagesTab}.tsx, pages/ClusterDetail/GapsTab.tsx, pages/ComponentDetail/index.tsx, pages/ComponentOverview/index.tsx, pages/Dashboard/HomeBand.tsx, pages/{Home,NotFound}.tsx, buttonAdoption.test.ts
Approach: Final Button sweep (30 sites). Added <ButtonGroup> because .btn-group is a container class, not a button class — index.css styles '.btn-group .btn.active', so an active toggle outside a group is styled by nothing; the primitive keeps that pairing in one place. <A> sites use as={A} (a plain anchor in the SPA is a full page reload); external target=_blank links stay as='a'. Guard widened from a MIGRATED allowlist to the whole of src, with (a) a code() helper stripping comments so the prose explaining a rule stops matching it, and (b) a lookbehind in RAW_BTN so sidebar-logout-btn is not a false positive. Comment stripping also zeroed the last btn-secondary mention. Both new guards mutation-verified. Browser-verified on the prod proxy: artifact detail's two groups render correct element kinds and the active toggle computes --color-secondary; NotFound's mt-6 computes 21px = the 1.5rem it replaced. Gates: lint 0 errors (5 pre-existing warnings), typecheck clean, 456 tests / 51 files green.

title: Migrate btn strings to <Button>: pages/admin/**
description:
Depends on the Button primitive story. Mechanical migration, one directory per session so each diff stays reviewable.

Scope: web/src/pages/Admin.tsx and web/src/pages/admin/*.tsx (UsersTab, APIKeysTab, NamespacesTab, SourcesTab, StatusTab, JobsTab). SourcesTab alone carries Add Registry / Edit / Scan / Force / Delete on every row.

Verify: make frontend-lint-fix && make frontend-lint && make frontend-typecheck && make frontend-test. Visual pass over each admin tab in both themes.
notes:
Files: pages/admin/{APIKeysTab,NamespacesTab,SourcesTab,JobsTab}.tsx, pages/admin/sources/{WebhookSecretBanner,RegistryFormDialog,registryColumns}.tsx, pages/admin/jobs/{EnrichmentJobsView,ScanJobsView,jobCells}.tsx, web/src/buttonAdoption.test.ts (new), pages/ComponentOverview/index.tsx (dead-class removal only)
Approach: scripted tag rewrite (scratchpad/btn.py) — parse each <button> opening tag, map its class list onto Button props (btn-primary->variant, btn-sm->size, bare btn->default secondary), drop the class attr, rewrite the matching </button>. 26 sites across 10 files. pages/Admin.tsx itself had zero btn strings — its tab strip is <A> links with inline styles, which is ocidex-ag4q.39.
Two unstyled <button style={{cursor:pointer}}> sort headers (EnricherHealthMatrix, jobCells) are deliberately not Buttons: they carry no .btn class and are not actions.
Three sites hand-rolled a small size inline (0.75rem/0.8rem + tight padding) instead of .btn-sm; converted to size="sm".
Verification: visual fidelity is by construction rather than by screenshot — Button emits identical class strings against unchanged CSS, and Button.test.tsx already asserts the exact strings plus that every emittable class has a stylesheet rule. The admin surfaces themselves cannot be loaded on the :3100 prod proxy (signed-out only), so no browser pass was possible; stated rather than claimed.
New guard: buttonAdoption.test.ts walks pages/admin recursively and fails on any raw btn class string; MIGRATED grows as .20/.21 land. Mutation-verified. It caught a live btn-secondary on ComponentOverview's all-versions link — a class no rule defines, exactly the failure Button.tsx's doc comment predicted; dead string removed, the <Button> migration there stays in .21.

title: Inline-style triage: extract the repeated ones
description:
207 inline style={{}} across web/src/**/*.tsx. They are the main reason the same visual idea looks slightly different on every page.

Change: sweep all of them. Any style object repeated 3 or more times becomes a utility class in index.css's @layer components (or a Tailwind utility where one already exists). Genuine one-offs stay inline.

Known clusters to look at first:
- pages/Admin.tsx:78-89 — the hand-rolled tab strip (also covered by its own story; coordinate)
- flex/gap row wrappers
- muted-text spans that should use an existing token class

Record the before/after count in the issue notes so the next session knows what is left. This story may be split if 207 is too many for one session — if so, close it with a note and file the remainder.

Verify: make frontend-lint + frontend-typecheck + frontend-test green; grep -ro 'style={{' --include=*.tsx web/src | wc -l has dropped materially.
notes:
Files: 33 .tsx under web/src (sweep), web/src/components/Skeleton.{tsx,css,test.tsx}
Approach: scripted sweep (scratchpad/sweep.py) — parse each style={{...}}, locate the enclosing JSX opening tag, merge the equivalent class into an existing static class= or insert one, delete the style attr. 15 shapes at >=3x mapped to Tailwind utilities plus the hand-written .text-muted.
Before/after: 177 occurrences / 105 distinct -> 100 / 90, with zero shapes remaining at >=3x. One dynamic class={} site converted by hand (registryColumns.tsx trust badge).
Verified in the browser on :3100 rather than trusting the stylesheet: mb-4 computes 14px (was 1rem), text-xs 10.5px (was 0.75rem), text-muted and card.mb-4 resolve on /vulnerabilities/CVE-*.
Deliberate value change: font-size: 0.85rem -> text-sm ships 0.8rem (11.2px, -0.7px) at 12 sites, merging them into the ~70 already on that class.
Trap found: <Skeleton class="inline-block"> is inert — .skeleton { display: block } in Skeleton.css is UNLAYERED, and unlayered CSS beats @layer utilities regardless of source order. Replaced with an inline prop backed by .skeleton-inline in the same unlayered file, plus a contract test (mutation-verified: flipping the declaration fails it, and the test strips comments so the prose mentioning inline-block does not rescue it).
Follow-up filed: ocidex-ag4q.53 — .text-sm is hand-written in index.css and shadows the --text-sm token the @theme comment claims backs it.

title: Bound the main content column
description:
components/Layout.css declares .main-content { flex: 1; padding: 2rem } with NO max-width. Measured on a 2200px window: the column is 1220px of usable content stretched across the full field, so tables become unreadably wide rows of mostly whitespace.

Change: add max-width and centering to .main-content (start at 1600px; the widest legitimate content is the 9-column Sources table and ClusterDetail's Workloads table — check both before settling on the number).

Verify: firefox MCP set_viewport_size to 2200px wide, evaluate getBoundingClientRect().width on .main-content -> capped, content centered. Then check 1440x900 is unaffected.
notes:
Files: web/src/components/Layout.css, web/src/typeScale.test.ts.

Approach: max-width 1600px + margin-inline auto on .main-content. Number chosen by measuring, not by feel: temporarily widened the column to 4000px in the browser and read each table's min-content width -- /artifacts (4 cols) 359px, /vulnerabilities (7 cols) 803px. The app's widest is admin Sources at 9 columns, unreachable from the signed-out prod-proxy rig, so 1600 was set to clear it with room. The pre-existing overflow-x: auto means the cap degrades to scrolling rather than clipping for anything wider.

Verify: browser at 2200x1000 -> column 1600px, centred with 190px symmetric gutters beside the sidebar, no body h-scroll. At 1440x900 -> 1220px, identical to the uncapped measurement, so nothing below the cap moved.

Caught a real flaw in the guard while writing it: typeScale.test.ts's rule() helper included CSS comments, so 'centres it rather than pinning it left' passed with margin-inline deleted -- it was matching the comment that explains margin-inline. rule() now strips comments, and all three new assertions were mutation-verified independently. 449 frontend tests pass.

title: Give --color-primary and --color-secondary a semantic rule
description:
--color-primary (red #DC3545, 30 uses) and --color-secondary (blue #5B8DEF, 17 uses) are currently used interchangeably, so nothing in the UI signals what red means. The sidebar brand slab, active tab underlines, and destructive buttons all share it.

Change: document the rule in a comment in index.css's @theme block and retag the offenders —
  red   = brand chrome (sidebar, --color-entry-edge) and destructive actions only
  blue  = interactive affordances: links, active states, focus
Note --color-info is already the same hex as --color-secondary; collapse or alias them deliberately rather than leaving the duplicate.

Verify: grep counts of color-primary / color-secondary shift toward the rule; visual pass over /admin, /artifacts, /diff in both themes.
notes:
Files: web/src/index.css (rule doc + --color-info alias + --color-severity-critical), web/src/colorSemantics.test.ts (new), and 13 retagged call sites across components/ and pages/.

Approach: Defined the split as red = identity and consequence (brand chrome, .btn-primary/.btn-danger), blue = navigation and state (links, active tabs/tiles, selected filters, focus). That is the version of the rule that survives contact with the code: .btn-primary is an affirmative CTA at all 17 of its call sites, none destructive, so 'red = destructive only' would have repainted every Save/Add button blue for no gain.

Retagged to blue: .tab-bar button.active, .tile.active, .sidebar nav a.active, .theme-icon.active, .copy-btn:hover, .dash-row-title/.dash-link hovers, .link-button, 3 landing-page hovers, Admin.tsx tab strip, JobsTab activeStyle, EnricherHealthMatrix selection, jobCells link button. Kept red: sidebar slab + gradient, wordmark (Home/Login), spinner, entry-edge, btn-primary. Counts moved 30->19 red, 17->39 blue.

Two collisions found while retagging, both fixed: .sev-critical was painted var(--color-primary), so restyling the brand would silently restyle the top of the severity redscale (now --color-severity-critical, same hex per theme); and JOB_STATE_COLORS named --color-error which has never existed, falling through to a hardcoded #e53e3e fallback no theme could override (now --color-danger). --color-info collapsed to var(--color-secondary) rather than a duplicate hex. Admin.css stat-card edge now names --color-entry-edge instead of re-specifying it. registryColumns' inline red badge became class=badge badge-primary, removing an inline style.

Verify: colorSemantics.test.ts (8 cases) asserts brand red is unreachable outside 5 named brand files, that the 4 active-state selectors use blue, that status vocabularies do not borrow the brand, and that --color-info is an alias. Mutation-verified: reintroducing red on the active tab, and adding var(--color-primary) to a new file, each fail it. Browser: /artifacts, /artifacts/:id, /diff in both themes -- tokens resolve per theme (#DC3545/#5B8DEF dark, #CC1429/#2563EB light); on /diff exactly 2 elements paint red, the sidebar slab and the one primary CTA. /admin not visually checked (prod-proxy rig is signed-out only); its retags are covered by lint/typecheck/tests. 439 frontend tests pass.

title: DataTable refetch dims instead of flashing to skeletons
description:
R7.

DataTable renders skeletonBody(rows().length) whenever loading && rows !== undefined, and every list on the cluster page passes isFetching. Sorting, paging, or typing in the debounced filter blanks the whole table. App-wide behaviour (Vulnerabilities, Components, Licenses all pass isFetching too), but the cluster page is the most filter-heavy in the app.

- components/DataTable.tsx: on refetch keep rendering the rows and mark the wrapper aria-busy with a dimming class, instead of swapping in skeletonBody. First load keeps its skeleton.
- Assertion in components/DataTable.test.tsx.
notes:
Files: web/src/components/DataTable.tsx, DataTable.css, DataTable.test.tsx
Approach: Dropped the isRefetching() -> skeletonBody(rows.length) swap; the card now carries classList={{'table-refetching'}} + aria-busy and the CSS dims .table-wrapper to 0.55 opacity with a 120ms transition (disabled under prefers-reduced-motion). isFirstLoad keeps its skeleton — nothing to keep there. Rewrote the test that pinned the old swap into one asserting the rows survive, no skeletons appear, and aria-busy flips; added a first-load-still-shimmers test beside it. App-wide change: 310 frontend tests green.

title: Gaps tab stops truncating silently at 200
description:
R6.

GapsTab requests limit: 200 for unknown images and for unresolvable workloads and renders no pagination. ListClusterUnknownImages has no offset and no count query, so a cluster past 200 unknown images shows a short list with no indication it is short - the same class of quiet omission K5 exists to prevent.

- ListClusterUnknownImages gains offset; add CountClusterUnknownImages; thread pagination through service, API types and useClusterUnknownImages.
- Both Gaps tables get DataTable pagination.
- OverviewTab's ready/blocked line reads the same query, so it must count from pagination.total, not from the page it happens to hold.
notes:
Files: db/queries/cluster.sql, internal/service/cluster_ingest.go, internal/service/cluster.go, internal/api/{cluster.go,types_cluster.go}, web/src/api/queries/clusters.ts, web/src/pages/ClusterDetail/{GapsTab,OverviewTab,index.test}.tsx, tests/cluster_inventory_test.go
Approach: Deviated from the plan's 'add OFFSET + CountClusterUnknownImages'. Ingestability is decided in Go against the namespace's registries, so no SQL aggregate can produce the per-reason tally, and that tally has to describe the whole gap rather than the page. Removed LIMIT from ListClusterUnknownImages entirely, resolve the gap whole, tally reasons, slice the page in Go (pageOf helper). Not a new cost class: IngestUnknown already resolved the gap whole on every run, and the count query the plan wanted would have been a second pass anyway.
Response gains reasons{ready,no_registry,registry_disabled,pattern_excluded,unparseable_ref} + pagination; input swaps its bare Limit for PaginationParams. GapsTab pages both tables at 50 with local offset signals (not search params: it is a review workflow and would have been the only URL state on the tab), and its bulk button + 'N of M can be ingested' line now read reasons.ready/pagination.total. OverviewTab drops to limit:1 since it only needs the totals.
Verified: make check green, openapi-check/generate-client-check clean, frontend-lint 0 errors, tsc clean, 47 ClusterDetail vitest pass, go test ./tests/ -run Cluster ok against real Postgres (adds page-seam, past-the-end and short-page assertions).

title: Coverage counts say what they count
description:
R4.

GetClusterWorkloadCoverage is COUNT(*) over cluster_workload rows, i.e. workload-containers, but the Containers tile sub-label reads 'running, deduplicated per image'. These are the denominators ADR-044 K5 requires beside every vulnerability figure.

- db/queries/cluster.sql GetClusterWorkloadCoverage: add SUM(w.pod_count) AS pods. make generate.
- WorkloadCoverageResponse.Pods in internal/api/types_cluster.go; service passthrough in internal/service/cluster.go. make openapi + make generate-client.
- CoverageBand.tsx: Containers sub-label becomes 'workload containers . N pods'; drop 'deduplicated per image'.
- Extend the coverage assertion in tests/cluster_api_test.go:216-219.

Additive only: existing coverage assertions stay green and ADR-044 needs no amendment.
notes:
Files: db/queries/cluster.sql (GetClusterWorkloadCoverage +SUM(pod_count)), internal/service/cluster.go (WorkloadCoverage.Pods), internal/api/types_cluster.go + cluster.go (new toCoverageResponse helper, was two copies), web/src/pages/ClusterDetail/CoverageBand.tsx + index.tsx, tests/cluster_api_test.go
Approach: coverage keeps counting workload-containers (the unit the match states partition, so the K5 denominator) and states that in the label; pods is a second additive figure. Regenerated sqlc/openapi/client/auth-matrix.

title: Shared surface: card header layout and tile band consolidation
description:
R2a + R5.

.card-header is justify-content: space-between (index.css:269) and CardHeader emits h3 + badge + actions as three flex children, so the count badge is marooned in the middle of the header. The only two call sites passing both count and actions are OverviewTab.tsx:39 and GapsTab.tsx:194.

- ClusterDetail.css:11-69 (.coverage-band/.coverage-tile*) is a near-copy of SummaryBand.css:1-70. Extract the band + tile CSS into one stylesheet imported by both. CoverageBand keeps rendering <A>, SummaryBand keeps rendering <button> - only the CSS is shared.
