Band/tile CSS extracted to TileBand.css imported by both callers; .summary-tile*/.coverage-tile* rules deleted, cluster keeps only its gap colour, larger value size and wrapping sub-label as modifiers on the shared classes. Selection class renamed selected -> active; tests updated.

title: Ingest surface in the UI + ADR-044 amendment
description: Overview shows the last ingest outcome; Gaps gets the bulk button and per-row action; cluster settings get the auto_ingest toggle. Append an ADR-044 amendment recording auto-ingest: trigger, the namespace-scoping rule, and why unmatched hosts are reported rather than retried.
notes:
Files: web/src/pages/ClusterDetail/{GapsTab,OverviewTab,index}.tsx, web/src/pages/Clusters.tsx, web/src/api/queries/clusters.ts + client.ts, internal/service/cluster_ingest.go, internal/api/{cluster,types_cluster}.go, docs/adr/0044-k8s-inventory-agent.md, docs/CLUSTER_INVENTORY.md
Approach: Backend prerequisite first — added IngestUnknownParams.ImageDigests, an optional filter applied in Go after resolveUnknownImages, so the per-row Ingest button queues the image it points at instead of the whole cluster (the committed endpoint ingests the whole gap). Frontend: useIngestUnknown mutation shared by the bulk button and the row buttons, one pending signal so only the clicked row shows its own label; ingestSummary names every skip reason separately rather than reporting 'queued N of M' (K5 applied to ingest). Overview gained an autoIngest prop and an Ingest card stating on/off plus ready-vs-blocked counts — deliberately no 'last run at' since nothing persists an attempt timestamp. Clusters list shows auto_ingest per row and edits it through the same Save as a rename (a stray table click must not spend registry credentials). ADR-044 rule K9 records the amendment and amends the 'gaps forever' consequence; docs/CLUSTER_INVENTORY.md is the user-facing guide, linked from DEPLOYMENT.md and CLAUDE.md. 9 new frontend tests (34 ClusterDetail, 10 Clusters); 293 frontend tests pass, make check + openapi/client/auth-matrix checks green.

title: Gaps tab
description: Two sections because the remedies differ: No SBOM (valid digest, never ingested) and Unresolvable (no digest readable — a node runtime problem; link the ADR-044 K3 table). Each No-SBOM row shows its resolved registry, or 'no registry configured for <host>' with a link to registry creation, plus per-row and bulk Ingest actions.
notes:
Files: db/queries/cluster.sql (ListClusterUnknownImages), db/queries/registry.sql (ListRegistriesByNamespace), internal/service/cluster_ingest.go (new: UnknownImage, resolveIngestTarget, SplitImageRef, NormalizeRegistryHost, Registry.Host) + cluster_ingest_test.go, internal/scanner/catalog.go (delegates normalizeRegistryHost), internal/api/{types_cluster,cluster,router,authclass}.go, web/src/pages/ClusterDetail/GapsTab.tsx, web/src/api/queries/clusters.ts (useClusterUnknownImages).
Approach: new GET /api/v1/clusters/{id}/unknown-images groups the No-SBOM gap by image (the unit of the remedy) and resolves each against registries in the cluster's OWN namespace only — cross-namespace would mean pulling with another namespace's credentials. Reason is a five-value enum (ready/no_registry/registry_disabled/pattern_excluded/unparseable_ref) rather than a boolean because each has a different remedy; the matched registry is named even when disabled or pattern-excluding, since 'ghcr is off' is only actionable if you know it is ghcr. Reuses Registry.MatchesRepository. Host normalisation consolidated into internal/service (scanner imports service, not vice versa) so the ingest matcher and the scanner cannot disagree. Story 8 reuses resolveIngestTarget to actually submit; per-row/bulk buttons land in story 9.

title: Image reference quality: prefer the spec image over a bare image ID
description:
cmd/k8s-agent/inventory.go buildSnapshot only falls back to the pod spec when containerStatuses[].image is empty. containerd often reports a bare 'sha256:<hex>' local image ID there, which renders as an unreadable hash in the UI.

Add displayRef(status, spec) preferring the spec image when the status image is a bare identifier (sha256:… or 64 hex chars). Table-driven test next to normalizeImageID's.
Frontend: render repo:tag with a short digest suffix; when the ref is still a bare identifier, say 'name not reported by runtime' rather than printing 71 chars of hex.
notes:
Files: cmd/k8s-agent/inventory.go, cmd/k8s-agent/inventory_test.go, web/src/utils/oci.ts (+oci.test.ts), web/src/pages/ClusterDetail.tsx
Approach: displayRef(statusImage, specImage) falls back to the pod spec whenever containerStatuses[].image is blank OR matches bareIDRe (^(sha256:)?[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$) — containerd puts the local image ID there. Preference is one-directional: a named status value is the resolved name (post-webhook/image-policy) and wins over the spec. Frontend imageRefName() returns null for a bare id so the cell renders 'name not reported by runtime' instead of hex; table-driven Go test + vitest cover both.

title: OpenAPI resource, packaging and docs for the MCP server
description: Expose web/openapi.json as an MCP resource so schema-aware agents can discover the full API surface beyond the curated tools. Package the binary: Makefile build target, a release artifact in the existing release flow, and a Docker stage only if a hosted use case emerges - the chosen shape is local stdio, so a container is not required by default. Document setup in docs/ including the claude mcp add invocation and the ocidex-cli login prerequisite. Verify the whole server end to end against a make dev-up stack rather than only against fake_client, since the generated-client-to-live-API path is exactly where a stubbed test would pass and reality would not.
acceptance_criteria: OpenAPI spec available as an MCP resource; make build produces the binary and it is in the release flow; setup documented with the claude mcp add invocation; every tool exercised against a live make dev-up stack and the results recorded on the issue.
notes:
Files: cmd/ocidex-mcp/resources.go + resources_test.go (ocidex://openapi.json resource), pkg/client/openapi.go + client.go + fake_client.go (GetOpenAPISpec), cmd/ocidex-mcp/analysis.go (ingest build_date), cmd/ocidex-mcp/catalog.go (component id in search output), .tektonic/jobs/sbom-push/spec.ts + regenerated .tekton/tasks/sbom-push.k8s.yaml, docs/MCP.md, README.md.

Approach: OpenAPI is fetched live from the target server, not embedded, so the spec can never disagree with the server the tools talk to. Packaging is the sbom-push shippedBinaries list, not a release asset (gh-release attaches none) and not an image (ADR-045 makes it local stdio); make build already produced the binary from .1.

Live verification (make dev-up's Talos+Tilt path was replaced by an equivalent real stack: dockerized postgres 16 + nats 2 with jetstream, migrated with 'ocidex migrate up', the API binary from this tree on :8098, seeded user/api-keys/namespace/source; the generated-client-to-live-API path is identical). All 14 tools driven over real stdio JSON-RPC against that server with two alpine fixture SBOMs, a licensed application SBOM and a seeded advisory:
- ok: whoami, lookup_artifact, get_artifact, lookup_sbom, lookup_license, search_components, list_namespaces, diff_sboms, diff_tree, artifact_changelog, artifact_vulnerabilities, component_vulnerabilities, get_vulnerability, ingest_sbom
- resource ocidex://openapi.json listed and read: OpenAPI 3.1.0, 77 paths
- ADR-042 409 ladder: name=dex matched container+application artifacts, tool returned both candidates with the separating qualifier; retry with type=container resolved
- read-only key: reads fine, ingest refused with the read-write scope message
- negative paths: 404 lookups, impossible-query rejections before any HTTP call

Three defects found only by the live run, all fixed: ingest lacked build_date (container SBOMs un-ingestable), search_components withheld the component id (component_vulnerabilities unreachable), and /api/v1/sboms/lookup 500'd on any SBOM without enrichment (filed and fixed as ocidex-klj4).

title: Diff, vulnerability and ingest tools
description: The analysis half of the tool set: SBOM diff and diff-tree, artifact and component vulnerability queries, artifact changelog, and SBOM ingest. Diff output is the one that needs care - the raw DiffTree response from ADR-021 carries roots, isDirect, direction, nodeRef and descendantChanges intended for a rendering frontend, and dumping it verbatim into an agent context is both large and hard to reason about. Summarise it into something an agent can act on, with the option to drill in. Ingest is the only write tool, so it must respect the read versus read-write API key scope and fail clearly rather than obscurely when the key is read-only.
acceptance_criteria: Diff tool returns an agent-legible summary with drill-down rather than the raw render-oriented tree; vulnerability tools resolve by artifact and by component; ingest respects API key scope and gives a clear error on a read-only key; unit tests via fake_client for each tool.
notes:
Files: cmd/ocidex-mcp/analysis.go, analysis_test.go, catalog.go (derefSlice), server.go; pkg/client/vulnerability.go, vulnerability_test.go, client.go, fake_client.go
Approach: seven tools. ocidex_diff_sboms returns the whole-diff summary counts plus a filtered/paged window of changes (selectChanges), with total and truncated so a model can tell a page from the answer; each change carries node_ref, the handle into the tree tool. ocidex_diff_tree is the drill-down the AC asked for: summariseTree collapses ADR-021's nodes/edges/roots/nodeRef payload into one level — without node it returns the direct dependencies sorted by total descendant changes (blast radius first, name as tiebreak); with node it returns that component's own change plus its direct children. Roots and edges are keyed by bom-ref while node_ref is a component id, so lookups accept either. ocidex_artifact_changelog returns per-step summaries plus the two SBOM ids rather than inlining changes, which would make a multi-version series unreadable; it echoes availableArchitectures/Flavors so the model learns the valid narrowing values from the response.
pkg/client had no vulnerability surface at all (types.go had the types, no methods), so added GetArtifactVulnSummary, GetComponentVulns and GetVulnerability (url.PathEscape on the advisory id) plus FakeClient fields and httptest tests. Those back ocidex_artifact_vulnerabilities (severity histogram, the cheap first question), ocidex_component_vulnerabilities (fixed_version omitted when no fix is published) and ocidex_get_vulnerability (blast radius across visible artifacts).
ocidex_ingest_sbom is the only write: Annotations.ReadOnlyHint=false so a gating client can see it, the bom passes through byte-for-byte (no re-encode), and ErrForbidden is intercepted before toolError to say the key cannot write, ingest needs read-write, re-run ocidex-cli login. Tests assert the annotation, the passthrough and the read-only-key message.
Gates: make check EXIT=0 (incl. generate-client-check with the new hand-written methods), golangci-lint 0 issues.

title: Watched-artifact change feed
description: A watchlist is only useful if it tells you when something changed. Build a feed over watched artifacts surfacing new versions, newly-affecting CVEs, and drift. The underlying signals already exist and should be reused rather than recomputed: the changelog service in internal/service/changelog.go covers version-to-version change, the drift history behind GET /api/v1/sboms/{id}/drift covers drift, and the vulnerability store covers CVEs. The work is joining those to the watch set and ordering by recency. Keep it a pull-based feed in this story - notifications by email or webhook are a separate concern and should be filed as follow-up rather than smuggled in here.
acceptance_criteria: Feed returns new versions, newly-affecting CVEs, and drift events for the caller's watched artifacts, newest first; it reuses changelog, drift-history and vulnerability queries rather than duplicating them; visibility is enforced so a since-privatised artifact drops out of the feed; pagination follows the ADR from ocidex-wp9b.5; follow-up issue filed for push notifications.
notes:
Files: db/queries/watch_feed.sql (new), internal/repository/watch_feed.sql.go (generated), internal/service/watch.go, internal/repository/repository.go, internal/api/{auth.go,types_auth.go,authclass.go}, web/src/api/queries/watches.ts, tests/watch_feed_test.go (new)

Approach: one ListWatchedArtifactEvents query, no new tables and no new migration. Three CTE branches over signals that already exist -- sbom rows (new_version), provenance_drift_events rows (drift), and the same component->package_vulnerability->vulnerability join the SBOM/artifact vuln panels use -- merged with UNION ALL onto one (occurred_at DESC, event_id DESC) timeline. Nothing is recomputed; the query only scopes existing rows to the watch set.

Three judgement calls worth reviewing:
1. Visibility IS re-checked here, unlike the watchlist. A watch is the user's bookmark and survives its artifact going private; events are content and must not keep streaming. Enforced once, in the visible_sbom CTE that all three branches read from, so no branch can bypass it. Recorded as noteWatchFeed in the auth matrix explicitly next to noteWatch, since the two disagreeing is the correct state.
2. 'Newly affecting' = GREATEST(v.published_at, sbom.created_at). package_vulnerability.updated_at is unusable -- the refresh loop delete-then-inserts every purl each cycle, so it would re-float the entire backlog to the top of the feed on every refresh. Vulns are reported against the latest visible SBOM only; fanning out per version re-emits the same CVE per tag.
3. Vuln events key on md5(canonical_id || artifact_id)::uuid so the cursor stays (timestamptz, uuid) like every other keyset feed rather than widening for one branch. Pagination is ADR-043 rule 2, reusing FeedPage + meCursorList from .3; each branch applies the cursor and takes row_limit before the merge so one noisy artifact cannot blow up the union.

Version events carry previousVersion (LAG window fn) so the UI deep-links to the existing changelog endpoint instead of restating the diff. sqlc types UNION columns from the first branch only, so previous_version is COALESCEd to '' everywhere and mapped back to nil in the service.

Frontend is the useWatchFeed query hook only -- rendering belongs to .5's dashboard shell. tests/watch_feed_test.go covers all three signals, latest-SBOM-only (control CVE on a purl in the superseded version does not appear), newest-first ordering, previousVersion linkage, self-scoping, the privatised-artifact drop-out with the watch surviving, and 401. Push notifications filed as follow-up ocidex-x5x8 rather than smuggled in.

title: Artifact watchlist: schema, endpoints, and star affordance
description: Users need to track artifacts they care about without owning them - a public base image they depend on, for instance. New goose migration adding artifact_watch with user_id, artifact_id, created_at and a unique constraint on the pair. Endpoints to add, remove, and list watches, all self-scoped like the API-key endpoints. Watching a PUBLIC artifact owned by someone else must be permitted, since that is the main use case; watching a private artifact the caller cannot see must not be. Add the star affordance to the artifact list and detail views using the components/ui primitives from ocidex-wp9b.9, with optimistic update through the existing query hook pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Migration applies and rolls back; a user can watch a public artifact they do not own but cannot watch one they cannot see; watch list is self-scoped; star toggles optimistically and survives reload; sqlc regenerated via make generate; Vitest coverage for the affordance.
notes:
Files: db/migrations/00058_artifact_watch.sql, db/queries/watch.sql, internal/service/watch.go, internal/api/{auth.go,types_auth.go,authclass.go,handler.go}, internal/service/{search.go,search_artifact.go,search_sbom.go}, web/src/api/queries/watches.ts, web/src/components/WatchStar.{tsx,test.tsx}, tests/watch_test.go

Approach: artifact_watch(user_id, artifact_id, created_at) composite PK, both FKs ON DELETE CASCADE, plus idx_artifact_watch_artifact for the .4 feed's who-watches-this direction. WatchService gates visibility exactly ONCE, at Watch(), via the existing artifact_visible() -> 404 not 403 so an invisible artifact is indistinguishable from a missing one. Unwatch and List deliberately do not re-check: re-filtering would make a watch silently vanish when its namespace flips private, with no way to clear it. Both verbs idempotent so an optimistic toggle can replay.

ArtifactDetail gained .watched so the star paints correct on first load and survives reload; skipped entirely for anonymous callers. Endpoints GET /users/me/watches (keyset, ADR-043 rule 2) + PUT/DELETE /users/me/watches/{artifact_id} (204, write scope). service.ActivityPage and WatchPage were field-identical, so they were unified into service.FeedPage and both handlers rewritten on the new generic meCursorList[T] helper -- this was forced by dupl but is a real simplification that .4/.5's feeds reuse.

Verified: TestArtifactWatchMigrationRollsBack exercises the Down half (nothing else in the suite ever rolls back); TestArtifactWatchlist seeds a second tenant owning both a public and a private namespace so watch-what-I-don't-own and can't-watch-what-I-can't-see are both real cases. 6 Vitest cases on WatchStar. Full make check green.

title: Package k8s-agent: Docker stage, Helm template, RBAC, Makefile
description: Ship the agent the same way the existing workers ship. Add a distroless gcr.io/distroless/static-debian13:nonroot stage to docker/Dockerfile mirroring the vuln-worker stage, per ADR-038's base image policy including Renovate pinDigests. Add charts/ocidex/templates/deployment-k8s-agent.yaml following deployment-scanner-worker.yaml, plus the ServiceAccount, ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding granting pod list and watch only. The agent is deployed into the TARGET cluster, not necessarily alongside OCIDex, so it likely needs its own minimal chart or a clearly gated values toggle - decide and document which. Add the Makefile build target and wire it into the existing build-all Docker stage.
acceptance_criteria: make build produces the k8s-agent binary; the image builds from docker/Dockerfile; make helm-check passes including PodSecurity restricted validation; RBAC is pod read-only; a target cluster can run the agent without OCIDex being deployed in it; deployment path documented in docs/DEPLOYMENT.md.
notes:
Files: docker/Dockerfile (build-all + k8s-agent distroless stage), Makefile (build target), charts/ocidex-k8s-agent/{Chart.yaml,values.yaml,templates/*}, scripts/helm-policy-check.sh, .tektonic/jobs/{image-build/spec.ts,sbom-push/spec.ts,helm-publish/publish.sh,helm-release/release.sh} + regenerated .tekton, docs/DEPLOYMENT.md, docs/CONFIGURATION.md.

Approach: SEPARATE chart (charts/ocidex-k8s-agent), not a gated toggle in charts/ocidex — the install target is a different cluster from OCIDex's (ADR-044 K1), so a toggle would mean installing a disabled copy of the whole server chart into every reported cluster and would couple release cadences. charts/ocidex-operator is the precedent. RBAC: pods list/watch cluster-wide only (ownership comes from ownerReferences + pod-template-hash, so no replicasets/jobs read); bound cluster-wide even when namespaces narrows reporting, since that allowlist is an app-level filter. Deployment sets maxSurge 0 — two agents on one cluster.id would make the stored inventory alternate between snapshots because each push replaces it (K7). CI: added k8s-agent to imageSpecs (synth wires image-build/image-release, and helm-release's runAfter picks it up automatically), shippedBinaries for SBOM upload, and both helm package/push scripts; helm-release resolves its scalar image.digest like the operator's.

Verified: make check exit 0; make build produces bin/k8s-agent; make helm-check lints 3 charts and runs kyverno over defaults + a configured render (PodSecurity restricted + writable-paths, negative control still rejected); helm package produces ocidex-k8s-agent-<ver>.tgz and the release.sh sed matches exactly one 'digest: ""' line; rendered image switches to @sha256 form with image.digest set; generated task carries TARGET=k8s-agent, IMAGE=ghcr.io/pfenerty/ocidex-k8s-agent.

NOT verified locally: the container image itself was not built — docker is unavailable in this env, and building it in-cluster via an ad-hoc TaskRun would publish a ghcr tag from an uncommitted tree. The stage is a line-for-line copy of the vuln-worker stage and the binary name/target agree, so the first push pipeline is the check.

title: Decompose the god files in internal/api and internal/service
description: tokensave reports equality 0.39 (gini 0.605, 'extreme inequality - god files likely'). internal/api/types.go is 1295 lines and already mentally split - it carries 37 banner comments - so splitting it along those existing boundaries into per-domain files mirroring the handler files (types_sbom.go, types_registry.go, types_search.go, ...) is nearly mechanical. Also split internal/service/changelog.go (1321 lines) and internal/service/sbom.go (1108). Note that per-FUNCTION complexity in production code is already fine: the worst prod function is internal/worker/enrichment/worker.go Run at cyclomatic 13 against the limit of 15, and everything ranked above it is a test function. This is an organisational problem, not a complexity one, so the work is moves and not rewrites. make openapi output must be byte-identical before and after - that is the regression test.
acceptance_criteria: internal/api/types.go is split into per-domain files aligned with the handler files; changelog.go and sbom.go are split along cohesive seams; make openapi and make generate-client produce zero diff; make check and make test-integration pass; tokensave_health equality dimension improves.
notes:
Files: internal/api/types.go -> types.go + 11 per-domain files (types_health/sbom/search/artifact/stats/auth/status/registry/jobs/namespace/source.go); internal/service/changelog.go -> changelog.go + changelog_candidates.go, difftree.go, version_compare.go, component_identity.go; internal/service/sbom.go -> sbom.go + sbom_components.go, sbom_metadata.go.

Approach: pure code motion — no declaration was rewritten, renamed, or reordered within its new file. types.go was split along the 37 banner comments it already carried, one file per handler file (types_sbom.go beside sbom.go, etc.); the shared pagination/cursor envelopes stay in types.go, which now carries a note explaining the convention. changelog.go was split along the four concerns it had grown into: candidate selection, the ADR-0021 diff tree, version ordering + upgrade/downgrade classification, and the ADR-0019 component identity/join key. sbom.go shed the bulk COPY insert path and the BOM metadata extraction, keeping ingest orchestration. Each new service file opens with a short note naming its seam and the ADR it implements.

Regression test per the acceptance criteria: make openapi and make generate-client produce zero diff on web/openapi.json, web/src/types/openapi.d.ts and pkg/client/types.go. make check green (gofmt, golangci-lint, unit tests with race). tokensave_health equality 0.39 -> 0.4186 (gini 0.605 -> 0.5814), off 'extreme inequality - god files likely' onto 'high inequality'.

Caveat: make test-integration compiles and runs but every case SKIPs here — no docker and no reachable postgres in this environment (neither TEST_POSTGRES_URL nor docker available). Given the change is code motion with byte-identical generated output, the unit suite plus the generated-output check is the coverage that actually applies; the integration suite still needs a real run in CI.

Still large and not in scope for this story: internal/api/router.go (30K) and internal/api/search.go (20K, which also carries the artifact, dashboard and system-status handlers).

title: Namespace and source CLI parity (ADR-039 follow-through)
description: The other half of the ADR-039 gap. cmd/ocidex-cli has artifact, component, job, key, login, registry, sbom, sbom_diff and version commands but no namespace or source command, even though pkg/client/namespace.go and pkg/client/source.go already exist. Add cmd/ocidex-cli/namespace.go and cmd/ocidex-cli/source.go on top of those SDK methods, following registry.go's command structure and the output/ package's table conventions. Note that pkg/client/types.go is oapi-codegen output guarded by make check - do not hand-edit it.
acceptance_criteria: ocidex-cli namespace list|get|create|update|delete and ocidex-cli source list|get|create|update|delete work against a live API; output follows the existing output/ table conventions; table-driven tests mirror registry_test.go using pkg/client/fake_client.go; make check clean.
notes:
Files: cmd/ocidex-cli/namespace.go, source.go, delete.go (all new), namespace_test.go, source_test.go (new), root.go (command registration + verbCreate/verbDeleteID vocabulary), registry.go/key.go/sbom.go (adopt the shared constants; registry delete moved onto newDeleteCmd).

Approach: built both nouns on the existing pkg/client SDK methods; pkg/client/types.go untouched (oapi-codegen output). namespace list/get/create/update/delete mirrors registry, including server-side by-name resolution via GetNamespaceByName for any non-UUID ref. namespace update sends only the flags actually given, since the PATCH is omit-to-keep, and rejects a no-flag invocation as a usage error. source get/update/delete take a UUID only: source names are unique just within a namespace and the API has no by-name resolver, so a name is a usage error rather than a client-side list-and-filter (the thing ADR-042 exists to avoid); source list --namespace does accept a name and resolves it to an id before filtering. source create makes an upload source (POST /sources is upload-only; OCI registry sources still come from registry create) and parses the resolved namespace id into the openapi_types.UUID the body wants.

golangci-lint dupl flagged the namespace/source delete pair, so the delete command body was extracted into newDeleteCmd(use, short, noun, resolve, del) in delete.go and registry delete adopted it too, giving one spelling of confirm/--yes/'deleted <id>' across nouns. goconst wanted 'create' and 'delete <id>' as constants; added verbCreate/verbDeleteID beside the existing verbList/verbGet in root.go and updated key.go and sbom.go to use them.

Tests: namespace_test.go (11 cases) and source_test.go (10 cases) table-driven against client.FakeClient via the existing runCLI harness — table rendering, -o json, by-name vs by-id routing, omit-to-keep PATCH bodies, required-flag usage exits, delete confirmation refusal without --yes, and ErrNotFound -> exit 3. make check green.

title: ADR: pagination convention, and apply it end to end
description: Two pagination conventions coexist with no stated rule. The API mixes offset (PaginationMeta) and cursor (CursorMeta) per-endpoint, and the frontend mirrors the split with Pagination.tsx (used by ArtifactDetail/VersionsTab.tsx, VulnerabilityDetail.tsx) and LoadMore.tsx (used by SBOMDetail/index.tsx, SBOMDetail/PackagesTab.tsx, Artifacts.tsx) chosen ad hoc. Record the rule as a short ADR - cursor for unbounded append-only feeds, offset for bounded countable lists - then apply it to the endpoints that violate it and align each frontend page's paging component with its endpoint's convention. Epics B, C and D all add list endpoints, so the rule needs to exist before they start.
acceptance_criteria: ADR recorded in docs/adr/; every list endpoint's pagination style matches the rule; each frontend list uses the paging component matching its endpoint; make openapi and make generate-client produce no unexpected diff.
notes:
Files: docs/adr/0043-pagination-convention.md (new), db/queries/provenance_drift.sql, internal/service/search.go + search_sbom.go, internal/api/types.go + search.go + registry.go, web/src/api/queries/{registries,sboms}.ts, CLAUDE.md ADR table.
Approach: Recorded ADR-043 as a three-step decision procedure keyed on the query's ORDER BY and write pattern, not a blanket preference. Rule 1: a mutable column in ORDER BY forces offset — keyset is ill-defined there, and the jobs lists genuinely hit this (they order by a CASE state bucket that changes under the client). Rule 2: append-at-head over an immutable ordering forces keyset. Rule 3: otherwise the UI decides (numbered pages/total => offset, Load-more => cursor). Classified all 16 paginated endpoints; only the two provenance drift feeds violated the rule, so those converted from OFFSET+COUNT(*) OVER() to keyset on (detected_at DESC, id DESC) with has_cursor/cursor_* nargs and row_limit+1 for HasMore. Added ID to ProvenanceDriftSummary (omitempty — the unpaginated GetLatestProvenanceDrift does not select it) since it is the cursor tiebreaker. Both frontend consumers read only .data, so the hook change was limit/offset -> limit/cursor at the type level only. make check EXIT=0.

title: Remove dead auth scaffolding and fix the pagination.go misnomer
description: Dead scaffolding sits on the auth path. Authenticate (internal/api/middleware.go:41) and RequireRole (middleware.go:117) have zero callers - only OptionalAuthenticate is wired in router.go:72. Authenticate additionally hardcodes the cookie name 'ocidex_session' while the live path uses the sessionCookieName const, so it is a decoy that will silently diverge from real behaviour. Delete both, plus publicPaths and any writeUnauthorized/writeForbidden left orphaned. Separately, internal/api/pagination.go contains no pagination at all - only a deprecated exported ParseUUID shim kept 'for backward compatibility with existing tests'. Delete the shim, update test callers to the unexported parseUUID, and move paginationMeta and cursorMeta out of search.go into pagination.go so the filename describes its contents.
acceptance_criteria: Authenticate, RequireRole, publicPaths and any orphaned write* helpers are gone; no deprecated exported ParseUUID remains; pagination.go contains paginationMeta and cursorMeta; tokensave_dead_code reports no dead functions in internal/api; make check passes.
notes:
Files: internal/api/middleware.go (deleted Authenticate, RequireRole, publicPaths, errUnauthorized, writeUnauthorized, writeForbidden), internal/api/pagination.go (ParseUUID shim deleted; paginationMeta + cursorMeta moved in), internal/api/search.go (helpers moved out), internal/api/parseuuid_test.go (new, package api), errors_test.go / pagination_test.go (external ParseUUID tests removed).
Approach: the two dead middlewares were the point — Authenticate read a hardcoded 'ocidex_session' cookie while the live path uses the sessionCookieName const, so it was a decoy that would have diverged silently on any rename. Deleting it orphaned publicPaths, errUnauthorized and both write* helpers, which went too. The parseUUID tests could not simply be repointed at the unexported function because every existing test file is package api_test, so they moved to a new internal test file; Go allows both packages in one directory. TestParseUUID_Invalid was renamed TestBadUUIDPathParamIsRejected — it exercises huma's path-param format validation, not parseUUID, and the old name hid that. tokensave_dead_code now reports only newTestHandlerWithPinger and newTestRouterFromHandler, both of which health_test.go calls (the graph does not resolve test-to-test edges); no production dead code remains in internal/api.

title: Route all VisibilityFilter construction through one constructor
description: A canonical helper exists and is bypassed. visibilityFilterFromContext (internal/api/search.go:28) is the correct constructor - it reads UserFromContext and returns a public-only filter for unauthenticated callers. But namespace.go:31, registry.go:112 and source.go:42 each hand-build service.VisibilityFilter{...} instead. Three hand-rolled copies of a security-relevant filter is exactly how a visibility bug ships. Move visibilityFilterFromContext out of search.go into a new internal/api/authz.go alongside the auth middlewares, and route all three call sites through it.
acceptance_criteria: visibilityFilterFromContext lives in internal/api/authz.go; no other file in internal/api constructs service.VisibilityFilter{} directly outside tests; existing visibility tests pass.
notes:
Files: internal/api/authz.go (new home for visibilityFilterFromContext), internal/api/authz_test.go (new source-scan guard), internal/api/search.go (constructor removed), namespace.go / registry.go / source.go (hand-rolled filters replaced).
Approach: moved the canonical constructor beside the auth middlewares and routed the three call sites through it. ListNamespaces and ListRegistries no longer bind 'user' at all — their defensive 401 became 'if _, ok := UserFromContext(ctx); !ok'; ListSources still binds it for the namespace-scoped canManageNamespace branch. Added TestVisibilityFilterHasOneConstructor, which scans the package's non-test .go files for 'service.VisibilityFilter{' outside authz.go — a blunt instrument, but a hand-rolled copy that is wrong-but-consistent passes every behavioural test written against the caller it was added for, so nothing else catches a fourth copy.

title: MCP server for agent access
description: Let agents query the catalog without hand-rolling HTTP. Shape chosen: cmd/ocidex-mcp, a standalone stdio MCP server wrapping the existing pkg/client SDK. That SDK is already generated from the OpenAPI spec and drift-guarded by make check (Makefile:58-66), so tool schemas stay in step with the API for free - no server changes, no new transport plumbing. The ADR-042 lookup resolvers are the natural core of the tool set: they are name-keyed rather than UUID-keyed, which is exactly what an agent can supply, and their 409-with-candidates response is usable disambiguation rather than an opaque error. Plus component search, artifact detail, SBOM diff, artifact vulnerabilities, namespace listing, and SBOM ingest. Auth reuses the CLI credential handling in cmd/ocidex-cli/config.go and login.go, so ocidex-cli login provisions the MCP server too. Tests run against pkg/client/fake_client.go, which already exists for exactly this purpose.
acceptance_criteria: cmd/ocidex-mcp builds and registers via claude mcp add; each tool is exercised against a make dev-up stack; lookup tools surface 409 candidate lists as actionable disambiguation; auth reuses ocidex-cli login credentials; unit tests cover every tool via fake_client; OpenAPI spec exposed as an MCP resource.

title: Kubernetes deployment inventory (standalone agent)
description: Connect running workloads to catalog data so a user can answer 'these three running Deployments carry CVE-X'. This is greenfield: the operator's CRDs are OCIRegistry, ScanRequest and APIKey only, and there is no workload or deployment model anywhere. Shape chosen: a standalone push-based reporting agent, not an operator controller and not pull-via-kubeconfig - it is decoupled from the operator and runs in clusters that do not want CRDs. cmd/k8s-agent is a per-cluster Deployment that watches Pods, reads running image digests from status.containerStatuses[].imageID, and pushes an inventory snapshot on an interval. Follows existing worker conventions: internal/config env loading, ADR-027 lifecycle logging, a distroless static-debian13 stage in docker/Dockerfile mirroring the vuln-worker stage, a charts/ocidex/templates/deployment-*.yaml, and a Makefile build target. New cluster and cluster_workload tables join to artifact BY DIGEST - ADR-040 guarantees sbom.digest is UNIQUE, which makes the join exact rather than heuristic, and is why this connector is cheap. Needs an ADR recording the decision and rejected alternatives.
acceptance_criteria: ADR recorded; cmd/k8s-agent builds, has a Docker stage and a chart template, and reports running image digests on an interval; cluster and cluster_workload schema joins to artifact by digest; POST /api/v1/clusters/{id}/inventory is API-key authenticated with an explicit auth class under Epic A's conformance test; workspace UI shows running workloads and vulnerabilities filtered to what is actually deployed; verified against make dev-cluster-up.

title: User workspace and owner-scoped actionable views
description: Give an owner a real view of their own data. Today there is no user-scoped anything: no my-namespaces, no my-artifacts, no watchlist, and UsersTab.tsx is a 2.3K admin role toggle. Worse, the genuinely actionable feeds are admin-only - /registries/drift-feed, /registries/trust-summary, and the scan/enrichment job listings all gate on admin, so an ordinary namespace owner cannot see drift, signing posture, or ingest health for their own artifacts. The substance of this epic is scoping, not new queries: the queries mostly exist and need owner-scoped variants filtered by visible_namespace_ids. Adds /api/v1/users/me/* resources, an artifact_watch table with a watched-artifact feed (new versions, new CVEs, drift), and a /dashboard workspace shell built on Epic A's components/ui primitives. Signed-in Home.tsx gains a personalized band alongside Epic B's public one.
acceptance_criteria: A namespace owner can see drift, trust summary, and ingest health for their own artifacts without admin role; /api/v1/users/me/* resources return only the caller's data; artifact watchlist persists and drives a change feed; /dashboard assembles these into a coherent workspace; integration tests prove a non-owner receives zero rows from every owner-scoped endpoint.

title: Public discovery home page
description: A landing page that demonstrates the product with real catalog data, safe for anonymous viewers. Today Home.tsx is five static feature cards plus a bare count band from GetDashboardStats; there is no popularity signal anywhere in the system. Derive ranking from data already present rather than adding telemetry: ADR-041 usages counts (how many SBOMs contain an artifact), version count, and scan recency. New GET /api/v1/discover returns top artifacts, recently updated artifacts, notable vulnerabilities by blast radius, and license spread. Every query is constrained to PUBLIC namespaces via the existing visible_namespace_ids SQL function - private data must never contribute to an anonymous-visible aggregate. These are expensive aggregates, so compute them through the existing stats_cache.go + stats_warmer.go pattern including the warming payload state Home.tsx already handles. The anonymous response is identical for every caller and is therefore edge-cacheable.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/v1/discover returns live ranked catalog content; an integration test asserts a private-namespace artifact never appears for an anonymous caller or an authenticated non-owner; aggregates are warmed through stats_warmer rather than computed per-request; Home.tsx renders live content built on Epic A's ui primitives and handles the warming state.

title: README quick-start seeding fails: .env.example ships scanner/poller disabled
description:
Following the README Quick Start on a fresh clone (cp .env.example .env; docker compose up -d; make seed) fails at the first step of seeding. Every registry POST is rejected 422:

  scan_mode 'poll' and 'both' require REGISTRY_POLLER_ENABLED=true
  registry type "ghcr" requires polling, but REGISTRY_POLLER_ENABLED is not set

Cause: scripts/seed.nu's registry table uses scan_mode: "poll" for all six entries, and the three ghcr entries require polling unconditionally regardless of scan_mode. But .env.example ships SCANNER_ENABLED=false (line 57) and REGISTRY_POLLER_ENABLED commented out (line 64), and the API validates both at registry-create time.

It works today only because a developer's existing .env happens to set both true — the local .env does. A fresh clone does not. Found while verifying ocidex-8wun on a native stack, where the API was started without them.

Options: (a) flip .env.example to SCANNER_ENABLED=true + REGISTRY_POLLER_ENABLED=true, (b) have seed.nu preflight the config and fail with an actionable message naming both vars, (c) both. (b) is in the spirit of ocidex-y19y's fail-loudly requirement — the 422 detail is already good, but seed.nu reports it as six FAIL lines then a generic 'check that the API key has write scope', which misdirects.

Note the failure IS loud and non-zero (make exits 1), so ocidex-y19y's core fix holds.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh clone following README Quick Start can run make seed successfully, or seed.nu fails with a message naming REGISTRY_POLLER_ENABLED/SCANNER_ENABLED
notes:
Files: .env.example (SCANNER_ENABLED=true, uncommented REGISTRY_POLLER_ENABLED=true, reworded both comment blocks); scripts/seed.nu (new scanner-disabled/scanner-disabled-msg helpers; create loop returns a record with status+body on failure instead of null; terminal error is cause-specific; scan loop counts 202s and fails immediately when none succeed).

Approach: fixed both halves. (a) .env.example was the only place disagreeing with the rest of the stack — docker-compose starts scanner-worker unconditionally and charts/ocidex/values.yaml already defaults both flags to true. Code defaults in internal/config/config.go left at envDefault:false (user's call) so docs/CONFIGURATION.md and the config tests stay accurate and no existing deployment starts polling on upgrade. Tilt is unaffected either way: the chart sets both as explicit env: entries, which beat envFrom.

(b) .env.example only helps clones made after this lands, so seed.nu now reads the errors the API already returns. Detection matches the substrings REGISTRY_POLLER_ENABLED / 'scanner not enabled' rather than status codes, so a genuine 422 from payload validation still gets the generic message. Rejected a GET /admin/status preflight: it is admin-gated, so a member-scoped key would 403 and learn nothing.

Second gate found during research: registry.go:493-495 returns 503 when SCANNER_ENABLED=false, so fixing only the poller flag would have left seed.nu waiting out the full 600s artifact poll before blaming scanner-worker. The scan loop now fails in <1s.

Verified against a throwaway python stub API (scratchpad, not committed), 5 cases: 422 create -> new message, exit 1, 1s; 503 scan -> new message, exit 1, 0s (was 600s); 403 -> old generic write-scope message unchanged; happy path -> full run to the closing banner; 409 -> EXISTS resolve path still works. Plus 'set -a; . ./.env.example' confirming both vars export as true. Docker daemon still wedged on this host so the compose path itself was not exercised.

Follow-up filed: ocidex-wur3 (README From Source says cp .env.example .env but no Go binary reads it).

title: Scanner queues cosign .sig artifacts it cannot scan, burning retries
description:
With ocidex-gsip fixed, the scanner-worker's remaining failures are a single distinct class:

  oci-registry: unsupported layer media type(s): layer 0: application/vnd.dev.cosign.simplesigning.v1+json

The catalog walk enqueues cosign signature tags (sha256-<digest>.sig) as if they were images. syft cannot catalog them — the layer media type is a signature payload, not a filesystem layer — so each one fails all 3 attempts and lands in 'failed'. 47 such failures in the 10 minutes after the gsip fix was verified.

This was completely masked by ocidex-gsip: while every scan died at 'mkdir /tmp: read-only file system', the .sig jobs failed for that reason instead of this one. Fixing gsip is what made this the top failure mode.

Impact is retry burn and failed-row noise, not lost data — real images scan fine.

Fix direction: filter signature/attestation artifacts out at catalog-walk time rather than discovering them at scan time. internal/scanner/catalog.go already reads each manifest's config and media types (see mediatypes.go); the cosign tag scheme (sha256-*.sig, *.att, *.sbom) and the OCI 1.1 referrers artifactType are both available there. internal/enrichment/provenance/provenance.go:31-32 already has the artifact-type constants.
notes:
Files: internal/scanner/mediatypes.go (attached-artifact media types + prefixes), internal/scanner/discover.go (IsAttachedArtifactTag, isAttachedArtifactType), internal/scanner/catalog.go (walkRepo tag skip; ociManifest.isAttachedArtifact; imageMetadata.attachedArtifact; skips in scanTag/scanIndex/discoverUntagged/submitUntaggedIndex), internal/api/webhook.go, tests in walk_test.go/discover_test.go/webhook_test.go (new).

Approach: two checks before Submit. (1) cosign tag scheme regex ^[a-z0-9]+-[0-9a-f]{32,}\.(sig|att|sbom)$ — short-circuits before the manifest HEAD/GET, which cost 2-3 requests per .sig tag. (2) manifest content: artifactType, config.mediaType, layers[].mediaType matched against cosign/sigstore/in-toto/DSSE types, read from the manifest GET ociGetImageMetadata already does, so zero extra requests and it also catches referrers-API artifacts with arbitrary tags. imageMetadata.attachedArtifact is only ever set on positive identification, never as an error default — ociGetImageMetadata returns the zero value on failure.

Webhook path fixed too: its media-type filter passes cosign sigs because they ARE image manifests; tag is the only signal available there.

Refactors forced by gocyclo (limit 15): extracted submitUntaggedIndex from discoverUntagged (16 -> under) and ociManifest + isAttachedArtifact method from ociGetImageMetadata (18 -> under).

Verified: make check green (fmt, golangci-lint, unit tests, helm-check). Not yet verified on ocidex-dev — needs a deploy, then confirm 0 new 'unsupported layer media type' failures.

Scoped out: ocidex-9eu4 (jobqueue non-retryable-error concept).

title: Add helm lint + PodSecurity render check to CI
description:
Nothing in the Makefile or .tektonic/ lints or renders the Helm charts, so chart defects reach a live cluster before anyone notices. This has now cost twice:

- ocidex-1d9: PodSecurity violations shipped and were caught only by a manual server-side dry-run.
- ocidex-gsip: readOnlyRootFilesystem broke every image scan for six days with no signal.

A render-time check would not have caught ocidex-gsip (it needs a real scan), but it would have caught the ocidex-1d9 class and would guard the ocidex-s3tu fix from regressing.
design:
Add a 'make helm-lint' target running 'helm lint' over charts/ocidex and charts/ocidex-operator, plus a render check that pipes 'helm template' through a PodSecurity validator.

The dry-run recipe used in ocidex-1d9 and ocidex-s3tu needs a live cluster (kubectl apply --dry-run=server into a namespace labelled pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted), which CI does not have. Either use a cluster-free policy checker over the rendered YAML, or accept a kind/Talos step. Decide which before implementing.

Include the negative control as part of the test — render with the securityContext values nulled and assert the check FAILS. Both prior verifications relied on that to prove the check had teeth, and a silently-passing lint is worse than none.

Wire it as a tektonic PR job gated on onChanges for charts/**, matching how the Go jobs are gated.
acceptance_criteria:
1. make helm-lint passes on the current charts.
2. The check fails when a workload's securityContext is removed (negative control is part of the suite, not a manual step).
3. Runs in the PR pipeline, gated on charts/** changes.
notes:
VERIFIED IN CLUSTER (ad-hoc TaskRun in ocidex-ci, pvc-4705d99d2b, with the podTemplate securityContext block). Both polarities of the exit-code contract confirmed:
- failing run: exit-code=1, state=failure, TaskRun StepFailed
- passing run: exit-code=0, state=success, TaskRun Succeeded
CI counts match the local run exactly (22/22/18/2 pass across the four renders, 18/18 kyverno test, negative control rejected).

Gotcha found only by running it in-cluster: Wolfi's kyverno-cli package installs the CLI as a kubectl plugin, so the binary in the image is kubectl-kyverno, while the nixpkgs build Flox provides calls it kyverno. The script now resolves whichever is present rather than pinning one and breaking the other environment (commit 184f11b). ghcr.io/pfenerty/apko-cicd/kyverno:1.18.1-helm4 is published (apko-cicd-9sa, merged to apko-cicd main as 389e7f7).

Remaining: none. Branch ocidex-9yq4 is ready to merge to main.

title: govulncheck-scan has been red on main since before ocidex-im4o
description:
The govulncheck-scan GitHub check reports failure on main and has done so for at least three consecutive push runs: a74d0ae7, b67b5494 (previous origin/main), and f041bc2 (the ocidex-im4o merge). The scan step exits 1 - govulncheck's 'reachable vulnerabilities found' code - not 99, so this is a genuine finding and NOT the memoryWatchdog firing or an OOM.

Confirmed pre-existing: it predates ocidex-im4o, which only changed how failures are reported, not what govulncheck finds. The report-only design is working correctly here (TaskRun Succeeded, GitHub check red, PipelineRun green).

CI step logs are GC'd after ~18h, so reproduce locally: flox activate -- bash -c 'export PATH="$HOME/go/bin:$PATH"; govulncheck ./cmd/...'
acceptance_criteria: Either the reachable vulnerability is remediated (dep bump) and govulncheck-scan goes green on a push to main, or the finding is documented as accepted with a rationale.
notes:
Files: .govulncheck-accepted.json (new), .tektonic/jobs/go-vulncheck/spec.ts, .tekton/tasks/govulncheck-scan.k8s.yaml (generated), docs/DEVELOPMENT.md, .gitignore

Approach: govulncheck has no native ignore flag, so the task now runs -format sarif (always exits 0; one result per vuln with level error=called / warning=imported / note=required) and computes the verdict itself in nushell against a repo-root .govulncheck-accepted.json, read from the checkout at runtime so edits need no tekton-synth. Fails on any un-accepted level:error result; ALSO fails when an accepted ID stops being reported, so the allowlist cannot outlive its justification. Uses error make, never exit (ocidex-es6 trap). Added uploadSarifStep + sourceBranchParam for the Security tab.

Allowlist has exactly one entry: GO-2026-5932 (golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp, upstream 'Fixed in: N/A'), reached only via internal/enrichment/provenance -> cosign/v3 -> rekor/pkg/types/rekord/v0.0.1 -> rekor/pkg/pki/pgp. Confirmed unfixable: cosign v3.1.3 and rekor v1.5.3 are the newest available and still carry it; PGP is structural to rekor v1's rekord type. Documented rule: stdlib findings are NEVER accepted.

CORRECTION to the earlier note on this issue: the '5 fixable by toolchain bump' claim was an artifact of the local Flox go1.26.3. The CI image already ships go1.26.6 (apko-cicd origin/main pins go-1.26 1.26.6-r0; the 1.26.5-r1 reading came from a stale local feature branch). No apko-cicd change is needed and the govulncheckImage tag does not move. Local scan on go1.26.3 showed 13 reachable; the real image shows 1.

Verified by ad-hoc TaskRun in ocidex-ci on main HEAD 58b39ab, with the full podTemplate securityContext: 3 findings / 1 reachable / 1 accepted -> report-status exit-code=0 state=success, sarif upload 202. Re-run with an emptied allowlist -> 'error [govulncheck-scan]: 1 unaccepted reachable vulnerabilities: GO-2026-5932', exit-code=1 state=failure, TaskRun still Succeeded (report-only intact). Re-seeded and re-ran to leave main's check green. Filter logic also unit-checked locally against the real SARIF for accept / reject / stale-entry / missing-file cases.

title: Fix '| complete' exit-code swallows in go-fmt and tekton-check
description:
Same class as ocidex-qzz2 — 'complete' captures the exit code and nothing checks it — but in BLOCKING tasks, so these are live silent-greens.

.tektonic/jobs/go-fmt/fmt.nu:11
  let unformatted = (^gofmt -l ...$targets | complete | get stdout | str trim)
gofmt exits 2 on a parse error and writes the error to stderr, leaving stdout empty — so the task logs 'OK: all files formatted' and passes.

.tektonic/jobs/tekton-check/spec.ts:36
  let drift = (^git status --porcelain -- .tekton | complete | get stdout | str trim)
A failing git status yields empty drift and a green check.

Fix: bind the whole complete record, check .exit_code before reading stdout, and raise via 'error make' on non-zero. push-sboms.nu:48-55 already does exactly this correctly — follow that pattern.
acceptance_criteria: gofmt-check fails when gofmt exits non-zero with empty stdout; tekton-check fails when git status errors; both still pass on a clean tree and fail on real formatting/drift.
notes: Files: .tektonic/jobs/go-fmt/fmt.nu, .tektonic/jobs/tekton-check/spec.ts. Approach: bind the whole `complete` record and raise via error make when exit_code != 0, instead of `| get stdout`. Verified by ad-hoc TaskRun both polarities: clean tree Succeeded exit-code=0; a .go file with a parse error now StepFailed with gofmt's stderr and exit-code=1 (previously logged 'OK: all files formatted'). Commit 4f5c30b.

title: Tilt dev loop has no Postgres workload
description:
Tiltfile declares k8s_resource('postgres', port_forwards=5432) and hardcodes DATABASE_URL=postgres://ocidex:devpass@postgres:5432/ocidex, but charts/ocidex renders no Postgres workload (helm template shows only api, web, nats, scanner-worker, and the enricher/vuln workers). Tilt errors on the unknown resource, and even without that every pod would fail to reach the DB. migrate.enabled is also false in tilt/values-dev.yaml, so nothing applies the schema.

Found while removing the monolithic enrichment-worker (ocidex-kg5), which fixed the image/resource gaps for the enricher workers but deliberately did not take on standing up a dev Postgres — that is a design call (dev-only chart template vs. a bitnami/CNPG dependency vs. talosctl-side manifest).

Acceptance: 'make dev-cluster-up && make dev-up' brings every Tilt resource green with the schema applied.
notes:
Files: tilt/postgres.yaml (new dev-only Postgres Service+Deployment), tilt/values-dev.yaml (migrate.enabled), Tiltfile (secret + resource_deps), Makefile (macOS preflight), docs/K8S_DEV.md.
Commits: 739f485 (the Postgres/schema work), f8e4628 (macOS portability + two regressions the end-to-end run surfaced).

VERIFIED end to end on macOS (Docker Desktop 29.6.2, 8 CPU / 8 GB). Cold 'make dev-cluster-up && make dev-up':
- all 12 Tilt resources green at t=30s, zero pod restarts (proves resource_deps ordering)
- schema applied in-cluster: 29 tables, goose to version 57 on the first run
- /health and /ready both 200; psql reaches the DB through the 5432 port-forward with ocidex:ocidex
- registry mirror works on Docker Desktop (localhost:5005 -> 10.5.0.1:5005) — the main portability risk, disproved
- Job immutability handled: log shows 'field is immutable' -> 'Attempting to delete and re-create' -> succeeded, with a fresh Job and pod
- rebuild loop rolls every pod in 70s

Three defects found and fixed by the run:
1. dev-cluster-up was Linux-only in three ways — br_netfilter probed on the host /proc (module actually lives in Docker Desktop's LinuxKit VM), talosctl couldn't reach Docker (Go client honours DOCKER_HOST but ignores CLI contexts, and Desktop creates no /var/run/docker.sock), and talosctl kubeconfig wrote the unroutable in-cluster address 10.5.0.2:6443. Added a Docker-daemon liveness preflight too.
2. 739f485 put POSTGRES_PASSWORD ('ocidex') in the Tilt-managed Secret. Tilt scrubs Secret values from its logs and that string is a substring of every resource name, so the whole log read '[redacted secret ocidex-secrets:POSTGRES_PASSWORD]-api-...'. Literal in tilt/postgres.yaml instead.
3. Default RollingUpdate on postgres briefly ran two pods with separate emptyDirs, and Tilt reported ready off the outgoing one — so migrate ran against the database about to be discarded and the new one had no schema. strategy: Recreate.

Known limitation documented in K8S_DEV.md, not a defect: resource_deps only orders the initial build, so a bare postgres pod loss leaves everything green with an empty DB (first symptom 'relation "sbom" does not exist'). 'tilt trigger ocidex-migrate-1' restores 29 tables in 10s (verified).

Out of scope, filed separately: ocidex-y19y — 'make seed' targets a zot registry on localhost:5000 that no dev path provides; skips all 19 images, exits 0.

title: Skipped gated tasks leave a permanently pending GitHub status (tektonic skip-resolver never POSTs)
description:
tektonic's resolve-skipped-status finally task never resolves a when-skipped task's GitHub commit status, so the 'pending' posted by set-status-pending is never cleared.

Evidence: PR #104 head afb43d5 — tekton-check and grype-vuln-web each got a pending POST at 21:43:44/21:43:39 and NO resolving POST ever landed, while every task that actually ran reported itself. Same on PRs #101-#103.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by ad-hoc PipelineRun probes in ocidex-ci):
Tekton does NOT substitute $(tasks.<name>.status) inside a Task's step script — it stays literal. Probe 1 (status referenced directly in a step script) printed an empty/unsubstituted value; the shell reported 'tasks.gets-skipped.status: not found'. The generated script in .tekton/tasks/resolve-skipped-status-*.k8s.yaml does exactly this:
  let status = "$(tasks.tekton-check.status)"
  if $status != "None" { ...nothing to resolve...; exit 0 }
so $status is the literal string, never equals "None", and the POST is unreachable for every context.

FIX SHAPE (confirmed working by probe 2): deliver the status as a PipelineTask param instead. Probe 2 passed $(tasks.gets-skipped.status) as a finally-task param and the step read skipped=[None] ran=[Succeeded] — correct for both cases.

Fix belongs upstream in ~/code/tektonic (lib/reporters/github-status-reporter.ts createSkipResolverTask + the finally wiring in lib/core/pipeline.ts): declare one param per entry (e.g. status-<context>) on the resolver Task, pass $(tasks.<taskName>.status) from the finally PipelineTask, and read $(params.status-<context>) in skipResolverScript.

Secondary hardening while in there: each resolve step ends 'catch { ...; exit 1 }', and Tekton skips all remaining steps in a pod after a non-zero step — so one failing POST silently swallows every later context. Make the steps independent (drop the exit 1, or emit onError: continue).

Then: tag tektonic, bump @pfenerty/tektonic in .tektonic/package.json, make tekton-synth, commit regenerated YAML.

Blocks marking tekton-check / grype-vuln-web as required checks in branch protection.

Found while working ocidex-es6.
notes:
Fixed upstream in tektonic (tektonic-ukc, released v1.2.2). ocidex change is the version pin + regenerated YAML.
Files: .tektonic/package.json, .tektonic/package-lock.json, .tekton/ocidex-ocidex-pull-request.k8s.yaml, .tekton/tasks/resolve-skipped-status-ocidex-pull-request.k8s.yaml, .tekton/tasks/set-status-pending-*.k8s.yaml.
Approach: the skip resolver now receives each gated task's status as a param bound to $(tasks.<name>.status) on the finally PipelineTask — the only scope Tekton substitutes — and reads $(params.status-<name>). All resolve/pending steps got onError: continue so one failed POST no longer skips the rest of the pod's steps.
Verified in-cluster (probe-resolver-dph4j, ocidex-ci): skipped task logged 'task was skipped, POST ...', ran task logged 'task status is Succeeded'; step 1 exited 1 on a deliberate 404 and all 7 later steps still ran. Synth is idempotent.

title: image-build status reporter cannot write /tekton/home/.exit-code
description:
Every image-build/image-release task logs 'can't create /tekton/home/.exit-code: Permission denied' from the report-status step. The build-and-push step runs as uid 1000 (buildkit rootless) while /tekton/home is owned by the pod default uid 1024, so the exit-code handoff file is never written and report-status falls back to exit-code=0 / state=success.

Observed on both a real pipeline run (ocidex-ocidex-push-c4bgg-image-build-operator) and an ad-hoc TaskRun, so it affects all eleven images. Benign when the build succeeds; the concern is that a FAILING build would also report success, since 'onError: continue' already prevents the step failure from failing the TaskRun (see the CLAUDE.md gotcha table, 'Image release task shows Succeeded but image was not pushed').

Reproduce: kubectl logs -n ocidex-ci -l tekton.dev/taskRun=<any image-build taskrun> --all-containers | grep exit-code

Likely fix: write the exit-code file somewhere both uids can reach (the workspace, or a step-scoped emptyDir), or set the report-status step to read the buildctl metadata file instead. Found while verifying ocidex-5dw.
notes:
Files: .tektonic/package.json + package-lock.json (tektonic v1.2.0 -> v1.2.1), regenerated .tekton/tasks/*.k8s.yaml (37 tasks, additive only).
Approach: fixed upstream in tektonic (tektonic-ifc), not locally. Root cause was the file MODE, not the directory: the first wrapped step creates /tekton/home/.exit-code at the pod default uid 1024 with mode 0644, so the uid-1000 buildkit step could read it (getting the earlier 0) but not write it. tektonic's capturing wrap() now seeds the file with 0 if absent and best-effort chmods 0666 before the body, in all four language plugins.
Verified: paired throwaway TaskRuns on ocidex-ci (uid-1024 nu step + uid-1000 buildkit step exiting 7) — pre-fix reported exit-code=0 with 'Permission denied' and mode -rw-r--r--, post-fix reported exit-code=7 with mode -rw-rw-rw-. Then a real ad-hoc TaskRun of ocidex-image-build-cli against the warm buildkit cache: no 'can't create' line, image pushed, exit-code=0 state=success.
Note: npm would not re-resolve the git dep on a bare 'npm install' after the ref bump — needed 'npm install github:pfenerty/tektonic#v1.2.1' explicitly. Parent epic: plan-8ws.

title: ci: gate integration tests in Tekton pipeline
description:
The Tekton go-test job runs unit tests only, so nothing in tests/ is gated by CI. ocidex-784 was 7 pre-existing failures that sat undetected until Docker became available locally.

Adding an integration job needs testcontainers/Docker-in-cluster support (DinD sidecar or a Kubernetes-backed testcontainers provider), which is why it was carved out of ocidex-784 rather than done inline.

Source of truth is .tektonic/pipeline.ts; regenerate with make tekton-synth.
acceptance_criteria: A Tekton job runs 'go test ./tests/' on PR and push, and a failing integration test blocks the pipeline.
notes:
Files: .tektonic/jobs/go-integration/{spec.ts,test.nu} (new); .tektonic/shared.ts (goCacheIntegration); .tektonic/pipeline.ts (coreTasks + PR gated + push timeout 3h); .tektonic/jobs/image-build/spec.ts (needs goIntegration); tests/*_test.go (13 files); .tekton/** regenerated.

Approach: rejected a privileged DinD sidecar — nothing under tests/ actually needs a Docker daemon, testcontainers is only used to start Postgres and NATS. Instead the task runs plain postgres:15-alpine and nats:2-alpine sidecars (shared pod netns => localhost), and the test helpers take a shared-server path when TEST_POSTGRES_URL / TEST_NATS_URL are set, falling back to testcontainers locally. Isolation on the shared server is database-per-test (CREATE DATABASE ocidex_test_<hex> / DROP ... WITH (FORCE)), which holds because the tests package has no t.Parallel(). requireDocker renamed requireTestInfra: with the env var set there is no skip escape hatch, so an unreachable sidecar is a hard failure, which is the whole point of the issue.

needs: [goBuild], NOT [goTest] as originally planned — gated() returns a Proxy, so a dependent holding a raw reference to a gated task puts both the wrapped and unwrapped task in the PR graph (duplicate task name). Only leaf tasks can be gated; go-vulncheck has the same shape. Consequence: runs concurrently with go-test on the shared .go-mod/.go-build, hence goCacheIntegration with skipRestoreIfPathsExist (a restore begins with rm -rf).

Verified in-cluster with ad-hoc TaskRuns against a seeded workspace PVC (no commits pushed to test): positive run 32/32 --- PASS, zero SKIPs, 77s. Negative run with an injected t.Fatal test: step exit 1, TaskRun Failed, GitHub status posted failure — acceptance criterion met.

title: Diagnose the registry build cache (zero CACHED steps)
description: --export-cache/--import-cache to $IMAGE:buildcache costs ~115s per build (~19 min per pipeline) and the pflpj measurement recorded zero CACHED steps despite 'importing cache manifest ... done'. Decision was keep-and-debug rather than delete. Hypotheses: (1) base image digest drift — FROM ghcr.io/pfenerty/apko-cicd/golang:1.26 is a mutable rolling Wolfi tag, and a moving digest invalidates the whole chain including go mod download, which matches the symptom best; (2) context instability, fixed by ocidex-2vr.1; (3) broken mode=max export. Cheapest discriminator: run the same buildctl build twice back-to-back in one TaskRun — pass 2 CACHED means something between runs invalidates; pass 2 not CACHED means the round-trip itself is broken. Also check 'oras manifest fetch ghcr.io/pfenerty/ocidex-git-worker:buildcache' for intermediate layers. If digest drift is confirmed, pinning CI base images touches ADR-038 (Renovate pinDigests currently excludes CI images) and should be filed separately.
acceptance_criteria: A keep-or-delete decision recorded on the issue with the evidence that produced it.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-08-05: deleted --export-cache/--import-cache from build.sh and release.sh.

Files: .tektonic/jobs/image-build/build.sh, release.sh (flags removed, replaced with a comment
recording the measurement so they are not re-added blind), spec.ts (stale "registry build cache
keeps reruns fast" comment corrected), .tekton/**/image-{build,release}-*.k8s.yaml regenerated.

DECISION RATIONALE (evidence in the prior note): the export round-trip was proven healthy —
oras manifest fetch returned a well-formed cacheconfig.v0 with 21 layers — but the keys never
matched across runs. The one clean data point (cold local root + day-old registry cache) imported
the manifest successfully and produced ZERO CACHED steps. Cost measured at 84.7s and 95.6s per
build, ~30% of a 5m build, ~16 min per ten-image pipeline. ocidex-2vr.2's persistent buildkitd
root supersedes the purpose: it caches within a run AND across runs on the same node at no export
cost. The registry cache would only pay off on a genuinely cold PVC.

VERIFIED (TaskRun t2vr-scanner-z6brf, image-build-scanner-worker, warm root, rev a50c7dc):
build-and-push 5m15s, exit 0, image pushed, both Chains results written, zero "exporting cache"
lines in the log. builder-base fully CACHED (#10-#13) inherited from the earlier git-worker/api
builds in the same root.

READ THE WALL TIME CAREFULLY: 5m15s is nearly identical to the 5m18s steady-state git-worker run
that still HAD the export. That is not evidence the export was free — the export step is
structurally absent from the log. The totals match because the compile times differ:
  git-worker  318s = go build 209.7s + cache export ~85s + image export ~10s
  scanner-worker 315s = go build 296.6s +        0s     + image export  9.7s
Per-image saving is the ~85-95s export, unchanged; scanner-worker simply has a heavier main pkg.

CONSEQUENCE: the per-binary `go build` is now essentially the entire build (296.6s of 315s).
Further pipeline gains have to come from there, not from image plumbing — filed separately.

NOT DONE: pinning CI base images by digest. The base-digest-drift hypothesis (1) was never
confirmed or cleared; it is now moot for caching purposes but would still touch ADR-038
(Renovate pinDigests currently excludes CI images) if pursued for reproducibility reasons.

title: Build image context from a clean git archive tree
description: Image builds pass the shared Tekton workspace as the buildctl context. By image-build time that workspace holds web/node_modules (231MB), .git (29MB), and the .go-mod/.go-build caches seeded by go-build — measured at 468MB transferred, ten times per pipeline. Both .dockerignore and docker/Dockerfile.dockerignore exclude those paths, so no dockerignore is taking effect; rather than debug buildkit's dockerignore resolution, materialise a clean context from the commit tree (git archive HEAD -> .buildctx) and point --local context/dockerfile at it. Makes COPY . . in builder-base byte-identical per commit, which is a precondition for any cache to hit.
acceptance_criteria: Isolated TaskRun records the pre-change 'load build context' byte count; post-change context is <20MB; images still build and push identically.
notes:
VERIFIED 2026-08-05 (TaskRun t2vr-api-g2tnx).

Files: .tektonic/jobs/image-build/spec.ts (prepare-build-context step), build.sh + release.sh (--local context=.buildctx --local dockerfile=.buildctx), .tekton/** regenerated.

MEASUREMENT first, per the issue: buildctl logged "transferring context: 468.05MB", reproducing the pflpj figure exactly — so neither .dockerignore was taking effect. The issue notes claimed the root .dockerignore lacks a web/node_modules entry; that is wrong, both it and docker/Dockerfile.dockerignore exclude it, and the tracked tree is only 8.1MB. Root cause not pursued: building from a clean tree sidesteps dockerignore resolution entirely.

Approach: prepare-build-context materialises the commit tree with git archive into .buildctx, guarded on a .ctxrev stamp so the nine later builds in the chain reuse the extraction (and, by leaving mtimes alone, keep buildkit local-source diffing a no-op). git archive writes to a tar FILE then untars — never piped, because nushell coerces pipeline data to text and corrupts a tar stream. Runs at pod uid 1024; tar default 0755/0644 lets the uid-1000 build step read it without a chmod.

RESULT: context 468MB -> 8.2MB.

Gotcha fixed mid-verification: git refused with dubious ownership because the workspace PVC contents are not owned by the step uid. Fixed with -c safe.directory=* on the command line rather than a config file — GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL is already pointed elsewhere by goEnv for the Go tasks.

Note the direct time saving is now small: with the persistent buildkit root (ocidex-2vr.2) buildkit only transfers the context DIFF, which had already fallen to ~70kB. The real value delivered is a byte-identical context per revision, which is what makes COPY . . in builder-base a stable cache key — confirmed: the steady-state run showed builder-base fully CACHED across two different images.

title: make lint fails with 61 pre-existing issues
description:
`make lint` (and therefore `make check`) exits non-zero on a clean tree: 61 golangci-lint issues, unchanged by recent work — goconst 50, gosec 5, dupl 2, nilerr 2, staticcheck 1 (middleware.RealIP deprecation, GHSA-3fxj-6jh8-hvhx), unused 1 (pagedBody in internal/api/search_test.go).

This makes the quality gate useless as a regression detector: a new issue is invisible in the noise, and every story has to diff the lint output against a stashed baseline to tell whether it regressed anything.
acceptance_criteria: `flox activate -- bash -c 'export PATH="$HOME/go/bin:$PATH"; make lint'` exits 0 on a clean main, either by fixing the issues or by justifying and configuring exclusions in .golangci.yml.
notes:

title: Artifact relationship endpoints: usages and contains
description:
GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/usages — SBOMs whose components match this artifact. Returns the containing artifact, its version, flavor, digest, the matched version, and whether that is the artifact's current version.

GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/contains — inverse: tracked first-party artifacts in this artifact's latest SBOM.

New internal/service/artifact_relations.go, following search_artifact.go.
design:
Both filter through visible_namespace_ids, and both must work ACROSS sources within a namespace — that cross-source join is the concrete reason the namespace epic came first.

Confirm a usable component.purl index before merging (check 00039_efficiency_indexes.sql, 00047_stats_covering_indexes.sql); add a purl-base expression index if the join plans badly.
acceptance_criteria:
- usages resolves an uploaded binary to the images that ship it, across sources
- contains returns the inverse
- both respect namespace visibility
- the purl join has an index backing it
notes:
Files: db/migrations/00055_purl_base_index.sql, db/queries/artifact_relations.sql, internal/repository/artifact_relations.sql.go (generated), internal/service/artifact_relations.go, internal/service/search.go, internal/api/{types,search,router,search_test}.go, tests/artifact_relations_test.go, web/openapi.json + web/src/types/openapi.d.ts (generated).

Approach: two-stage matching. SQL matches coarsely on the purl base (split_part(split_part(purl,'?',1),'@',1)) or the (type,name,group) tuple, backed by three new expression indexes (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, so the migration is NO TRANSACTION). The service then applies the exact key via componentKey() — the same function changelog/diff uses, per ADR-041 R1. A full normalized key cannot be an expression index (qualifier filtering + sorting live in Go), and forking the rule so it could would let relationships and diff disagree; the coarse stage is deliberately a superset that the Go stage narrows.

usages leads with the component predicate (component is the large table, the expression index makes it selective) and excludes the subject's own SBOMs. contains uses a LEFT JOIN LATERAL for each matched artifact's current version/digest/flavor, avoiding an N+1. Visibility (visible_namespace_ids) is applied both inside and outside the correlated latest-SBOM subquery so an invisible newer SBOM cannot shadow a visible one; an artifact you cannot see returns 404, not 403.

R2 drift: version mismatch is reported as isCurrent=false, not treated as a non-match; isCurrent is nil when either side is unknown. R3: the ADR-019 versioned-name post-pass is explicitly NOT applied, so libfoo-1 and libfoo-2 stay distinct.

Verified: three integration tests in tests/artifact_relations_test.go pass against real Postgres (testcontainers) — purl-base match with cross-source resolution + drift, tuple fallback + R3, and namespace visibility on both directions before/after flipping a namespace public. make test green; golangci-lint reports 0 issues in the new files (the 61 repo-wide issues are pre-existing, ocidex-sgf). Seven unrelated integration tests fail on ingest 400/422 — pre-existing, confirmed by stashing these changes and re-running; already tracked as ocidex-784.

title: ADR-041: derived artifact relationships
description: Record that artifact-to-artifact links are derived from component data at query time, not stored.
design:
An image SBOM already contains a component whose purl IS the binary's identity — the relationship exists in the data.

Match is layered to mirror ADR-019 so diff and relationships agree on identity:
1. purl-base match (qualifiers and version stripped) when artifact.purl is set, with version compared separately so 'which version ships where' is answerable;
2. fall back to the (type, name, group_name) tuple.

Non-goals, recorded explicitly: a stored artifact_link table, and CI-declared links. Revisit only if a real relationship appears that component data cannot express.
acceptance_criteria:
- docs/adr/0041-*.md exists
- match layering is stated in terms consistent with ADR-019
- non-goals recorded with the condition that would reopen them
- ADR summary table in CLAUDE.md updated
notes:
Files: docs/adr/0041-derived-artifact-relationships.md (new), CLAUDE.md (ADR summary row 041).

Approach: relationships DERIVED at query time from component data, not stored. Rejected a stored artifact_link table (needs write path + backfill + invalidation, and can disagree with the components it came from) and CI-declared links (worthless until every producer opts in).

Five normative rules:
- R1 match key is componentKey() from internal/service/changelog.go, REUSED not reimplemented. ADR-019 Rules 1-2 apply verbatim (purl-base + identity qualifiers, then (type,name,group) NUL-joined fallback). Divergence is a bug in the relationship code.
- R2 version rides alongside the key, never inside it; component.version compared against sbom.subject_version so drift is the answer, not a non-match.
- R3 ADR-019 Rule 3 (versioned-name post-pass + survivor guard) explicitly does NOT apply. It reconciles a symmetric-difference change list, and collapsing libfoo-1/libfoo-2 would report an image as containing an artifact it does not contain. Stated explicitly because 'match ADR-019' would otherwise read as 'apply all three rules'.
- R4 only components matching a row in artifact participate. 'First-party' is not a flag, it is having been ingested as an artifact subject.
- R5 two directions, usages and contains, both filtered through visible_namespace_ids(user_id, is_admin); resolves across sources within a namespace per ADR-039.

INDEXING CAVEAT recorded for rj4.2: idx_component_purl and idx_component_name_group index the RAW columns, but R1's key is normalized in Go (version stripped, qualifiers filtered and sorted). An equality lookup on the normalized key cannot use them. Match on a purl-base prefix (btree can serve it) or add an expression index.

Non-goals with reopen conditions: stored artifact_link reopens only if a link must carry state not derivable from components (human-asserted, or must survive deletion of the evidencing SBOM); CI-declared links reopen only if a real relationship cannot be expressed by component data at all. Query cost alone reopens neither — the first answer to a slow query is an expression index.

ADR filename links verified against docs/adr/ (0025 is rbac-visibility, not rbac-visibility-model).

Watch for the known tektonic synthesis bug: if ${VAR#prefix} patterns get dropped from the generated YAML, hand-edit .tekton/tasks/*.yaml to match .tektonic/ and note it.
