title: ocidex-cli sbom push (minimal slice)
description:
A Cobra root plus one command, over pkg/client. Sequenced ahead of epic ocidex-e3g, which stays queued for the full subcommand surface.

  ocidex-cli sbom push ./ocidex.cdx.json \
    --artifact-file ./bin/ocidex \
    --subject-type application --subject-name ocidex \
    --subject-purl pkg:golang/github.com/pfenerty/ocidex@v1.2.3 \
    --version v1.2.3 --source ocidex-ci
design:
pkg/client.IngestSBOM already exists (pkg/client/sbom.go); thread the new subject and source params through.

--artifact-file makes the CLI compute the sha256 rather than asking CI to. Auth via OCIDEX_API_KEY. Non-zero exit on validation failure so CI fails loudly rather than silently skipping the upload.

Deliberately does not pre-empt ocidex-e3g's design work (ADR-029, the output package) — this is one command, not a CLI framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- pushes a real syft-generated SBOM for ./bin/ocidex end-to-end
- computes the digest from the artifact file
- exits non-zero on validation failure
notes:
Files: cmd/ocidex-cli/{main,sbom,sbom_test}.go, pkg/client/{sbom.go,sbom_test.go,types.go}, tests/cli_push_test.go, Makefile, go.mod

Approach: cobra root + 'sbom push' over pkg/client, nothing more — the full subcommand surface stays with epic ocidex-e3g.

- API key is env-only (OCIDEX_API_KEY), no --api-key flag: a flag puts the credential in the process table and in any CI log that echoes its commands.
- --artifact-file computes sha256 of the file and sends it as ?digest=, prefixed 'sha256:' so uploads and container scans store digests in the same form. Mutually exclusive with --digest.
- --source is validated client-side to UUID or <namespace>/<name>. This is the ONE piece of server validation duplicated in the CLI: a bare name is unresolvable because source names are unique per namespace, not globally, and the server's 400 arrives a round trip later. All other rules (digest required for non-container subjects, etc.) are left to the server to avoid drift.
- Optional flags map to nil params, so the server distinguishes 'not supplied' from 'supplied empty'.
- tests/cli_push_test.go builds and execs the real binary rather than calling runSBOMPush: the acceptance criterion is the process exit code, and a command that errored but exited 0 would publish nothing while looking like success. Fixture is a realistic 'syft dir:' SBOM whose metadata.component is the scratch dir — the exact condition the declared-subject params exist for. Asserts 201 + declared identity on the artifact (not '.sbom-bins'), 403 for a namespace the caller does not own, non-zero for an unresolvable source.
- pkg/client/types.go had to be regenerated: 'make check' halts at lint (61 pre-existing issues, ocidex-sgf) before reaching generate-client-check, so the 0gp.3 params had never made it into the generated client.
- make build now also builds bin/ocidex-cli, which 0gp.5 needs.

title: Ingest subject overrides in IngestParams
description: Extend service.IngestParams with SubjectType, SubjectName, SubjectGroup, SubjectPurl, Digest, NamespaceID, SourceID, and honour them in resolveArtifact (internal/service/sbom.go:86).
design:
Params take precedence over bom.Metadata.Component — the existing doc comment on IngestParams already states this contract ('Fields take precedence over BOM-extracted values when set').

Add validateUploadRequired beside validateContainerRequired (internal/service/sbom.go:227): for a non-container subject on an upload source, require subject type, name, version and digest. Container rules are untouched.
acceptance_criteria:
- a purl-less directory-component BOM ingests correctly when subject identity is supplied
- container ingest behaviour is byte-identical to before
- missing subject fields on an upload return a validation error, not a silent bad artifact
notes:
Files: internal/service/sbom.go, internal/service/sbom_ingest_test.go.
Approach: IngestParams gains SubjectType/SubjectName/SubjectGroup/SubjectPurl/Digest (NamespaceID/SourceID already existed from ocidex-9xs). New resolveSubjectIdentity() layers params over bom.Metadata.Component field by field, so a caller can correct just name+purl of a 'syft dir:' BOM. resolveArtifact() now works off that resolved identity; container name-digest stripping and the container-missing-digest error are unchanged, and a declared digest wins over both BOM sources.
validateUploadRequired(info) sits beside validateContainerRequired and requires subject_version + digest. Gate is subject TYPE, not source kind: the scanner produces container subjects exclusively (verified — no helm/non-container scan path exists), so a non-container subject can only have arrived via upload, and no source lookup is needed. Type/name are not checked because without them no artifact is resolved at all.
Also fixed the ADR-040 consequence from 0gp.1: new resolveIngestDigest(bom, params) feeds the pre-transaction GetSBOMByDigest short-circuit, so an upload dedups before the transaction rather than falling through to the UNIQUE index. Guarded resolveSubjectVersion against a nil metadata.component, now reachable when identity is declared entirely by params.
Tests: 6 new — params override, partial override keeps BOM fields, container unaffected (pins the byte-identical criterion), no-subject-no-params, declared identity with no subject component, table-driven validateUploadRequired, resolveIngestDigest precedence.
Note for 0gp.3: an upload with a missing subject NAME still silently resolves no artifact rather than erroring; the API layer is the right place to catch that once it knows the ingest is source-bound.

title: ADR-040: non-container artifact identity
description: Record that subject identity for a non-container artifact is caller-declared at upload, not inferred from the BOM, and that digest is the sha256 of the artifact file.
design:
Rationale: syft over a directory emits a metadata.component describing the directory, with no purl. There is nothing in the BOM to infer identity from, so the caller must state it.

Digest = sha256 of the artifact file mirrors the container rule that digest is identity, and preserves the sbom.digest UNIQUE idempotency guarantee for uploads.
acceptance_criteria:
- docs/adr/0040-*.md exists
- states the digest rule and its idempotency consequence
- ADR summary table in CLAUDE.md updated
notes:
Files: docs/adr/0040-non-container-artifact-identity.md (new), CLAUDE.md (ADR summary table row 040).
Approach: Identity is caller-declared on IngestParams (type/name/group/purl/version), extending the struct's existing 'params take precedence over BOM' contract rather than adding a second identity mechanism. Digest = sha256 of the artifact FILE, mirroring the container rule that digest identifies the subject not the description — this is what preserves the 00006 partial UNIQUE index as the idempotency guarantee. Rejected: BOM inference (a syft dir: subject is the scratch directory, nothing to infer from), SBOM-document hash (a scanner upgrade would fabricate a new artifact version), no digest (partial UNIQUE index means every upload bypasses dedup).
Found while writing: extractDigestFromBOM (sbom.go:891) reads only metadata.component, so the pre-transaction GetSBOMByDigest short-circuit is skipped for uploads — dedup still converges via the UNIQUE index but only after a full transaction. Recorded as a consequence; ocidex-0gp.2 must make that check consult params.Digest.

title: Operator + test updates for namespace/source
description: The controller creates namespace + source + registry rows, defaulting the OCIDex namespace from the CR's K8s namespace. Update the test suites that assert registry ownership.
design:
This is where the K8s naming collision is actually felt. Keep the two concepts visibly distinct in controller code — never a bare `ns` variable.

Run make generate-operator after touching api/v1alpha1 types; commit both the types and the regenerated output.
acceptance_criteria:
- an OCIRegistry CR in K8s namespace foo lands in OCIDex namespace foo by default
- internal/service/registry_test.go, internal/api/auth_boundary_test.go and tests/ pass
- private namespace SBOMs are invisible to a non-owner
- two sources in one namespace share visibility
notes:
Files: db/queries/registry.sql, internal/repository/{registry.sql.go,repository.go}, internal/service/registry.go, internal/api/{types.go,registry.go}, api/v1alpha1/ociregistry_types.go, internal/controller/ociregistry_controller.go, internal/service/registry_test.go, internal/controller/ociregistry_controller_test.go, tests/namespace_visibility_test.go
Approach: CreateRegistry gained an optional namespace_id — NULL keeps the pre-ADR-039 shape (namespace/source/registry share one id), a supplied id writes only source+registry into an existing namespace. service.resolveNamespace looks the namespace up by name and creates it on first use (nothing orders OCIRegistry reconciles), treating 23505 as a lost race and re-reading. The operator's ocidexNamespace(cr) defaults the OCIDex namespace from cr.Namespace (K8s), overridable via spec.namespace; create-only, since UpdateRegistry's new guard makes it a no-op otherwise. Because registries can now share a namespace: all 5 registry reads project source.name instead of namespace.name; GetRegistryByName matches source.name (unique per namespace only) and takes the oldest; UpdateRegistry propagates name/visibility to the namespace only when registry.id = namespace.id (owns it outright). Commit bfdea6f.

title: Artifact relationships and type-aware UI
description:
Surface the link between a first-party artifact and the artifacts that ship it, and stop the UI assuming every artifact is a container image.

An image SBOM already contains a component whose purl *is* the binary's identity — the relationship exists in the data, it is just never queried. Meanwhile ArtifactDetail renders flavor selectors, registry links, image metadata and signing unconditionally, and Home.tsx says 'what's in your containers'.

The actionable payoff is drift: seeing that ocidex v1.2.3 ships in 4 images, and that one of them still carries an older build.

Depends on the namespace/source epic — usages must resolve across sources within a namespace (the uploaded binary and the scanned image are two channels, one project).
design:
Links are DERIVED, not stored. Match is layered to mirror ADR-019 so diff and relationships agree on identity:
1. purl-base match (qualifiers and version stripped) when artifact.purl is set, with version compared separately so 'which version ships where' is answerable;
2. fall back to the (type, name, group_name) tuple.

Non-goals: a stored artifact_link table, and CI-declared links. Revisit only if a real relationship appears that component data cannot express.

UI follows the existing pattern rather than a parallel one: ArtifactDetail/index.tsx already branches on 'container' at line 102 — extend that. Relationship entry cards reuse DiffEntryCard structure per ADR-023/ADR-036.
acceptance_criteria:
- GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/usages returns containing artifacts across sources within a namespace
- GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/contains returns tracked first-party artifacts in the latest SBOM
- both filter through visible_namespace_ids
- ArtifactDetail shows no image chrome for non-container artifacts
- version drift is the most prominent thing on a relationship card
close_reason: All 5 children complete and merged to main (527c1f1..f5e9dd9, pushed to origin/main). Derived-relationship endpoints (usages/contains) filtered through visible_namespace_ids per ADR-041; ArtifactDetail image chrome gated on artifact.type; RelationshipsTab leads with version drift; list/landing surfaces broadened beyond containers. Deferred and filed, not dropped: artifact-type breakdown tile on Home (ocidex-l1e0). Entry-card redesign of Artifacts table declined — outside binding AC, would churn 7 tests for no gain.

title: Non-container artifact lifecycle: caller-declared subject identity + upload path
description:
Make uploading an SBOM for a non-container artifact (a Go binary, a library) a first-class, owned, identifiable operation.

Ingest is already type-agnostic — resolveArtifact (internal/service/sbom.go:86) upserts artifact with whatever metadata.component.type the BOM declares, and container-only rules are correctly gated on type == container. Three things are missing:
1. syft over a directory (dir:.sbom-bins) emits a metadata.component describing a *directory*, with no purl — the artifact is unidentifiable and cannot be linked to anything.
2. IngestSBOM (internal/api/sbom.go:15) never sets RegistryID, and sbom_visible() treats NULL as visible-to-everyone. The upload path is a read-visibility hole.
3. No client-side way to push an SBOM from CI.

Ends with OCIDex dogfooding itself: the push/tag pipeline uploads SBOMs for its own Go binaries.

Depends on the namespace/source epic — an upload needs a namespace to be owned by and a source to be attributed to.
design:
Subject identity is caller-declared at upload, not inferred. Digest is the sha256 of the artifact *file*, mirroring the container rule that digest is identity — which preserves the sbom.digest UNIQUE idempotency guarantee for uploads.

IngestParams gains SubjectType/SubjectName/SubjectGroup/SubjectPurl/Digest/NamespaceID/SourceID. Params take precedence over bom.Metadata.Component — the existing precedence comment on IngestParams already states this contract. validateUploadRequired sits beside validateContainerRequired; container rules are untouched.

CLI: a minimal 'ocidex-cli sbom push' slice sequenced ahead of epic ocidex-e3g, which stays queued for the full subcommand surface.
acceptance_criteria:
- an SBOM can be pushed with declared subject identity and lands owned by a namespace
- ingest without a resolvable source is a 400; the IS NULL disjunct is gone from the visibility functions
- ingest against a namespace you do not own returns 403
- the push/tag pipeline uploads SBOMs for ocidex's own binaries
close_reason: All 5 children closed and merged to main. End-to-end outcome verified on ocidex-dev: the push pipeline's 9 binary SBOMs are ingested with caller-declared subject identity and now visible in the artifacts list (the last blocker, ocidex-m7vv, is fixed). Follow-on work — --arch on the CI push, artifact-type stats tile (ocidex-l1e0) — is tracked separately.

title: Push pipeline takes ~2h40m: serial image builds are the bottleneck
description: The timeout bump to 4h is a band-aid. Nine image builds run serially at ~15-18 min each, dominating a ~2h40m pipeline. They were chained deliberately so two builds never overlap and burst the single homelab node's memory. Options worth evaluating: parallelise with a concurrency cap of 2 once node memory allows; share a buildkit cache across the nine builds (they share a Go builder stage, so the compile is likely repeated per image); or split image builds into their own pipeline triggered separately from the lint/test gate. Measure first — confirm whether the ~16 min is Go compile, base pull, or multi-arch emulation.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-08-06. Measured on a real push pipeline, not a projection.

RESULT: run ocidex-ocidex-push-t2t4l (rev 6939d54) took 70m03s end to end, against the
133m52s baseline of push-pflpj (rev a50c7dc, 2026-08-04). 47% reduction. The ten-image serial
chain itself went from ~121m to 61m23s.

Per-image, warm root: api 7m19s (first in chain, absorbs the COPY . . re-key for the new
revision), scanner-worker 5m25s, oci-metadata-worker 4m33s, enrichment-worker 4m30s,
vuln-worker 4m28s, user-enricher-worker 4m15s, provenance-worker 4m06s, git-worker 3m38s,
operator 9m15s, web 13m47s.

WHAT DID IT (children):
- 2vr.2 persistent buildkitd root on a PVC — the main lever. builder-base, the base image pull,
  go mod download and the Dockerfile --mount=type=cache mounts now survive across all ten builds
  in a run and across runs on the same node.
- 2vr.1 clean git-archive build context — 468MB -> 8.2MB, and byte-identical per revision, which
  is the precondition for COPY . . being a stable cache key.
- 2vr.3 deleted the registry build cache — 85-96s of export per build for zero import hits.

PIPELINE TIMEOUT: push lowered 4h -> 2h30m. Not 2h: the binding case is a COLD run (cache PVC
recreated or rebound to another node), ~11 min per build cold, which lands near 2h; a 2h ceiling
would convert a cache miss into a pipeline failure. Tag pipeline deliberately LEFT at 4h — those
builds are multi-arch (amd64+arm64) and no tag run has happened since these changes, so
buildkit-release-cache is still cold and unmeasured. Lower it only after a real tag run.

CACHE PVC SIZING (plan verification step 5): ocidex-buildkit-cache at 9.5G of 25Gi after the full
ten-image run, all under root/runc-native. Still below the 14GiB keepBytes, so GC has not had to
prune yet — the ceiling is correctly placed and the claim has room for the native snapshotter to
materialise during a build. Node disk 63% used, 82G free.

WHERE THE REMAINING TIME IS, filed as follow-ups:
- ocidex-2j2 (P3) per-binary `go build` is now essentially the whole Go image build (296.6s of
  315s for scanner-worker); covers the operator 9m15s outlier too.
- ocidex-5343 (P3) image-build-web 13m47s — npm/vite, shares no builder-base with the Go images.
- ocidex-pakf (P3) `make tekton-check` is referenced by CLAUDE.md but does not exist.

title: Enable Renovate digest pinning for runtime and build images
description: renovate.json: pinDigests:true scoped to dockerfile/docker-compose/helm-values managers; add digest to the automerge updateTypes; minimumReleaseAge 0 for cgr.dev/chainguard/nginx. CI images in .tekton/ stay on tags.
notes:
Files: renovate.json
Approach: pinDigests: true scoped to matchManagers [dockerfile, docker-compose, helm-values]; extended the existing automerge rule to cover 'digest' so pins don't accumulate as manual PRs; cgr.dev/chainguard/nginx gets minimumReleaseAge 0 (free tier is :latest only, so the digest IS the version, and a new digest is usually the CVE fix we picked the image for — the global 3-day hold would delay exactly the updates that motivated this epic). .tekton/ CI images deliberately excluded: apko-cicd/base:stable appears 100+ times as a moving tag, so pinning would force a Renovate PR + make tekton-synth on every upstream rebase. The .tektonic/**/*.ts customManager left untouched for the same reason. Renovate raises the pinning PRs itself — no digests looked up by hand. Validated as JSON.

title: Bump distroless base to static-debian13 for the nine Go images
description: docker/Dockerfile lines 134-169: gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot -> static-debian13:nonroot across all nine final stages.
notes:
Files: docker/Dockerfile
Approach: Nine final stages bumped gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot -> static-debian13:nonroot via sed; verified 9 replaced, 0 remaining. Mechanical — binaries are CGO_ENABLED=0 static so there is no libc coupling. debian13 is 5 packages (base-files, media-types, netbase, tzdata, tzdata-legacy).

title: Replace Caddy with Chainguard nginx in the web image
description: New web/nginx.conf (static + SPA fallback + gzip, no proxy_pass, nonroot-safe paths, include /etc/nginx/ocidex.d/*.conf). Delete web/Caddyfile. Update docker/web/Dockerfile. Port ripple 80->8080 across deployment-web.yaml, services.yaml targetPort, docker-compose. Update docs/DEPLOYMENT.md and Tiltfile comment.
notes:
Files: web/nginx.conf (new), web/Caddyfile (deleted), docker/web/Dockerfile, charts/ocidex/templates/deployment-web.yaml, charts/ocidex/templates/services.yaml, docs/DEPLOYMENT.md, Tiltfile
Approach: cgr.dev/chainguard/nginx, 19 packages vs caddy:2-alpine's 178 (verified with syft on the BUILT image, not just the base). Replaced /etc/nginx/nginx.conf wholesale — the image ships conf.d/nginx.default.conf as a full server{} block and has no shell to rm it. Zero upstreams by design: nginx resolves literal proxy_pass hostnames at config-load time and won't start if they don't resolve. Runs as UID 65532 so listens on 8080; Service keeps port 80 with targetPort 8080 so the HTTPRoute backendRef is untouched. Plan assumptions corrected by inspecting the real image: /run is already 0777-owned by 65532 (compiled pid path works, no override), /var/log/nginx/*.log are already symlinks to /dev/stdout|stderr, and temp paths are already compiled to /var/lib/nginx/tmp — so none of the planned overrides were needed. Verified: nginx -t as UID 65532 ok; live container / -> 200, /some/spa/route -> 200, gzip on, clean logs.

title: Compose: bind-mount an nginx proxy snippet
description: New web/nginx.compose.conf with the four location blocks proxying to http://ocidex:8080, preserving the Host header. Bind-mount to /etc/nginx/ocidex.d/proxy.conf in docker-compose.yml; drop the BACKEND_URL env.
notes:
Files: web/nginx.compose.conf (new), docker-compose.yml
Approach: Compose has no L7 router, so it bind-mounts the four location blocks at /etc/nginx/ocidex.d/proxy.conf, included from inside server{} in nginx.conf. The image ships nothing there — a wildcard include matching zero files is legal nginx, verified with nginx -t both with and without the mount, so one image serves both deployments. Hoisted the four proxy_set_header directives to server context (the include site is inside server{}) rather than a per-location include, avoiding a second bind mount. Host must be $host not the upstream: the GitHub OAuth redirect derives from r.Host, same reason vite.config.ts sets changeOrigin: false. Dropped BACKEND_URL (no shell to substitute it). Verified against a stub upstream: all four prefixes proxy with Host preserved; / and /healthy correctly fall through to the SPA.

title: Move /api,/auth,/health,/ready routing into the web HTTPRoute
description: Add four higher-precedence rules to the -web HTTPRoute in charts/ocidex/templates/httproutes.yaml targeting the -api Service on port 80, with the / catch-all last. Document the non-Gateway install caveat in values.yaml + NOTES.txt, and fix web/src/api/queries/registries.ts:123 to use API_BASE_URL.
notes: VERIFIED (post-implementation): Cloudflare gateway rule ordering is honoured — the risk flagged in the plan is closed. Two ways: (1) live cluster — https://ocidex.app/api/v1/<random> returned a text/plain 404 from the API (not the SPA's text/html fallback), marker appeared in the api pod logs and never in the web pod's; (2) controller source — httproute_controller.go builds ingress with 'for _, rule := range route.Spec.Rules', appending in slice order, so ordering holds by construction. The nginx proxy_pass fallback is not needed. Two caveats recorded in ADR-0038: match.Path.Type is ignored by that controller (Exact degrades to a Cloudflare regex, so /health would also match /healthy — kept Exact anyway as it's the correct spec semantic and conformant controllers honour it), and match order WITHIN a rule is nondeterministic (map iteration), so keep one backend per rule.

title: Harden runtime images: Chainguard nginx, Gateway-native routing, distroless debian13, digest pinning
description: Replace the vulnerable caddy:2-alpine web image (178 packages) with cgr.dev/chainguard/nginx (19 packages), move the /api, /auth, /health, /ready reverse-proxy rules out of the web container and into the Gateway API HTTPRoute, bump the nine Go service runtimes from distroless static-debian12 to static-debian13, and digest-pin all runtime/build images with Renovate maintaining the digests. See plan: the-caddy-image-we-binary-catmull.md

title: test: 7 integration tests fail on POST /api/v1/sboms with 400/422
description:
Pre-existing, confirmed at 5b3578d (migration 49) as well as at HEAD -- NOT caused by ocidex-ckv. Docker only became available locally today, so the integration suite had not been run in a while.

Failing (all assert 201 on POST /api/v1/sboms and get 400 or 422):
- TestEnricherDependencyChain_GitEnqueuedAfterOCIMetadata (422, enrich_chain_test.go:90)
- TestEnricherDependencyChain_NoGitJobOnOCIMetadataFailure (422, enrich_chain_test.go:90)
- TestSigningStatusParity_AllStatuses + 5 subtests (400, integration_test.go:596)
- TestProvenanceRecheckErrorPreservesData (400, integration_test.go:732)
- TestProvenanceDriftFullCycle (400, integration_test.go:835)
- TestVulnDuplicatePurlSummaryParity (400, vuln_integration_test.go:499)
- TestScanToEnrichFlow (244s)

The two 422s vs five 400s suggest more than one cause. Tests discard the response body, so the first step is to surface the validation error. CI's go-test job runs unit tests only, so this is invisible to the pipeline.
notes:
Files: tests/auth_integration_test.go, tests/enrich_chain_test.go, tests/integration_test.go, tests/scan_to_enrich_test.go, tests/vuln_integration_test.go. No production code changed.

All 8 failures were stale test-side assumptions.

The reported 400/422s: fixtures predated validateBOM (>=1 component) and validateContainerRequired (subject_version + architecture + build_date). Added the missing syft:image:labels properties to duplicatePurlSBOM, signingStatusSBOMTemplate, chainTestSBOM, plus a component to chainTestSBOM. chainTestSBOM also needed an explicit version property because resolveSubjectVersion (internal/service/sbom.go:899) skips a metadata.component.version starting with 'sha256:'.

Added mustIngest helper (tests/auth_integration_test.go) that t.Fatalf's with the response body on non-201, so the next validation change names the rejected field instead of '400 != 201'.

Three more bugs surfaced once ingest stopped failing first:
1. signingStatusSBOMTemplate varied only the digest, so all 5 subtests shared one artifact and the parity assertion read the artifact rollup across them (verification_failed saw 'verified' from the prior subtest). Now varies the repository name.
2. TestScanToEnrichFlow reused the ingest deadline for the enrichment wait; a 4-min syft pull consumed it and the loop never iterated. Separate 1-min deadline.
3. Same test claimed enrichment_jobs with enricher_name='all', which nothing enqueues -- the submitter enqueues per root enricher (user/oci-metadata/provenance, ADR-033). Now claims 'oci-metadata'. cmd/ocidex and cmd/scanner-worker also pass 'all' but only call Enqueue (name is a per-call arg), so it is inert there.

Added scan_jobs and enrichment_jobs diagnostics on both timeout paths.

Verified: full ./tests/ suite green (88s, no skips); unit tests green. The 61 golangci-lint issues are pre-existing -- identical with these changes stashed, all in files not touched here.

Follow-ups: ocidex-113l (CI go-test job runs unit tests only, does not gate tests/), ocidex-jxlt (docs/INGESTION.md section 3 stale: says 422, code returns 400).

title: fix(web): replace signing legend with styled tooltip
description:
SigningLegend on the Artifacts page is too prominent. SigningBadge already carries the full description as a native title= attribute from STATUS_INFO in web/src/utils/trust.ts.

- New web/src/components/ui/Tooltip.tsx + .css: CSS-driven primitive (ADR-015, no Kobalte), hover + :focus-visible, aria-describedby, prefers-reduced-motion
- SigningBadge: wrap Badge in Tooltip, drop title prop, keep unknown-status fallback
- Artifacts.tsx: remove <SigningLegend /> and its import
- Delete web/src/components/SigningLegend.tsx and SigningLegend.css (sole usage)
notes:
Files: web/src/components/ui/Tooltip.tsx (new), Tooltip.css (new), SigningBadge.tsx, SigningBadge.test.tsx, ui/index.ts, pages/Artifacts.tsx, utils/trust.ts; deleted components/SigningLegend.tsx + .css
Approach: new Tooltip primitive per ADR-015. Deviation from plan: not CSS-only. SigningBadge renders inside .table-wrapper (overflow:auto both axes, max-height 70vh), so an absolutely-positioned tooltip is clipped by the table it annotates. Tooltip portals to <body> and uses fixed coords from the trigger's getBoundingClientRect, flipping below when within 64px of the viewport top, and dismisses on scroll (capture phase, so .table-wrapper scroll counts), resize and Escape. Trigger is tabindex=0 with aria-describedby so it is keyboard-reachable; prefers-reduced-motion respected.
Verified: 135/135 frontend tests; new tests assert the description is reachable on focus via aria-describedby and that no native title remains. make frontend-lint down to the 2 pre-existing warnings; tsc + vite build clean. Commit 5ac2cff.
NOT verified: visual check on hover/keyboard in light and dark themes (needs make frontend-dev).

title: Namespace-scoped operator strands OCIRegistry finalizers; 'ocidex' ns stuck Terminating 19 days
description: The 'ocidex' namespace has been Terminating since 2026-07-12. Six ociregistries.ocidex.io objects have deletionTimestamp set and still hold the ocidex.io/registry-protection finalizer (ghcr-dex, ghcr-flux, ghcr-traefik, quay-container-tools, quay-keycloak, quay-metallb). Nothing will remove them: the operator restricts its cache to a single WATCH_NAMESPACE (cmd/operator/main.go:91-95) and now watches ocidex-dev, so the removal path at internal/controller/ociregistry_controller.go:127 never runs for these objects. Two parts: (a) immediate cleanup — patch the finalizers off the six objects so the namespace drains; (b) design gap — a namespace-scoped operator orphans its own finalizers whenever it is moved or uninstalled. Decide on a mitigation (documented uninstall procedure, a cleanup Job, or multi-namespace watch).
acceptance_criteria: The ocidex namespace is fully deleted; a documented or automated path exists to release registry-protection finalizers when the operator no longer watches their namespace.
notes:
Files: internal/config/config.go, internal/config/config_test.go, cmd/operator/main.go, charts/ocidex-operator/values.yaml, docs/OPERATIONS.md, docs/adr/0030-k8s-operator-crds.md

CORRECTION to earlier notes: the claim that multi-namespace watch would need 'a Role per watched namespace or a ClusterRole' was stale. RBAC has always been cluster-scoped (charts/ocidex-operator/templates/clusterrole.yaml, config/operator/rbac/role.yaml, ADR-030 RBAC Requirements are all ClusterRole). The only namespace restriction is the manager cache scoping. Multi-namespace watch cost zero RBAC change.

Part (a) - DONE, live. Re-verified all six OCIRegistry objects in ns 'ocidex' had empty status.registryID, so handleDeletion's 'if cr.Status.RegistryID != ""' guard would short-circuit and its path reduces to exactly RemoveFinalizer+Update - hand-patching is behaviourally identical with no orphan-row risk. Patched finalizers off all six (ghcr-dex, ghcr-flux, ghcr-traefik, quay-container-tools, quay-keycloak, quay-metallb). Namespace drained immediately: 'kubectl get ns ocidex' -> NotFound. All 8 ocidex-dev registries intact with real UUIDs. Stuck 26 days.

Part (b) - design gap closed:
- WATCH_NAMESPACE is now comma-separated, parsed into OperatorConfig.WatchNamespaces with envSeparator:"," and normalised in validate() (trim, drop empties, error if none remain - env.Parse yields []string{""} for an unset var, and an empty cache key would widen the watch to every namespace rather than narrowing it). main.go builds cache.Options{DefaultNamespaces} from the slice and no longer reads the env var raw.
- watch_namespaces is logged at manager startup; reading it back from pod env was the only way to diagnose this bug.
- ADR-030 gained a 'Finalizer lifecycle and watch scope' subsection: the finalizer is a promise that a controller watching the namespace will remove it, so the watch scope is an operational contract, not a tuning knob. Hand-patching is safe only when status.registryID is empty.
- docs/OPERATIONS.md gained incident #7 (namespace stuck Terminating) and a 'Retargeting or uninstalling the operator' procedure: drain CRs first (preferred), or live-migrate via comma-separated watch (add new ns -> move CRs -> drop old).

Approach note: draining before retargeting avoids the bug entirely - the ordering discipline is the real fix. Multi-namespace watch is what makes a LIVE retarget safe as a two-step rather than a hard cutover. Neither alone is sufficient.

Deliberately out of scope: OCIDEX_SERVER/OCIDEX_API_KEY/OPERATOR_NAMESPACE remain raw os.Getenv in main.go.

Verified: TestLoadOperator 10/10 subtests pass (incl. 'ocidex-dev' -> [ocidex-dev] backwards-compat guard); make test PASS; operator builds; helm template renders value: "ocidex-dev" unchanged and "ocidex-dev,ocidex" for the list form. 61 golangci-lint issues in the tree are pre-existing (confirmed identical on a stashed clean baseline), none in the touched packages.

title: Diff tree header counts changes that are never rendered
description:
DiffTreeView.tsx computes header counts from the flat tree.changes array but renders visibleRows(), which only recurses into expanded nodes. expandedRefs starts empty and showContext/showTransitive default false, so a changed transitive node is counted and never shown. removedOrphans rescues only direction==='removed'.

Fix: auto-expand ancestors of changed nodes on mount (expandAllChanged already computes the set), generalise removedOrphans to any change visibleRows did not emit, and add a 'showing X of Y changes' reconciliation line with a control to reveal the rest.
acceptance_criteria: A tree whose only change is a transitive grandchild renders that row; header count equals rendered change-row count or is explicitly reconciled; tests cover both
notes:
Files: web/src/components/DiffTreeView.tsx, web/src/components/DiffTreeView.test.tsx
Approach: Header counted tree.changes while the table rendered visibleRows(), which only recurses into expanded nodes — expandedRefs started empty, so any change on a transitive node was counted and never rendered. Three changes: (1) createEffect keyed on treeData() calls expandAllChanged() on mount and on every new tree, so ancestors of changes are open by default; (2) removedOrphans generalised to orphanChanges — any direction whose nodeRef/purl has no node in the graph, rendered with its real direction badge and a prev -> new version cell via a new shared changeBadgeClass() helper (also replaces the inline changeCls in the tree rows); (3) a reconciliation line 'Showing X of Y changes - N hidden under indirect dependencies' with a 'Show hidden changes' button (setShowTransitive + expandAllChanged), where X counts DISTINCT rendered node ids so a diamond dependency isn't double-counted. Also deduped the standalone changes() filter to reuse treeData().changes. showContext/showTransitive still default false. Tests: transitive-grandchild change renders (verified failing without the effect, and that the reconciliation line appears in its place); orphan with direction=downgraded renders under its own badge.

title: UI bugs: correctness and usability defects in the deployed UI
description:
Umbrella for defects reported from ocidex.app that make the UI wrong or unusable. Members share no single root cause but land on one branch for review.

Reported:
1. Diff tables show github.com/pfenerty/ocidex as 'downgraded' for a semver rc -> release transition.
2. Diff tree header counts changes that are never rendered ('up1 upgraded' with an empty table).
3. Dashboard stats never load - request timeout plus a cache that is only written on success.
4. /vulnerabilities table is not sortable.
5. /admin/registries gives no indication that a registry is managed by a Kubernetes CRD.

Also folds in the already-fixed signing-badge work (ocidex-xxr) and the pre-existing Artifacts.test.tsx failure (ocidex-f13).

title: Signing badges: contradictory 'Signed / no signature', misleading amber warning styling, and artifact_missing rendered as Unsigned
description:
Four defects in the provenance/signing badge UI, all sharing one root cause: two independent sources of truth for the status->presentation table (web/src/utils/trust.ts STATUS_INFO and a hardcoded Switch in web/src/components/ui/SigningBadge.tsx), which have drifted apart.

1. SummaryBand.tsx:55-58 prints 'no signature' as the fallback for a missing builderId, so an SBOM with signaturePresent=true renders 'Signed / no signature'.
2. /artifacts mixes Signed and Verified with no explanation. The split reflects registry verification_mode (6 of 8 are 'none'), not any artifact property.
3. 'Signed' is styled amber with ShieldAlert (a '!' icon), blaming the artifact for an OCIDex config gap. 'Verified' is green, off the ADR-023 palette.
4. SigningBadge has no artifact_missing case, so a deleted artifact falls through and renders as grey 'Unsigned'.
acceptance_criteria:
- trust.ts is the single status table; SigningBadge derives from it
- Color axis: verified=brand blue, signed/unsigned=grey, artifact_missing=amber, verification_failed=red; no green
- Every badge has a tooltip; /artifacts has a legend
- artifact_missing renders 'Artifact missing', not 'Unsigned'
- SummaryBand never prints 'no signature' when a signature is present
- Unit tests cover trust.ts, SigningBadge, and the SummaryBand regression
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md badge table lists all five values
notes:
Files: web/src/utils/trust.ts (single source of truth), web/src/components/ui/SigningBadge.tsx (derives from trust.ts), web/src/components/SummaryBand.tsx (provenanceSubline), web/src/components/SigningLegend.tsx + .css (new), web/src/pages/Artifacts.tsx (mounts legend), docs/CONFIGURATION.md; tests: web/src/utils/trust.test.ts, web/src/components/ui/SigningBadge.test.tsx, web/src/components/SummaryBand.test.tsx.

Approach: root cause was two independent status->presentation tables — trust.ts STATUS_INFO (ProvenanceCard/SummaryBand/RegistriesTab) and a hardcoded Switch in SigningBadge (Artifacts/ArtifactDetail/VersionsTab) — which had already drifted: SigningBadge had no artifact_missing case, so a deleted artifact rendered as grey 'Unsigned'. Collapsed onto trust.ts, which now carries variant + icon + tooltip description per status.

Colour axis is now green-free: blue=affirmed (verified/ShieldCheck), grey=no information (signed/Shield, unsigned/ShieldOff), amber=availability problem (artifact_missing/ShieldAlert, was danger), red=trust problem (verification_failed/ShieldX). 'signed' loses the ShieldAlert '!' — per ADR-037 it means no check was performed, an OCIDex config gap, not an artifact defect. No CSS change needed: .badge-primary already renders brand blue.

SummaryBand's 'no signature' sub-line was the fallback for a missing SLSA builderId, not a missing signature; replaced with provenanceSubline() which degrades builder -> facts present -> 'no signing material' -> em dash.

Added tooltips on every badge plus an always-visible legend above the artifacts table (renders through SigningBadge itself so it cannot drift).

Verified: make frontend builds clean; make frontend-lint 0 errors (2 pre-existing warnings in untouched files); vitest 119 passed / 1 failed — that failure confirmed pre-existing on main by stashing web/ and re-running, filed as ocidex-f13.

title: Reverifier batch cap silently stretches PROVENANCE_RECHECK_INTERVAL into a multi-day sweep
description: recheckBatchSize=500 is hardcoded at internal/enrichment/reverify.go:14 and tick() runs once per PROVENANCE_RECHECK_INTERVAL. The two combine so that with 3,764 provenance enrichments in ocidex-dev, a configured 24h recheck interval yields an effective full-sweep period of ~8 days, degrading linearly as the corpus grows. Discovered while investigating ocidex-hb9: 147 stale verification_failed rows from the ocidex-33h bug were still displayed a day after the fix deployed, because the oldest-first sweep had 1,553 rows queued ahead of them. The batch cap is a legitimate load guard; the defect is that it silently redefines the documented meaning of the interval, with no signal when the sweep falls behind.
design: Decouple sweep cadence from the staleness cutoff. Keep 'interval' feeding the Cutoff param (its documented meaning) and add a distinct sweepInterval driving the ticker, derived as interval/24 floored at ~1 minute so a 24h interval sweeps hourly. Keep recheckBatchSize as a per-tick rate cap and document that sweepInterval x batch must exceed corpus size for the interval to hold. Log WARN when a tick returns a full batch, which is the currently-invisible signal that the sweep is falling behind.
acceptance_criteria: A corpus larger than recheckBatchSize is fully swept within one interval (regression test). Cutoff is still computed from interval, not sweepInterval. Full-batch WARN fires when len(due)==recheckBatchSize. make check passes.
notes:
Files: internal/enrichment/reverify.go, internal/enrichment/reverify_test.go

Approach: decoupled sweep cadence from the recheck interval. Reverifier gains a
sweepInterval field, derived in NewReverifier via deriveSweepInterval():
interval/sweepDivisor (24), floored at minSweepInterval (1m) and capped at
interval so a short interval never sweeps less often than it asks for. interval
still feeds the Cutoff param (its documented meaning); sweepInterval drives the
ticker. Default 24h recheck now sweeps hourly = 12,000 rows/day of headroom vs
the 3,764-row corpus. recheckBatchSize stays 500; its doc comment now states it
bounds rate, not period. tick() logs WARN when len(due) >= recheckBatchSize --
the falling-behind signal that was previously invisible.

No config or main.go change needed: NewReverifier's signature is unchanged.

Tests: TestReverifier_SweepsWholeCorpusWithinOneInterval (regression -- drains a
3,764 corpus across one interval's worth of sweeps),
TestReverifier_Tick_CutoffUsesIntervalNotSweepInterval,
TestReverifier_Tick_WarnsWhenBatchIsFull (table: full/partial/empty),
TestDeriveSweepInterval (table incl. floor and cap cases). Existing tests pass
unchanged -- the cap-at-interval rule preserves TicksAtConfiguredInterval's 15ms
behaviour.

description: govulncheck flags 2 reachable vulns via cosign in internal/enrichment/provenance/{keyless,verify,parse}.go: GO-2026-5932 (x/crypto/openpgp, frozen/no-fix, reachable through cosign's internal legacy-PGP fallback) and GO-2026-4529/CVE-2026-24122 (cert-chain expiry gap, fixed in cosign v3.0.5, no v2 backport). notes:
Files: go.mod, go.sum, internal/enrichment/provenance/{keyless,verify,parse}.go, docs/adr/0037-cosign-delegated-provenance-verification.md
Approach: bumped github.com/sigstore/cosign/v2 -> v3.1.2 (go get + go mod tidy), fixed import paths in the 3 files. VirtualSigstore keyless tests) all green.

title: govulncheck-scan: fix OOM root cause + chmod verification blocker
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
Run the govulncheck-scan Tekton task on ocidex's cmd/... entrypoints. It OOMKilled repeatedly even after raising the memory limit 2Gi->4Gi->6Gi->10Gi (ocidex-2w2).

## Root Cause
govulncheck's whole-program SSA call graph is memory-hungry and grows with the dependency tree (grype/syft/AWS-SDK/k8s/cosign/sigstore-go). onError:continue does not protect against OOMKilled — a kernel-level cgroup kill bypasses step-level error handling entirely, hard-failing the TaskRun/PipelineRun despite the report-only design.

## Fix
GOMEMLIMIT=8GiB gives the Go GC a soft target below the 10Gi hard cgroup limit so it collects proactively. A watchdog polling the cgroup's own memory.current against memory.max self-terminates govulncheck before the kernel OOM-killer fires, converting a would-be OOMKilled into a normal non-zero exit — which onError:continue (step) + failOnError:false (reportOnlyStatusReporter) already handle correctly.
acceptance_criteria: govulncheck-scan no longer OOMKills; a real nonzero exit (vulnerabilities found) stays report-only and does not fail the PipelineRun. Verified live via isolated TaskRun: govulncheck-scan completed at ~8.5Gi peak (watchdog backstop not needed this run), found the 2 known reachable cosign/sigstore-go vulns, exited non-zero internally, and onError:continue/failOnError:false correctly kept the TaskRun Succeeded with a failure GitHub status report.
notes:
Files: .tektonic/jobs/go-vulncheck/spec.ts, .tekton/tasks/govulncheck-scan.k8s.yaml
Approach: Added GOMEMLIMIT=8GiB env var + a POSIX-sh watchdog (embedded via nushell raw string r#'...'#) that polls /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.{current,max} (v2, falling back to v1 paths) and self-SIGTERM/SIGKILLs govulncheck at 92% of the cgroup limit, before the kernel OOM-killer can fire. This converts a would-be OOMKilled (which bypasses onError:continue entirely, since it's an infra-level kill not a script exit) into a normal non-zero exit, which onError:continue (step) + failOnError:false (reportOnlyStatusReporter) already handle as report-only. No @pfenerty/tektonic library changes needed -- failOnError:false was already the correct existing mechanism for non-OOM failures.
Also discovered and worked around an unrelated verification blocker: ad-hoc isolated TaskRuns (kubectl create -f-, for live-testing without a real PipelineRun) reusing a workspace PVC from a prior real PipelineRun failed with `chmod: .go-mod: Operation not permitted` in restore-go-cache-cache, reproduced across two different PVCs. Root cause: real PipelineRuns set taskRunTemplate.podTemplate.securityContext.{runAsUser,fsGroup}=1024 (see .tekton/ocidex-ocidex-pull-request.k8s.yaml), which ad-hoc TaskRuns must also set to match the UID that originally wrote files into the reused PVC. Fixed by adding the same podTemplate.securityContext to the isolated TaskRun manifest -- not a code/pipeline bug, just a gap in the manual verification technique.
Verified live: isolated TaskRun completed Succeeded, govulncheck-scan peaked ~8.5Gi (never needed the watchdog backstop), found the 2 known reachable cosign/sigstore-go vulns (exit 1 internally), onError:continue masked it to container exitCode 0, and report-status correctly read the real exit code and posted a failure GitHub status while the TaskRun stayed Succeeded.

title: govulncheck-scan Tekton task gets OOMKilled at 6Gi limit despite node having 11GB+ free
description: govulncheck-scan step (internal/enrichment/provenance/... and cmd/... scan) is OOMKilled at its current 6Gi memory limit (.tektonic/jobs/go-vulncheck/spec.ts), even though the pod is scheduled on talos-jlf-6ro which has ~11GB free at scan time — so this is not a scheduling/node-headroom problem, the container's own cgroup limit is the binding constraint. A local reproduction on this machine (govulncheck v1.1.4 against ./cmd/...) shows ~3.2GB RSS / 88s wall time and surfaces 7 real reachable vulnerabilities from 2 modules, so genuine memory need has grown since the 6Gi limit was set (comment in spec.ts predicted node headroom would be the next bottleneck, not the container limit — that prediction didn't hold this time). Likely driver: recent ocidex-goh epic added several heavy dependency trees (cosign v2, sigstore-go, sigstore/rekor client, in-toto/attestation) that govulncheck's whole-program SSA analysis now has to walk.
acceptance_criteria: govulncheck-scan completes without StepOOM on a live TaskRun against current main; memory limit is raised to a value with real margin over observed local RSS.
notes:
Files: .tektonic/jobs/go-vulncheck/spec.ts, .tekton/tasks/govulncheck-scan.k8s.yaml
Approach: Diagnosed via kubectl (pod landed on talos-jlf-6ro, the largest node with 11GB+ free, and was OOMKilled at its own 6Gi container limit — not a scheduling/node-headroom issue as the old code comment predicted). Local repro of `govulncheck ./cmd/...` measured ~3.2GB peak RSS in 88s, well under 6Gi, and also surfaced 7 reachable vulnerabilities in 2 modules (separate finding, not yet triaged). Raised the memory limit to 10Gi (request to 2Gi) with real margin over the observed baseline, accounting for likely cgroup page-cache overcounting on the restored Go module/build cache plus the heavier dep tree the provenance epic (cosign/sigstore-go/rekor/in-toto) added. Verified live via an isolated TaskRun on a fresh workspace PVC (kubectl apply + kubectl create taskrun) before committing — all 4 steps completed with exitCode=0, no OOMKilled, no restarts.

title: RegistryService.Create/Update take 19/20 positional params; trust-preserve invariant split across layers
description:
internal/service/registry.go Create now takes 19 positional parameters and Update takes 20. Beyond readability, the epic introduced a concrete defect here: Update stopped reading 'existing' to preserve TrustIdentity/TrustIssuer, and internal/api/registry.go:UpdateRegistry now compensates by falling back to existing.TrustIdentity/existing.TrustIssuer when the request body field is nil.

The 'preserve unset trust fields' invariant is now split across the API and service layers, so any second caller of the service (operator reconciler, CLI, tests) silently wipes those fields.

Refactor to CreateRegistryParams / UpdateRegistryParams structs and move the preserve-on-nil logic back into the service where it can be enforced once.
acceptance_criteria: Create and Update take params structs. The preserve-unset-trust-fields behaviour lives in the service layer and is covered by a test that calls the service directly, without going through the HTTP handler.
notes:
Files: internal/service/registry.go, internal/service/registry_test.go, internal/api/registry.go, internal/api/middleware_test.go
Approach: Added CreateRegistryParams/UpdateRegistryParams structs; RegistryService.Create/Update now take these instead of 19-20 positional args. Update fetches existing registry via s.repo.GetRegistry and preserves VerificationMode/TrustPublicKey/TrustIdentity/TrustIssuer when params leave them unset, making the service (not the API handler) authoritative for the preserve-on-nil invariant. API's UpdateRegistry handler still computes a merged view for validateVerificationConfig (huma-error-coupled, must stay in API) but now passes raw in.Body.* trust fields to the service call. Added TestRegistryUpdate_PreservesTrustFieldsWhenUnset calling svc.Update directly to verify the invariant without going through HTTP.

title: no test coverage for drift recording or the reverifier
description:
atd.13 shipped provenance drift detection and the hourly reverifier with no direct test coverage. Nothing exercises:

- recordProvenanceDrift: the regression-only guard, sameSigner(), the three reason codes ('trust_config_changed', 'artifact_missing', 'reverification_failed'), or the silent-return-on-unmarshal-failure path.
- Reverifier.tick: batch sizing (recheckBatchSize = 500), cutoff computation, RequeueSucceededEnrichmentJob behaviour.
- The dispatcher.go:137 prior-provenance read and its 'err == nil' guard.

The absence of these tests is why ocidex-goh.2 (data destruction on transient error) shipped undetected. Add coverage as part of, or alongside, that fix.

Contrast with what atd.14/82g.3 did right: TestArtifactDetailSigningStatusParity (tests/integration_test.go:440) and the Go-vs-SQL ladder parity assertion at :581.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover recordProvenanceDrift's guard, sameSigner, and each reason code. An integration test covers a full drift cycle: verified -> regression -> event recorded -> visible via the API.
notes:
Files: internal/enrichment/provenance_drift_test.go (new), internal/enrichment/reverify_test.go, tests/integration_test.go
Approach: Added isolated unit tests for sameSigner (5 cases) and recordProvenanceDrift's regression-only guard + malformed-JSON silent-return paths (3 cases), reusing existing fakeStore/provenanceJSON helpers from dispatcher_test.go. Extended fakeRecheckStore to capture ListSBOMsDueForProvenanceRecheck args and added a test asserting RowLimit=recheckBatchSize and Cutoff=now-interval. Added TestProvenanceDriftFullCycle integration test: seeds a verified provenance enrichment via repository.Queries (which satisfies enrichment.Store directly), drives a real Dispatcher.ProcessOne with a fake provenance enricher returning a regressed (verified:false) result, and asserts both the SBOM's signingStatus flips to verification_failed and the drift event is visible via GET /api/v1/sboms/{id}/drift with correct previousStatus/newStatus/reason. title: OCIRegistry CRD accepts keyless config the API rejects
description:
internal/api/registry.go:validateVerificationConfig returns 400 when verificationMode is 'keyless' without both trustIdentity and trustIssuer. The CRD has no equivalent constraint: api/v1alpha1/ociregistry_types.go:64-82 marks VerificationMode with an Enum and default, but TrustPublicKey, TrustIdentity and TrustIssuer are all bare +optional with no cross-field rule.

An operator-managed OCIRegistry can therefore be admitted with mode=keyless and no identity/issuer — a configuration the HTTP API considers invalid. Same for mode=public_key with no trustPublicKey.

Add +kubebuilder:validation:XValidation CEL rules to the spec so both paths enforce the same invariant, then 'make generate-operator' and commit the regenerated CRDs.
acceptance_criteria: A CEL rule rejects keyless without identity+issuer and public_key without a key at admission time. config/operator/crd/*.yaml is regenerated. The API and CRD enforce identical invariants.
notes:
Files: internal/api/registry.go, internal/api/registry_test.go, api/v1alpha1/ociregistry_types.go, config/operator/crd/ocidex.io_ociregistries.yaml
Approach: validateVerificationConfig now also rejects public_key mode without trust_public_key (previously unenforced by the API at all — TestValidateVerificationConfig_OtherModesUnaffected asserted this as a no-op). Added matching struct-level +kubebuilder:validation:XValidation CEL rules on OCIRegistrySpec for both keyless and public_key, using size(x) > 0 instead of != '' to sidestep a tool-layer smart-quote corruption issue hit while editing. Regenerated CRD via make generate-operator. Unit tests pass, make lint clean (no new findings). Skipped live admission-time verification per user choice: only reachable cluster is the live Flux-managed homelab rpi-cluster, and its ociregistries.ocidex.io CRD is sourced from charts/ocidex-operator/crds/, which is discovered to be stale (missing verificationMode/trust* fields entirely, and untouched by make generate-operator) -- worth a separate follow-up issue.

title: reverifier: hardcoded ticker, no first tick, no enable flag, undocumented config
description:
internal/enrichment/reverify.go Run() has several rough edges:

- 'time.NewTicker(time.Hour)' is hardcoded, ignoring r.interval — which IS used for the recheck cutoff ('Cutoff: time.Now().Add(-r.interval)'). Interval and tick rate are silently decoupled.
- No immediate first tick: the sweep waits a full hour after startup before doing anything, so a short-lived pod never reverifies.
- No enable/disable flag. The reverifier runs unconditionally wherever it is wired up.
- PROVENANCE_RECHECK_INTERVAL appears in neither docs/CONFIGURATION.md nor .env.example.

Fix: derive the ticker from the configured interval, tick once immediately on start, add an explicit enable flag, and document the config.
acceptance_criteria: Ticker period derives from the configured interval. A sweep runs at startup. The reverifier can be disabled by configuration. PROVENANCE_RECHECK_INTERVAL and the enable flag are documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md and .env.example.
notes:
Files: internal/enrichment/reverify.go, cmd/ocidex/main.go, internal/config/config.go, docs/CONFIGURATION.md, .env.example, internal/enrichment/reverify_test.go
Approach: Run() now builds the ticker from r.interval instead of a hardcoded hour, and ticks once immediately before entering the select loop. Added PROVENANCE_REVERIFIER_ENABLED config flag (default true, preserving current unconditional behavior) gating the main.go LeaderElect wiring, mirroring the ScannerEnabled/RegistryPollerEnabled pattern. Documented both PROVENANCE_RECHECK_INTERVAL and the new flag in docs/CONFIGURATION.md and .env.example. Added TestReverifier_Run_TicksImmediatelyOnStart and TestReverifier_Run_TicksAtConfiguredInterval covering Run() (previously only tick() was tested).

title: TUF trusted-root fetch serialises workers under mutex and staleness is unbounded
description:
getTrustedRoot() in internal/enrichment/provenance/keyless.go holds the cache mutex for the entire duration of root.FetchTrustedRoot(), an unbounded network round trip with no context. Every concurrent enrichment worker therefore serialises behind one TUF fetch.

Second issue in the same function: the stale-serve fallback has no bound. If TUF keeps failing, the cached root is served indefinitely, which means revoked Fulcio CAs remain trusted forever — a fail-open with no ceiling.

Fix: fetch outside the lock (single-flight, e.g. golang.org/x/sync/singleflight, already a likely indirect dep), pass a context with timeout, and refuse to serve a root older than some hard maximum (a multiple of trustedRootCacheTTL) rather than serving it forever.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent verifications do not serialise behind the TUF fetch. The fetch honours a context deadline. A trusted root older than the configured hard maximum causes verification to fail rather than proceed on stale trust material.
notes:
Files: internal/enrichment/provenance/keyless.go, internal/enrichment/provenance/keyless_test.go
Approach: getTrustedRoot no longer holds trustedRootMu across the TUF fetch. Concurrent
callers on a stale/empty cache now collapse into one in-flight fetch via
golang.org/x/sync/singleflight (already a direct dep; errgroup from the same module is
used in internal/service/search_stats.go). The fetch is bounded by a 30s context timeout
via tuf.Options.WithContext (root.FetchTrustedRoot itself takes no context). The stale-serve
fallback on fetch error now has a hard ceiling, trustedRootMaxStaleness = 7 * trustedRootCacheTTL
(7 days) -- beyond that, verification fails closed instead of trusting indefinitely-stale
material. Added fetchTrustedRootFn test seam (mirrors existing trustedMaterialProvider
pattern) and 5 new tests covering cache-hit-skips-fetch, singleflight collapse, context
deadline propagation, stale-served-within-ceiling, and fail-closed-beyond-ceiling. Verified
with go test -race on the provenance package and golangci-lint (only pre-existing,
unrelated findings remain, e.g. the unparam finding tracked separately as ocidex-goh.17).
Full-repo make check/make test could not be run in this session due to the host disk
being nearly full (unrelated to this change) -- flagged to the user.

title: provenance drift banner never clears after recovery
description:
lookupProvenanceDrift (internal/service/search_sbom.go:137) returns GetLatestProvenanceDrift unconditionally, and ProvenanceCard.tsx renders it under <Show when={drift}>. Because drift recording is regression-only (recordProvenanceDrift returns early unless the old status was 'verified' or 'signed'), recovery is never recorded.

Result: once an artifact is removed and later restored, the SBOM detail page shows a green 'Verified' badge directly above the text 'changed from verified to artifact_missing on <date>' — permanently, and self-contradictorily.

Two viable fixes: (a) only surface the drift summary when drift.NewStatus still equals the current detail.SigningStatus; or (b) record recovery transitions as drift events too and let the banner describe the latest transition either way. (b) is more informative and makes the drift feed a complete history rather than a regression log.
acceptance_criteria: A recovered SBOM does not display a stale drift banner contradicting its current signing status. Behaviour is covered by a test.
notes:
Files: internal/service/search_sbom.go, internal/service/search_test.go
Approach: gate SBOMDetail.ProvenanceDrift on drift.NewStatus == current signing status via new currentDrift() helper. Recovery is not itself recorded as a drift event, so once status changes away from a regression's NewStatus, the stale event is suppressed instead of shown forever.

title: refactor: single source of truth for signing status derivation
description:
The mapping from a provenance enrichment's JSON to a terminal signing status (unsigned | signed | verified | verification_failed | artifact_missing) is implemented five times across three languages:

  1-3. db/queries/artifact.sql — the CASE expression, duplicated 3x (ListArtifacts, GetArtifact, ListArtifactVersions)
  4.   internal/enrichment/provenance_drift.go:signingStatus()
  5.   web/src/utils/trust.ts:trustStatus()

Adding artifact_missing in ocidex-atd.13 required editing all five. A sixth status will too. The frontend copy is the weakest: it re-derives status from the raw provenance JSON blob rather than reading a server-computed value, so it can silently disagree with what the API sorts and filters on.
design:
Two moves:

DB side — collapse the three CASE copies into one Postgres function:
  CREATE FUNCTION signing_status(provenance_data jsonb) RETURNS text IMMUTABLE
and call it from all three queries in db/queries/artifact.sql. New migration; sqlc regenerates unchanged types since the return is still text.

API side — surface signingStatus as a first-class field on the SBOM/provenance response (it already exists on ArtifactVersionSummary). web/src/utils/trust.ts then maps status -> label/variant only, and stops inspecting p.verified / p.signaturePresent / p.artifactMissing.

internal/enrichment/provenance_drift.go:signingStatus() stays in Go — it must classify from two in-memory JSON blobs (old vs new) before either is queryable. But it should be the ONLY Go copy, and its doc comment should point at the SQL function as the normative definition. Consider a shared test fixture (table of provenance JSON -> expected status) asserted against both the Go function and the SQL function so they cannot drift apart silently.
acceptance_criteria: db/queries/artifact.sql contains one signing-status derivation, not three. web/src/utils/trust.ts consumes a server-provided status string and no longer re-derives from raw provenance fields. A parity test asserts the Go signingStatus() and the SQL function agree on a shared fixture table covering all five statuses. Adding a sixth status requires editing at most two places (SQL function + Go classifier).
notes:
Files: db/migrations/00049_signing_status_function.sql, db/queries/artifact.sql, internal/enrichment/provenance/status.go, internal/enrichment/provenance_drift.go, internal/service/search.go, internal/service/search_sbom.go, web/src/utils/trust.ts, web/src/components/ProvenanceCard.tsx, web/src/components/SummaryBand.tsx, web/src/pages/SBOMDetail/index.tsx, tests/integration_test.go
Approach: Consolidated 6 duplicate signing-status derivations into 3: signing_status(jsonb) Postgres function (used by GetArtifact/ListArtifacts/ListArtifactVersions), provenance.SigningStatus Go classifier (leaf package, avoids import cycle; replaces provenance_drift.go's local copy; also called from search_sbom.go to populate SBOMDetail.SigningStatus), and trust.ts's status->label/variant map (frontend now consumes server value via signingStatus prop instead of re-deriving from raw Provenance fields). Added TestSigningStatusParity_AllStatuses covering all 5 statuses (unsigned/signed/verified/verification_failed/artifact_missing), asserting Go classifier + SBOM detail endpoint + artifact detail endpoint all agree. Verified: make openapi, make frontend-lint (0 errors), go vet + targeted go test on service/enrichment/api packages (pass), golangci-lint scoped to changed packages (0 new issues vs pre-existing 53-issue baseline). Integration test compiles and skips cleanly without Docker in this environment (make test-integration not run — Docker unavailable).

title: refactor: unify public_key verification onto cosign.CheckOpts
description:
internal/enrichment/provenance/verify.go is ~120 lines of hand-rolled ECDSA + DSSE PAE crypto for the public_key verification path, while the keyless path (keyless.go, shipped in ocidex-atd.15) delegates to cosign/v2's own verify pipeline.

Two verification pipelines exist: one hardened by the reference implementation, one hand-written. The hand-written path re-implements digest binding itself (sigBoundDigest, subjectsBindTo) instead of reusing cosign's SimpleClaimVerifier / IntotoSubjectClaimVerifier, and silently accepts only ECDSA keys (parsePEMPublicKey type-asserts to *ecdsa.PublicKey).

cosign/v2 is already a direct dependency, so this costs zero new modules.
design:
Replace applyVerification's bespoke crypto with the same cosign.CheckOpts path applyKeylessVerification already uses, swapping TrustedMaterial/Identities for SigVerifier:

  verifier, err := signature.LoadVerifier(pubkey, crypto.SHA256)  // sigstore/sigstore/pkg/signature
  co := cosign.CheckOpts{SigVerifier: verifier, IgnoreTlog: true, IgnoreSCT: true}

Then reuse the existing buildOCISignature / buildStaticOptions helpers from keyless.go and call cosign.VerifyImageSignature / VerifyImageAttestation with ClaimVerifier set — identical structure to verifyKeylessSignature/verifyKeylessAttestation.

Note IgnoreTlog: true is correct here — a public-key signature has no Rekor bundle to check offline; that is the semantic difference from the keyless path, not an accident.

Deletes: parsePEMPublicKey, verifySig, verifyDSSE, sigBoundDigest, subjectsBindTo, dsseEnvelope (~100 lines).
Gains: RSA/ed25519 key support, shared claim verification, one crypto path to reason about.

Extract the shared setup (buildOCISignature, buildStaticOptions, the verify-sig-and-att AND-ing) so both modes call one helper differing only in CheckOpts construction.
acceptance_criteria: verify.go's hand-rolled ECDSA/DSSE crypto is deleted. Both public_key and keyless verification flow through cosign.VerifyImageSignature/VerifyImageAttestation with a ClaimVerifier set. Existing provenance_test.go public-key tests pass unchanged (they are the regression net). A test proves a public-key signature transplanted from a different image digest fails, mirroring TestApplyKeylessVerification_TransplantedSignatureFails. go.mod gains no new modules.

Files: internal/enrichment/provenance/{verify,keyless,parse,provenance,provenance_test}.go, go.mod

Deleted subjectsBindTo/parsePEMPublicKey/verifySig/verifyDSSE from verify.go, and the now-orphaned simpleSigning/sigBoundDigest from parse.go (caught by golangci-lint unused, not by initial plan). go.mod: sigstore/sigstore promoted indirect->direct via go mod tidy, no version bump. title: Tekton Chains PipelineRun-level signing fails (signed=failed after 3 retries)
description: On push run ocidex-ocidex-push-l6bh5, the build TaskRun signed successfully (chains.tekton.dev/signed=true, image sig+attestation attached, Rekor logIndex 2247152855) but the PipelineRun-level annotation is chains.tekton.dev/signed=failed after chains.tekton.dev/retries=3. Per-image signing (TaskRun-level, drives signing_status) works; the aggregate PipelineRun SLSA provenance is not being stored. Investigate tekton-chains-controller logs for the PipelineRun deep-inspection signing/storage error (likely OCI push or subject-resolution for the pipeline-level attestation). Found while validating ocidex-07x.
notes:
RESOLVED in homelab, not ocidex. Fix: homelab-374 (commit fda1edc, pushed + Flux-reconciled).

Root cause: chains-config had artifacts.pipelinerun.storage: 'tekton, oci' (homelab talos-cluster/flux/apps/tekton-chains/kustomization.yaml:22). The 'tekton' backend writes the signed DSSE payload back as a k8s annotation; with enable-deep-inspection and ocidex's 10 image subjects the aggregate slsa/v2alpha4 payload exceeds the 262144-byte annotation limit:
  PipelineRun.tekton.dev "ocidex-ocidex-push-lzrqc" is invalid: metadata.annotations: Too long
  (chains/signing.go:265, tekton/tekton.go:76)
apko-cicd runs were signed=true because their payload stays under the limit.

The original report overstated the impact: the aggregate provenance was NEVER lost. For lzrqc the payload was signed, uploaded to Rekor, and the OCI backend pushed the attestation to all 10 images. Only the redundant annotation copy 422'd. The real cost was the retry storm - the reconciler re-ran the whole sign+store cycle each requeue, producing 9 Rekor entries and 90 OCI uploads per push run, plus a signed=failed status that misrepresented reality.

Fix: artifacts.pipelinerun.storage: 'oci'. TaskRun storage unchanged. No ocidex code touched - internal/enrichment/provenance/parse.go:91 reads chains.tekton.dev/transparency from the OCI manifest annotations, not the k8s object, so nothing here depended on the tekton backend.

Verified on a live re-sign of lzrqc: signed=true, 1 Rekor upload, 10 OCI uploads, 0 errors, cosign verify-attestation passes.
close_reason: Fixed in homelab-374 (Tekton Chains config); no ocidex code change required

title: Fix creds-init permission-denied on /.docker (pod-level runAsUser 1024 + no HOME)
description: Tekton's auto-injected creds-init container fails with 'mkdir /.docker: permission denied' across many CI jobs. Root cause: .tektonic/pipeline.ts's defaultPodSecurityContext (runAsUser: 1024) applies pod-wide via taskRunTemplate.podTemplate.securityContext, forcing creds-init (which materializes the ghcr-docker-config secret attached to the default ServiceAccount) to run as uid 1024. That uid has no /etc/passwd entry, so $HOME defaults to / (unwritable) -- same root cause class as the already-fixed GOPATH bug, but creds-init isn't a Task step so stepTemplate.env doesn't reach it.
design: Add { name: "HOME", value: "/tekton/home" } to podTemplateEnv in .tektonic/pipeline.ts. podTemplateEnv flows into taskRunTemplate.podTemplate.env, which per Tekton's own API schema applies to all containers in the pod (not just step containers), so it reaches creds-init. /tekton/home is already proven writable regardless of uid in this cluster (go-security.k8s.yaml steps already write there). No tektonic library change needed -- PACProject/TektonProject already plumb podTemplateEnv straight through to the real Tekton API field.
acceptance_criteria: Regenerated .tekton/*.k8s.yaml via make tekton-synth shows HOME=/tekton/home in the PipelineRun podTemplate.env. Verified live via an isolated TaskRun/PipelineRun that creds-init no longer logs the permission-denied warning.
notes:
Files: .tektonic/pipeline.ts, .tekton/ocidex-ocidex-{pull-request,push,tag}.k8s.yaml
Approach: defaultPodSecurityContext (runAsUser: 1024) applies pod-wide via taskRunTemplate.podTemplate.securityContext, including to Tekton's auto-injected creds-init step run by the entrypoint wrapper on every step. uid 1024 has no /etc/passwd entry so HOME defaults to '/', which is unwritable, causing 'mkdir /.docker: permission denied'. Added HOME=/tekton/home to podTemplateEnv (also pod-wide per Tekton's PodTemplate API), same writable-scratch pattern already used for stepTemplate.env (goEnv/nodeEnv). No tektonic library change needed - confirmed via pac-project.ts and the v1 swagger schema that podTemplateEnv/defaultPodSecurityContext correctly map to real pod-wide Tekton API fields. Verified live via ad-hoc TaskRuns in ocidex-ci before committing: with the fix, step logs show no cred-copy warning; a recent real pipeline pod (ocidex-ocidex-push-bbtnh-go-fmt, pre-fix) shows the warning in every step's log.

title: OCIRegistry reconciler retries CreateRegistry forever if status write fails after success
description: Discovered while diagnosing an empty artifacts page on the ocidex-dev homelab deployment. internal/controller/ociregistry_controller.go Reconcile() only calls OCIDexClient.CreateRegistry when cr.Status.RegistryID == "". If CreateRegistry succeeds but the subsequent r.Status().Update(ctx, cr) fails (conflict, API server blip, etc.), the new registryID is never persisted to the CRD. Every later reconcile sees RegistryID=="" again and calls CreateRegistry again, which now collides with the row already created in Postgres on registry_name_key (SQLSTATE 23505) and fails forever — the CRD never reaches Ready and no scans are ever queued. All 6 OCIRegistry CRDs in ocidex-dev were stuck like this for ~31 days. Related to ocidex-01v (K8s operator + CRDs, now closed).
acceptance_criteria: Reconcile is idempotent even if the status write after a successful CreateRegistry fails: either persist RegistryID immediately/atomically with creation, or on a create conflict look up the existing registry by name and adopt its ID instead of erroring forever.
notes:
Files: db/queries/registry.sql, internal/repository/{repository.go,registry.sql.go}, internal/service/registry.go, internal/api/{registry.go,types.go,router.go}, pkg/client/{client.go,registry.go,fake_client.go,types.go}, internal/controller/ociregistry_controller.go, plus tests in registry_test.go / ociregistry_controller_test.go / middleware_test.go.
Approach: Added GetRegistryByName (DB query -> repo -> service -> new GET /api/v1/registries/by-name/{name} endpoint -> Go SDK method). Service Create() now returns ErrConflict on a unique-violation (via existing isUniqueViolation helper) instead of a generic 500. Controller Reconcile() catches ocidexclient.ErrConflict on CreateRegistry, looks up the existing registry by spec.Name, and adopts its ID (condition reason 'Adopted') instead of retrying CreateRegistry forever. If the by-name lookup also fails, the original conflict error still surfaces. Covered by TestRegistryCreate_UniqueViolationReturnsConflict, TestRegistryGetByName_*, TestOCIRegistryReconciler_CreateConflictAdoptsExisting, TestOCIRegistryReconciler_CreateConflictLookupAlsoFails. Full unit suite (make test) and package build pass; make lint has pre-existing unrelated failures in other files (license.go, auth.go, etc.) not touched by this change.

title: Fix postgres 18 docker-compose volume mount layout
description: docker-compose.yml mounted the named volume at /var/lib/postgresql/data (old-style child path). Postgres 18+ images fatally reject any mount at that path — they require a single mount at the parent /var/lib/postgresql so the major-version subdirectory scheme can live there. This broke local docker compose startup after the postgres image was bumped to 18.4 via Renovate.
acceptance_criteria: docker-compose.yml mounts db-data at /var/lib/postgresql (parent); docker compose up brings postgres to healthy and migrate completes without the previous fatal 18+ layout error
notes:
Files: docker-compose.yml
Approach: Changed postgres service volume mount from db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data to db-data:/var/lib/postgresql. Also cleaned up an orphaned anonymous volume (the postgres image's own implicit VOLUME declaration at /var/lib/postgresql) that was silently shadowing real leftover PG18 data at the old path and caused the error to persist even after the named db-data volume was manually deleted. Verified: docker compose up -d brings postgres to healthy, migrate runs cleanly to version 46, and /health + /ready return ok.
close_reason: Fixed volume mount path for postgres 18 layout; verified stack starts healthy

title: Refine global table + interaction CSS in index.css
description: Implement the refined field-guide spec from ADR-0023 in web/src/index.css: sort-affordance styling, row hover/motion (150ms), sticky headers, consistent density, unified empty/loading treatment. Extend existing tokens only. Run make frontend-lint-fix then make frontend-lint.
notes:
Files: web/src/index.css, web/src/components/DataTable.css

Approach:
- thead th: position:sticky; top:0; z-index:2; background:var(--color-surface) (matches card/group-header token).
- tbody tr: added transition: background-color 150ms ease (sitewide hover convention).
- tr.group-header-row td: added z-index:1 so thead (z-index:2) always wins stacking (Artifacts.tsx grouped table).
- DataTable.css: th.th-sortable:has(.sort-arrow) keeps text at full --color-text while active-sorted; .sort-arrow colored --color-accent-amber. No TSX change needed — DataTable.tsx only renders .sort-arrow for the active sortKey column.

Deviation from ADR-0023 literal text (important): the ADR assumed thead sticky would work against page/viewport scroll with 'no new scroll container' since .table-wrapper only had overflow-x:auto. Empirically verified via Playwright that this is wrong: per the CSS overflow spec, overflow-x:auto with overflow-y left as visible forces the browser to compute overflow-y as auto too, making .table-wrapper the sticky containing block — but since it had no bounded height, scrollHeight==clientHeight, so there was never any internal scroll for sticky to react to (thead top tracked window.scrollY 1:1, i.e. completely non-functional).

Fix (approved by user via AskUserQuestion, chose 'Bound table-wrapper height' over dropping sticky): added max-height:70vh; overflow-y:auto to .table-wrapper, making it a genuine internal scroll region. This changes UX for every .table-wrapper table sitewide (Artifacts, Components, Vulnerabilities, Licenses, PackagesTab, admin tables): tables now scroll internally within a 70vh box rather than the whole page. Re-verified sticky + group-header z-index stacking correctly after the change (Playwright: thead top stays fixed under internal scroll, group-header-row stays under thead).

Verified: PackagesTab.tsx does not use group-header-row (only Artifacts.tsx does) — ADR's reference to PackagesTab for that interaction was imprecise; no stacking regression there, just standard sticky-header-in-bounded-wrapper behavior.

Verification: make frontend-lint-fix + make frontend-lint clean (0 errors, 2 pre-existing unrelated warnings). Real-browser Playwright verification of sticky pin, active-sort coloring, hover transition, and group-header/thead stacking on light theme.

Follow-up worth considering: ADR-0023's 'no new scroll container' claim in the Table & interaction refinement section is now inaccurate and should be amended to describe the bounded-height wrapper.
close_reason: Sticky headers, row hover transition, group-header z-index, and active-sort styling implemented in index.css/DataTable.css; bounded .table-wrapper height added to make sticky actually function (ADR assumption was empirically wrong). Lint clean, browser-verified.
